children.translated_text: That which is of the nature of dense bliss and consciousness, incomparable, free from the limitations of time and space,
ever-liberated, eternally free, illuminated by hundreds of thousands of <s>Vedas</s> (scriptures),
imperceptible to mere sight, yet constituting the highest goal of human endeavor — that <s>Brahman</s> (Absolute Reality), that Truth,

children.text: tattāvad bhāti sākṣād gurupavanapure hanta bhāgyaṃ janānām //
children.translated_text: that very [<s>Brahman</s>] shines directly in the holy city of <s>Guruvāyūr</s> (the city of the Guru-Wind) — ah, what fortune for mankind! //
When such a rare treasure is thus easily obtained, within reach, yet people with body, speech, or mind

children.text: tanvā vācā dhiyā vā bhajati bata janaḥ kṣudrataiva sphuṭeyam /
children.translated_text: worship something else — alas! this is plainly their pettiness.

children.text: ete tāvad vayaṃ tu sthirataramanasā viśvapīḍāpahatyai
children.translated_text: But we, with steadfast minds, for the removal of the suffering of the world,
take refuge in this very Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, who is the complete Self of all. //

children.text: sattvaṃ yattat purābhyāmaparikalanato mirmalaṃ tena tāvad
children.translated_text: That <s>sattva</s> (pure quality), which is unstained by the other two [<s>guṇas</s>] due to non-association — with that, indeed,
You assume a form composed of elements and sense-organs — thus the statement of <s>Vyāsa</s> is heard many times.
That [form], on account of its transparency, is of the nature of a radiant mass of supreme bliss and consciousness, covering what is beyond,

children.text: tasmin dhanyā ramante śrutimatimadhure sugrahe vigrahe te //
children.translated_text: in that [form] — sweet to hearing and intellect, easily grasped — the blessed ones delight, O Lord, in Your embodiment! //
In the immovable, eternally full, limitless ocean of supreme bliss-nectar, the pure ocean of <s>Brahman</s>,
most beautified by the immersion of countless strings of liberated souls,
that which they call the purest <s>sattva</s>, like the play of waves — that is Your very Self;

children.text: kasmānno niṣkalastvaṃ sakala iti vacastvatkalāsveva bhūman! //
children.translated_text: why then are You [called] 'without parts'? You are whole! — such words apply to Your parts alone, O All-pervading One! //
Though without activity, O Unborn One! You engage without cause in the action called 'seeing' (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>),
by that very [glance], <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), though latent and almost unreal, rises forth at the beginning of a cosmic cycle.
Of that [<s>Prakṛti</s>], a certain supremely pure aspect, the form of <s>sattva</s>, which conceals [impurity] —

children.text: sa tvaṃ dhṛtvā dadhāsi svamahimavibhavākuṇṭha! vaikuṇṭḥa! rūpam //
children.translated_text: that You assume and bear Your form, O <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>! whose glory is unobstructed by Your own majesty! //
That form of Yours — playful with rows of beautiful arts as tender as a stream of fresh rain,
the quintessence of charm, the perfect incarnation of merit for the eyes of the virtuous,
the carefree abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s sport, inwardly sprinkling a flood of nectar
upon those who contemplate it — I meditate upon, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! //
'Painful is Your creative activity, bringing manifold suffering of existence to living beings' — thus
I had formerly reflected, O Unconquered One! But now I understand otherwise.

children.text: no cejjīvāḥ kathaṃ vā sadhurataramidaṃ tvadvapuścidrasārdraṃ
children.translated_text: For if there were no living beings, how would they drink through eyes and ears this most exquisite form of Yours, moist with the essence of consciousness,
and revel in the flood of the ocean of supreme nectar-bliss? //
To the humble, You constantly bestow, even unasked, treasures that are always near at hand;
You incessantly grant desires and the path dense with supreme bliss.

children.text: itthaṃ niśśeṣalabhyo niravadhikaphalaḥ pārijāto hare! tvaṃ
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Hari</s>! You are the wish-fulfilling tree (<s>Pārijāta</s>) obtainable by all, with unlimited fruits —
this throng of supplicants desires in vain that petty tree of <s>Śakra</s>'s (Indra's) garden. //

children.text: kāruṇyāt kāmamanyaṃ dadati khalu pare svātmadastvaṃ viśeṣā-
children.translated_text: Others, out of compassion, may give what is desired, but You especially give Your very Self;
others rule over people in the world by their sovereignty, but You are the Lord even of Yourself.
Highly fortunate beings rejoice in You, who are sweet at every step; yet You
are Self-delighting (<s>ātmārāma</s>) — O <s>Śauri</s>! foundation of incomparable virtues, salutations to You! //
Sovereignty that commands even <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva) and other lords; splendor that eclipses the luster of all the luminaries of the universe;
a valor that is pure; fame sung even by the desireless;

children.text: aṅgāsaṅgā sadā śrīrakhilavidasi na kvāpi te saṅgavārtā
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) inseparably attached to Your limbs; You are the knower of all, yet nowhere is there talk of Your attachment —
therefore, O Dweller in <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! O Slayer of <s>Mura</s>! You are the foremost referent of the word '<s>Bhagavān</s>' (the Blessed Lord)! //
A diadem rivaling the sun, a forehead shining with the upward <s>tilaka</s> mark,
eyes brimming with compassion, a face radiant with a tender smile, with beautiful nostrils,
a pair of gleaming earrings shaped like <s>makaras</s> (sea-creatures) on the cheeks, a <s>Kaustubha</s> gem blazing at the throat —
I worship that form of Yours, resplendent with the forest garland, diamond clusters, and the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark! //
Marked with armlets, bracelets, bangles, and magnificent jeweled rings, adorned with four beautiful arms bearing the mace, conch, discus, and lotus;
wearing a brilliant yellow garment, girdled with a shining golden belt — I take refuge in that form of Yours, with feet radiant as pure lotuses, which destroys affliction! //
That which is enchanting — surpassing even the enchantment that is venerated by the three worlds — and which is
beautiful beyond the very treasury of beauty, sweet beyond the very essence of sweetness,
more lovely than the very summit of loveliness, and wondrous beyond wonder itself —

children.text: bhuvane na kasya kutukaṃ puṣṇāti viṣṇo! vibho! //
children.translated_text: whose curiosity in the world does Your form not nourish, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>! O All-pervading Lord! //
Having obtained that sweet form of Yours, the Goddess (<s>Devī</s>) of abundant wealth,

children.text: sā devī paramotsukā cirataraṃ nāste svabhakteṣvapi /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> herself, supremely eager, does not long remain even among her own devotees.
Therefore, alas, O <s>Acyuta</s>! O Lord! on account of the uncontrollable force of her steadfast love for the delight of Your beautiful form, the report of her fickleness has arisen! //
<s>Lakṣmī</s> would not remain with others, captivated as she is by Your incomparable charm,
for which there is yet another proof — now I shall declare it, O Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>!
Those devotees who are attached to the pleasure of recounting Your qualities in song —
in them she dwells steadfastly, honoring the mention of her beloved. //
Your form — streaming with the fresh nectar-earth of such captivating beauty,
made of the supreme elixir of consciousness, heart-stealing to those who hear of it —
instantly inspires the mind, intoxicates [it], causes horripilation of the body,
and drenches [the devotee] with cool tears born of the rising wave of bliss! //

children.text: evambhūtatayā hi bhaktyabhihito yogaḥ sa yogadvayat
children.translated_text: Devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) thus characterized is indeed called a <s>yoga</s> — and by the lords of <s>yoga</s>,
it is celebrated as far superior to the other two <s>yogas</s>: that of action (<s>karma</s>) and that of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>).
For in You, whose very essence is the singular flavor of beauty, devotion (<s>bhakti</s>), whose nature is the excellence of love,
is attained effortlessly by all people, O Beloved of <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī)! //
<s>Karma-yoga</s> (the yoga of action), which is the desireless performance of one's own prescribed duties,
yields its fruit only after a long time; and the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> knowledge that is to be attained through <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) —

children.text: tat tvavyaktatayā sudurgamataraṃ cittasya tasmād vibho!
children.translated_text: that, by its abstract nature, is exceedingly difficult for the mind. Therefore, O Lord!
devotion (<s>bhakti</s>), whose essence is love for You, is always the most natural and the most beneficial. //
Having performed heaps of most arduous rites, those who are spotlessly pure
arrive at the path of knowledge or the path of devotion — but what [is gained] by just that much?

children.text: kliṣṭvā tarkapathe paraṃ tava vapurbrahmākhyamanye punaś
children.translated_text: Others, having struggled on the path of logic, then, having contemplated Your supreme form called <s>Brahman</s>,
without the softening of the heart, succeed only after many births. //
But Your devotion, of its own accord, through immersion in the nectar-stream of [Your] narrative-delight,
accomplishes the path of pure purification without distress.

children.text: sadyaḥ siddhikarī jayatyayi vibho! saivāstu me tvatpada-
children.translated_text: Granting immediate success — may it prevail, O Lord! May that very thing be mine: the intensity of love
overflowing with the rich flavor of devotion to Your feet — swiftly, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! //
Reciting Your names, plunged into the ocean of ecstatic joy,

children.text: smaranto rūpaṃ te varada! kaṭhayanto guṇakaṭhāḥ /
children.translated_text: remembering Your form, O Boon-granter! recounting the stories of Your virtues,

children.text: caranto ye bhaktāstvapi khalu ramante paramamu-
children.translated_text: those devotees who thus move about — they indeed revel in the supreme [bliss];
I deem them blessed, having attained all their desires. //
Afflicted by disease, alas — even though my heart is filled with the delight of devotion to Your feet,

children.text: 'pyanāsaktaṃ cittaṃ bhavati bata viṣṇo! kuru dayām /
children.translated_text: my mind does not remain steady. O <s>Viṣṇu</s>! show mercy!
Delighting in the remembrance of Your lotus feet, singing the collections of Your names,
again and again singing, I shall dwell somewhere in solitude. //

children.text: kṛpā te jātā cet kimiva na hi labhyaṃ tanubhṛtāṃ
children.translated_text: If Your grace should arise, what indeed is not obtainable for embodied beings?
The condition of quelling my mass of afflictions — how great is that [for You]?
How many in this world, perpetually free from sorrow,
devoted to You, liberated, do not enjoy the path of happiness without attachment? //
Great sages, renowned in the world, their inner path deeply hidden,
headed by <s>Nārada</s> and others, free from disease through the remembrance of Your lotus feet,
wander freely, constantly effulgent with the supreme consciousness beyond,
immersed in the flood of eternal bliss and non-duality — what more [could they want]? //

children.text: bhavadbhaktiḥ sphītā bhavatu mama saiva praśamaye-
children.translated_text: May my devotion to You flourish — that alone shall pacify
the entire flood of afflictions; there is not even a particle of doubt in my heart.

children.text: na ced vyāsasyoktistava ca vacanaṃ naigamavaco
children.translated_text: For if the statement of <s>Vyāsa</s>, and Your own word, and the <s>Vedic</s> utterance
were false, then everything would be as worthless as the speech of common street-folk. //
Your devotion is, to begin with, supremely sweet from the relish of Your qualities;
even when it has ascended [to maturity], it pacifies all suffering.
And finally, in the inner self, the arising of pure awakening,
the great non-dual bliss — it bestows! What else beyond this could be desired? //

children.text: vidhūya kleśān me kuru caraṇayugmaṃ dhṛtarasaṃ
children.translated_text: Dispelling my afflictions, make my pair of feet inclined toward
the attainment of Your sacred place, and my hands for the rite of Your worship;
my eyes for beholding Your sacred form, and my nose for smelling
the <s>tulasī</s> at Your feet, and my ears for [hearing] Your beautiful deeds! //
In my heart, violently assailed by abundant physical and mental ailments,
may that form of Yours — of the nature of supreme bliss and consciousness — arise!
With horripilation rising, with abundant tears of joy streaming down,
may I thereby forget even the tribulation of intractable suffering! //
O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Even those who turn away from You are happy;

children.text: bhavatsnehī so'haṃ subahu paritapye ca kimidam /
children.translated_text: yet I, who love You, suffer greatly — what is the meaning of this?

children.text: akīrtiste mā bhūd varada! gadabhāraṃ praśamayan
children.translated_text: Let there be no dishonor to You, O Boon-granter! Quelling the burden of disease,
make me swiftly the crest-jewel of Your devotees, O Slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>! //
What need of more words? Until Your compassion should arise,
I, O Lord! shall keep uttering the various entreaties of the afflicted.

children.text: puraḥ klṛpte pāde varada! tava neṣyāmi divasān
children.translated_text: Before Your feet, O Boon-granter! I shall pass my days,
performing, as best I can, obeisance, praise, and devoted service. //

children.text: kalyatāṃ mama kuruṣva tāvatīṃ kalyate bhavadupāsanaṃ yayā /
children.translated_text: Grant me that much well-being by which the worship of You becomes possible;
through the well-nourished practice of the eightfold <s>yoga</s>, may I swiftly attain Your satisfaction! //
Purified by <s>yamas</s> (restraints) such as firm <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) and the like, and by <s>niyamas</s> (observances) such as ablution and the like,

children.text: kurmahe dṛḍhamamī sukhāsanaṃ paṅkajādyamapi vā bhavatparāḥ //
children.translated_text: we shall firmly practice the comfortable seat (<s>sukhāsana</s>), or the lotus posture (<s>padmāsana</s>) and others, devoted to You. //
Continuously meditating on <s>Oṃ</s> (<s>tāra</s>-mantra) within, restraining the <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), purified,
then withdrawing the senses from their objects — we shall remain poised for Your worship. //

children.text: asphuṭe vapuṣi prayatnato dhārayema dhiṣaṇāṃ muhurmuhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Upon the yet-indistinct form, we shall hold our minds with effort, again and again;
thereby, contemplating Your feet, we shall carry the essence of devotion to its fullness. //
Your form, beautiful in the clarity of its distinct limbs — through long practice,
we shall meditate upon it effortlessly in the mind, absorbed in the <s>yoga</s> of meditation (<s>dhyāna-yoga</s>), taking refuge in You. //
For those who meditate on such a complete form, whose minds are seized by the emerging sweetness —
the inner <s>Brahman</s>, in the form of a dense mass of bliss, manifests, O embodiment of form! //
That state of savoring [bliss], which is Your <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), O Ruler of the universe! —
having attained it, then upon falling from it, we shall resume <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) and the rest. //
Thus, through practice, with the festival of bliss fashioned from the ever-emerging joy of the supreme Self,
having attained the crown of the community of liberated devotees, we shall roam like <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Nārada</s>. //

children.text: tvatsamādhivijaye tu yaḥ punarmaṅkṣu mokṣarasikaḥ krameṇa vā /Ṇ
children.translated_text: But he who, upon conquering Your <s>samādhi</s>, whether desiring liberation swiftly or gradually,
raises the breath (<s>vāyu</s>), controlled through <s>yoga</s>, slowly through the <s>suṣumṇā</s>, passing through the six centers (<s>cakras</s>), O Unborn One! //

children.text: liṅgadehamapi santyajannatho līyate tvayi pare nirāgrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Abandoning even the subtle body (<s>liṅga-deha</s>), he dissolves into You, the Supreme, without grasping;
but one curious about the higher worlds exits through the crown of the head, together with the faculties. //
Conveyed by the deities presiding over fire, daytime, the bright fortnight, the auspicious constellation, and the northern solstice —
devoted to You, joyful, he reaches the sphere of the sun and proceeds to the realm of <s>Dhruva</s> (the Pole Star). //
Then, when dwelling in the great hall [of <s>Brahmā</s>], he is scorched by the heat of the fire from <s>Śeṣa</s>'s mouths,

children.text: īyate bhavadupāśrayastadā vedhasaḥ padamataḥ puraiva vā //
children.translated_text: he who has taken refuge in You proceeds then to the realm of <s>Brahmā</s>, or even before that. //

children.text: tatra vā tava pade'thavā vasan prākṛtapralaya eti muktatām /
children.translated_text: Dwelling either there or in Your abode, at the time of cosmic dissolution (<s>prākṛta-pralaya</s>), he attains liberation;

children.text: svecchayā khalu purāpi mucyate saṃcibhidya jagadaṇḍamojasā //
children.translated_text: or, by his own will, he is liberated even before, bursting through the cosmic egg by his might. //
And [he passes through] the sevenfold covering of that [cosmic egg] — earth, water, fire, wind, space, <s>mahat</s> (cosmic intellect), and <s>Prakṛti</s> —

children.text: tattadātmakatayā viśan sukhī yāti te padamanāvṛtaṃ vibho! //
children.translated_text: entering each as identical with its essence, happy, he reaches Your uncovered abode, O Lord! //

children.text: arcirādigatimīdṛśīṃ vrajan vicyutiṃ na bhajate jagatpate! /
children.translated_text: Traversing this path of light (<s>arcirādi</s>), the Lord of the world does not undergo return, O Lord of the world!
O One whose nature is Being-Consciousness! Through the arising of Your qualities — singing [of them], O Lord of the Wind-Temple! protect me! //
Before the primordial dissolution, this [universe], neither manifest nor unmanifest, was nothing at all
When <s>Māyā</s> (illusion), whose modifications had ceased due to the equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), had dissolved into You,

children.text: no mṛtyuśca tadāmṛtaṃ ca samabhūnnāhno na rātreḥ sthiti-
children.translated_text: there was then neither death nor immortality, neither the existence of day nor of night;
there You alone shone, as the very essence of the manifestation of supreme bliss.

children.text: kālaḥ karma guṇāśca jīvanivahā viśvaṃ ca kāryaṃ vibho!
children.translated_text: Time, <s>karma</s> (action), the <s>guṇas</s>, the multitude of <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls), and the entire created universe, O Lord,
when You were absorbed in the sport of consciousness, all of these had attained a state of dissolution.

children.text: teṣāṃ naiva vadantyasattvamayi bhoḥ! śaktyātmanā tiṣṭhatām
children.translated_text: Of them, while they subsisted by way of potency, one does not say they were non-existent, O Lord!

children.text: no cet kiṃ gaganaprasunasadṛśāṃ bhūyo bhavet sambhavaḥ //
children.translated_text: For otherwise, how could there be a re-emergence for those resembling flowers in the sky?
Thus, when the period of two <s>parārdhas</s> had passed and You bore the gaze of creative will,

children.text: bibhrāṇe tvayi cukṣume tribhuvanībhāvāya māyā svayam /
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s> herself stirred forth to bring about the existence of the three worlds.
From <s>Māyā</s> indeed, the power of time, the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), and inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>)
emerged, and manifesting the <s>guṇas</s>, they performed their auxiliary function for her.
Present near <s>Māyā</s> yet without entering her in bodily form, You are celebrated as the Witness;
the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) who entered her through reflections of differentiation is truly none other [than You].
Then, awakened by time and the rest, and impelled by You as well,

children.text: māyā sā khalu buddhitattvamasṛjad yo'sau mahānucyate //
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s> created the <s>Buddhi-tattva</s> (principle of intellect), which is called <s>Mahat</s> (the Great).

children.text: tatrāsau triguṇātmako'pi ca mahān sattvapradhānaḥ svayaṃ
children.translated_text: That <s>Mahat</s>, though constituted of the three <s>guṇas</s>, is itself predominantly <s>sattva</s> (pure);
in this <s>jīva</s>, it effects the awakening of the undifferentiated sense of 'I' (<s>aham</s>).
From <s>Mahat</s>, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle), which produces differentiated awareness, was created;
nourished by the three <s>guṇas</s>, predominantly <s>tamas</s> (darkness), O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by Your impulsion.
That <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, by the sequence of the three <s>guṇas</s>, attained a threefold nature — <s>Vaikārika</s> (modified),
<s>Taijasa</s> (luminous), and <s>Tāmasa</s> (dark) — and You, by the first, of the nature of <s>sattva</s>,
created the gods who preside over the senses: the [deities of the] directions, Wind, Sun, <s>Pāśī</s> (<s>Varuṇa</s>), the <s>Aśvins</s>,
Fire, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), <s>Mitra</s>, the Moon, <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), and <s>Rudra</s> as their embodiments.
O Infinite one! The inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), endowed with the functions called mind (<s>manas</s>), intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), ego (<s>ahaṅkṛti</s>), and <s>citta</s>,

children.text: taccāntaḥ karaṇaṃ vibho! tava balāt sattvāṃś evāsṛjat /
children.translated_text: O Lord, that was also produced from the <s>sattva</s> aspect, by Your power.
From the <s>Taijasa</s> (luminous aspect) arose the group of ten sense organs; and from its <s>Tāmasa</s> (dark) aspect,
the <s>tanmātra</s> (subtle element) of space — namely, sound — was born, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, by Your power.

children.text: śabdād vyāma tataḥ sasarjitha vibho! sparśaṃ tato mārutaṃ
children.translated_text: From sound, You created space; from that, touch, and thence wind;

children.text: tasmād rūpamato maho'thaca rasaṃ toyaṃ gandhaṃ mahīm /
children.translated_text: from that, form, and thence light; then taste, water; then smell, and earth.
Thus, O <s>Mādhava</s>, from the inclusion of each preceding [element], each successive [element] possesses the properties of the earlier ones;
this group of elements You, O Lord, manifested from the <s>Tāmasa</s> (dark) [aspect].
These groups of elements, and likewise the groups of senses and the gods, born separately,
were unable, even together with the gods, to accomplish the creation of the cosmic egg.
You, praised by various Vedic hymns, entering into these principles,
arousing the power of activity, combining them all, fashioned the golden egg (<s>Hiraṇyāṇḍa</s>).

children.text: aṇḍaṃ tat khalu pūrvasṛṣṭasalile'tiṣṭhat sahasraṃ samā
children.translated_text: That egg remained in the primordially created waters for a thousand years;
breaking it open, You fashioned the form of the fourteen worlds, called <s>Virāṭ</s> (the Cosmic Person).
With thousands of hands, feet, heads, and other members, embodying all living beings,

children.text: nirbhāto'si marutpurādhipa! sa māṃ trāyasva sarvāmayāt //
children.translated_text: You manifested [as <s>Virāṭ</s>], O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! May He protect me from all ailments.
Thus, having attained the nature of the fourteen worlds,
they say, O Lord, that the netherworld (<s>Pātāla</s>) is Your sole,
and the region above the feet, O God, is <s>Rasātala</s>;
Your pair of ankles is indeed <s>Mahātala</s>, O wondrous one!
The shanks are <s>Talātala</s>, and the knees <s>Sutala</s>;
the pair of thighs is the two [regions] <s>Vitala</s> and <s>Atala</s>.
The surface of the earth is Your loins; the sky, O limbed one, Your navel;
and Your chest is the abode of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), O Wielder of the discus!
Your neck is <s>Mahas</s> (the world of greatness); Your mouth is <s>Janas</s> (the world of beings); <s>Tapas</s> (the world of austerity)
is Your forehead; and Your head, of him who comprises all, is <s>Satya</s> (the world of truth).
Thus, to You who are the universe in form, O Lord, and who are embodied
also by other beings that depend on the world — obeisance to You, O Lord!
The aperture of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmarandhra</s>) at Your crown, O Lord, is the root of the universe;
the Vedic meters are Your hair, O Lord of hair, and the rain-clouds are Your locks.
Your pair of gleaming eyebrows is the abode of <s>Brahmā</s> (the Creator);
Your eyelashes are night and day, and the Sun is Your eyes.
The creation of the entire universe is but a sidelong glance of Yours;
Your ears are the directions; the pair of <s>Aśvins</s> are Your two nostrils.
Greed and modesty, O Lord, are Your lower and upper lips;
the hosts of stars are Your teeth, and <s>Yama</s> (Death) is Your fang.
<s>Māyā</s> is Your playful laughter; breath is the wind;
Your tongue is water; speech, O Lord, is the flock of birds.
The <s>Siddhas</s> and others are the musical notes; the opening of the mouth is fire;
the gods are Your arms; and Your pair of breasts is <s>Dharma</s>.
Your back is <s>Adharma</s> (unrighteousness), O God; the Moon is [Your] mind;
the unmanifest itself is the lotus of the heart, O lotus-eyed one!
The belly is the multitude of oceans; garments are the twilights;
the organ of generation is <s>Prajāpati</s>; and in the testicles is <s>Mitra</s>.
The buttocks are the herds of deer; the nails of the feet are
elephants, camels, horses, and the like; and locomotion is time.
The face, arms, beautiful thighs, and feet of You,
O ocean of compassion, are the abodes of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and other <s>varṇas</s> (social orders).
The cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) is [Your cycle], O bearer of the discus; Your actions
are valor; the hosts of great <s>asuras</s> are [Your] bones; the mountains are the skeletal frame.
The rivers are the veins; the trees are the body-hair —
may this body of Yours, indescribable, O Lord, be victorious!
This universe-pervading body of Yours, they say, is to be contemplated
by those engaged in <s>karma</s> (ritual action) at the time of the conclusion of their actions.
To You, whose inner form is the pure Self —
O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, obeisance! Ward off [my] diseases.
Thus, O God, having been born in the form of the fourteen-world universe,

children.text: tasyodharvaṃ khalu satyalokanikalaye jāto'si dhātā svayam /
children.translated_text: above that again, in the abode of <s>Satyaloka</s>, You Yourself were born as the Creator (<s>Dhātā</s>),
whom they extol as <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the Golden Embryo), the soul of all beings in the three worlds,
who became endowed with the abundant desire to create, arising from the burgeoning modification of <s>rajas</s> (passion).
He, with his heart given over to the creation of the universe, looking about on his own,
not having attained knowledge regarding the universe, remained troubled with anxiety.

children.text: tāvat tvaṃ jagatāṃ pate! tapa tapetyevaṃ hi vaihāyasīṃ
children.translated_text: Then You, O Lord of the worlds, caused him to hear a celestial
voice, pleasing to the ear, urging him to austerity: 'Perform <s>tapas</s> (austerity)!'
'Who is this person that speaks to me?' — thus, in the world-sphere filled with water,
looking in all directions and not perceiving anything, yet grasping the meaning of the words,
for a divine thousand years he worshipped You with accomplished austerity,
and to him You revealed Your own abode, the wondrous <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>.

children.text: māyā yatra kadāpi no vikurute bhāte jagadbhyate bahiḥ
children.translated_text: Where <s>Māyā</s> never effects any transformation; which shines forth beyond all worlds;
where states such as grief, anger, delusion, and fear have gone far away;
where there is a flood of dense bliss, of the nature of supreme radiant light —

children.text: tat te dhāma vibhāvitaṃ vijayate vaikuṇṭharūpaṃ vibho! //
children.translated_text: that abode of Yours, in the form of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, triumphs, O Lord!
Wherein four-armed beings, of dark complexion like sapphire with bright radiance,
illuminating all directions with the splendor of their various gem-ornaments, dwelling in radiant celestial mansions,
divine beings who have attained such exalted states through devotion sport in bliss —

children.text: tat te dhāma nirastasarvaśamalaṃ vaikuṇṭharūpaṃ jayet //
children.translated_text: may that spotless abode of Yours, in the form of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, be victorious!
Attended by various divine women, with a body lovely as a flash of lightning,
enchanting to the entire universe with her graceful limbs, illuminating all the quarters,
<s>Lakṣmī</s> herself is seen, her sole delight being devotion to the lotus of Your feet —

children.text: yasmin vismayanīyadivyavibhavā tat te oadaṃ dehi me //
children.translated_text: in that [abode] of wondrous divine splendor — grant me that state, [O Lord]!
There, when His own abode was thus revealed, seated upon a jeweled throne,
radiant with millions of gleaming crowns, bracelets, and other ornaments,
marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> sign, bearing the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem, reddened by its glow — the cause

children.text: viśveṣāṃ tava rūpamaikṣata vidhistat te vibho! bhātu me //
children.translated_text: of all beings — that form of Yours did <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) behold. May that, O Lord, shine upon me!
With a luster soft as a blue rain-cloud, covering the circle of the directions with the discus,
with a face brightened by the flow of a generous, gentle smile,
with a glorious circle of arms bearing the radiant conch, mace, sword, and lotus —
may that form of Yours, which delighted the Creator, O Lord, dispel my diseases!
Seeing [You], the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>, filled with wonder, fell
at the lotus of Your feet, overcome with the rush of joy, becoming fulfilled with love.

children.text: jānāsyeva manīṣitaṃ mama vibho! jñānaṃ tadāpādaya
children.translated_text: 'You know my heart's desire, O Lord! Grant me that knowledge
supreme, concerning Your true nature, both dual and non-dual' — thus he addressed You, whom I worship.

children.text: ātāmre caraṇe vinamramatha taṃ hastena haste spṛśan
children.translated_text: Touching with Your hand his hand as he bowed at Your reddish feet, [You said:]
'Knowledge shall be yours; and even in the acts of creation, no bondage shall arise.'

children.text: ityābhāṣya giraṃ pratoṣyta nitarāṃ taccittagūḍhaḥ svayaṃ
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken and gladdened him greatly, You Yourself, hidden within his mind,
impelled him toward creation. O Lord, may [that] shine forth with delight!

children.text: evaṃ tāvat prākṛtaprakṣayānte brāhme kalpe hyādime labdhajanmā /
children.translated_text: Thus, at the end of the dissolution of [the previous] material creation, at the very first <s>Brāhma</s> <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic day), having obtained birth,

children.text: brahmā bhūyastvatta evāpya vedān sṛṣṭiṃ cakre pūrvakalpopamānām //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, receiving the Vedas again from You, performed creation resembling that of the previous <s>kalpa</s>.
He has spent many [cosmic] days measured by a thousand sets of four <s>yugas</s>,
and nights of equal measure.
When he sleeps, merged in You along with his creations,
they call that the <s>naimittika-pralaya</s> (periodic dissolution), and that is his night.
For beings like ourselves, he performs creation comparable to the daily routine
each day, by Your grace;
and for those born in the earlier <s>Brāhma</s> <s>kalpa</s>, whose lifespan is supreme,
that creation is like an awakening from sleep.
Now, in the form of one half of his own age,
having surpassed one <s>parārdha</s>, he continues [in the second].
O Infinite One, I shall now recount the events of the [most recent] night's end,
and Your divine plays at the commencement of the [present] day.
At the day's end, the lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>), desiring deep sleep, merged into You;
and the worlds entered Your belly — thus the entire universe became a single ocean.

children.text: tavaiva veṣe phaṇirāji śeṣe jalaikaśeṣe bhuvane sma śeṣe /
children.translated_text: In Your own guise, upon the serpent-king <s>Śeṣa</s>, in the world that was nothing but water, You reclined —
Your essential nature being the experience of dense bliss, Your Self sealed in <s>Yoganidrā</s> (the sleep of cosmic yoga).
At the very outset, by Your command, 'Awaken at the end of dissolution,' addressed to the power called Time,
You slept there, with the host of all dormant powers, the abode of all <s>jīvas</s>.

children.text: caturyugāṇāṃ ca sahasramevaṃ tvayi prasupte punaradvitīye /
children.translated_text: When You had slept for the second [period of] a thousand sets of four <s>yugas</s>,

children.text: kālākhyaśaktiḥ prathamaprabuddhā prāvodhayat tvāṃ kila viśvanātha //
children.translated_text: the power called Time, awakening first, aroused You, O Lord of the universe.

children.text: vibudhya ca tvaṃ jalagarbhaśāyin! vilokya lokānakhilān pralīnān /
children.translated_text: Awakening, O You who recline in the womb of the waters, and seeing all the worlds dissolved,

children.text: teṣveva sūkṣmātmatayā nijāntaḥ sthiteṣu viśveṣu dadātha dṛṣṭim //
children.translated_text: You cast Your gaze upon all those worlds that lay within You in subtle form.
Then from the aperture of Your navel, O Lord, there rose up a certain divine lotus,
in bud form, containing in compressed form the entire series of dissolved objects.
That lotus bud, sprouting from Your body upon the surface of the waters,
having emerged outward, with its own radiance shining in all directions, dispelled the enveloping darkness.

children.text: saṃphullapatre nitarāṃ vicitre tasmin bhavadvīryadhṛte saroje /
children.translated_text: Upon that lotus, with petals fully unfolded and exceedingly variegated, sustained by Your power,
<s>Brahmā</s>, the lotus-born Creator, appeared — with the entire treasury of the Vedas self-awakened within him.
In this <s>Pādma</s> <s>kalpa</s>, O Supreme Self, You thus raised up the lotus-born one;

children.text: anantabhumā mama rogarāśiṃ nirundhi vātālayavās! viṣṇo! //
children.translated_text: O Infinite One, ward off the mass of my diseases, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who dwells at <s>Guruvāyūr</s>!
He, the lotus-born, standing upon the lotus sprung from Your navel,
'Whence has this arisen upon the waters?' — thus wondering, not perceiving [the source],
curious to see it, turning his face in every direction,
he attained four-facedness, with eight eyes blossoming like lotuses.
Seeing only that very lotus, tossing about upon the great ocean,

children.text: vilokya tadupāśrayaṃ tava tanuṃ tu nālokayan /
children.translated_text: and not beholding Your body, which was its support,

children.text: ka eṣa kamalodare mahati nissahāyo hyahaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Who am I, here within this great lotus, helpless?
Whence has this lotus come into being?' — such was the anxiety that seized him.

children.text: amuṣya hi saroruhaḥ kimapi kāraṇaṃ sambhaved
children.translated_text: 'Surely there must be some cause of this lotus' —
having thus made up his mind, he descended through the passage of the stalk;
endowed with the power of <s>yoga</s> and knowledge, of mature intellect, he descended,
yet did not behold Your supremely enchanting body.
Then, traveling through every aperture of the entire stalk, searching,
for a hundred years he searched, yet found nothing at all.
Having returned to the lotus-womb, seated comfortably, with single-pointed mind,
he gathered the power of <s>samādhi</s>, yearning solely for Your grace.
After a hundred divine years, shining with the splendor of firm <s>samādhi</s>,
that lotus-born one was indeed purified by the dawning of awakening.
With his inner vision, he beheld Your wondrous form, never seen before,
resting upon the coils of the great serpent, with a satisfied mind.
A crown, brilliant earrings, necklace, armlets,
a girdle sparkling with gems, and well-draped yellow garments,
with the radiance of the <s>kalāya</s> flower, the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem gleaming on the throat —
that form, O Lord! — I meditate upon what was revealed to the lotus-born.
O Lord of <s>Śrī</s>, whose abundant glory is shown by the assemblage of the <s>Śrutis</s>!

children.text: hare! jaya jaya prabho! padamupaiṣi diṣṭyā dṛśoḥ /
children.translated_text: O <s>Hari</s>! Victory, victory, O Lord! By good fortune You have come within the reach of my eyes!
Quickly grant me an intellect skillful in the creation of the worlds —
thus praised by <s>Brahmā</s>, whose own virtues' greatness was thereby affirmed — protect me!
'Receive the unimpaired ability to create the three worlds;

children.text: gṛhāṇa madanugrahaṃ kuru tapaśca bhūyo vidhe! /
children.translated_text: accept my grace, and perform further austerities, O <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>)!
May all-accomplishing devotion to Me, most intense, arise in you' —
thus having spoken, You made <s>Brahmā</s> joyful in heart.
Then for a hundred divine years he performed austerities,

children.text: navāpya ca tapobalaṃ matibalaṃ ca pūrvādhikam /
children.translated_text: and having obtained the power of <s>tapas</s> and the power of intellect greater than before,

children.text: udīkṣya kila kampitaṃ payasi paṅkajaṃ vāyunā
children.translated_text: seeing the lotus shaken by the wind upon the water,
by Your power expanding, he drank in the wind and the waters.

children.text: tavaiva kṛpayā punaḥ sarasijena tenaiva sa
children.translated_text: By Your grace again, with that very lotus,
he proceeded to fashion the three worlds and began the creation of beings.
O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, laden with such compassion!
Quickly protect me with Your glances moistened with great mercy!
O <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>! Then, with strength augmented by Your grace,
the lotus-born one created the bodies of living beings.
Immovable things made of trees, then the species of animals,
the hosts of humans, and also the varieties of gods.
False attachment, egoism, passion, agitation, and fear —
having created these five kinds of ignorant tendencies,
distressed by the creation of things steeped in the darkest <s>tamas</s>,
he resorted to the remembrance of Your feet for purification.
Then with his mind he created <s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sananda</s>,
and again <s>Sanātana</s> the sage, and <s>Sanatkumāra</s>.
But they, when directed by him to the work of creation,
relishing devotion to Your feet, did not accept his command.
Then, from the suppressed anger that arose in him,
from between his brows was born <s>Mṛḍa</s> (<s>Rudra</s>), a portion of You.

children.text: nāmāni me kuru padāni ca hā viriñcet
children.translated_text: 'Give me names and give me abodes, O <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>)!' —

children.text: yadau rurod kila tena sa rudranāmā //
children.translated_text: because he wept, he received the name <s>Rudra</s> (the Weeper).
Having fashioned <s>Rudra</s> in eleven forms,
with eleven names, and having given him beloved consorts,
and having granted him as many abodes, impelled by You,
he instructed him, along with his wives, to create progeny.
When the host of <s>Rudras</s> created by <s>Rudra</s>, terrifying in form,
began to fill the three worlds, the lotus-born one, frightened in heart,

children.text: mā mā prajāḥ sṛja tapaścara maṅgalāyet
children.translated_text: 'Do not, do not create progeny! Perform austerities for auspiciousness!' —
thus the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>, inspired by You, beseeched him.
Then, for that one who delighted in creation: <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>,
and <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Kratu</s>, <s>Mini</s> (Pulaha?), <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>,
from his limbs was born <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and also <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Dakṣa</s>,
and the glorious <s>Śrī Nārada</s>, the servant of Your feet.
Having created <s>Dharma</s> and others, and also <s>Kardama</s>,
and having fashioned <s>Vāṇī</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>), <s>Brahmā</s> was seized by desire.
Admonished by Your enlightened sons, led by <s>Sanaka</s> and <s>Dakṣa</s>,
he was awakened and desisted, abandoning <s>tamas</s> (darkness).
Producing the gods, the hosts of ancient beings, and all the sciences
from his own mouths, that four-faced one,
having entrusted the growth of creation to those sons
and finding no success, took refuge at Your lotus feet.
Knowing the means, the unborn one then divided his body,
taking on female and male forms — as <s>Manu</s> and his consort.
Through those two, multiplying the human races — O <s>Govinda</s>!
O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Ward off my diseases!

children.text: krameṇa sarge parivardhamāne kadāpi divyāḥ sanakādayaste /
children.translated_text: In the course of time, as creation grew, once the divine <s>Sanaka</s> and others,
desiring to see You, arrived at <s>Vaikuṇṭhaloka</s>, O Lord of the Temple of the Wind!
With charming groves of <s>Śreyasa</s> trees, with many lakes and jeweled pavilions,

children.text: anopamaṃ taṃ bhavato niketaṃ munīśvarāḥ prāpuratītakakṣyāḥ //
children.translated_text: those chiefs among sages reached Your incomparable abode, passing beyond all boundaries.

children.text: bhavaddidṛkṣūn bhavanaṃ vivikṣūn dvāḥsthau jayastān vijayo'pyarundhām /
children.translated_text: The two doorkeepers, <s>Jaya</s> and <s>Vijaya</s>, barred those who wished to see You and enter Your dwelling;

children.text: teṣāṃ ca citte padamāpa kopaḥ sarvaṃ bhavatpreraṇayaiva bhūman //
children.translated_text: and anger arose in their hearts — all by Your own prompting, O Supreme One!
'You two, whose conduct is unworthy of <s>Vaikuṇṭhaloka</s>, may you go to the fate of <s>daityas</s>!' —

children.text: iti praśaptau bhavadāśrayau tau harismṛtirno'stviti nematustān //
children.translated_text: thus cursed, those two, devoted to You, bowed to the sages, praying 'May our memory of <s>Hari</s> remain!'
Knowing this, You, O Lotus-Eyed One, came forth together with <s>Lakṣmī</s>,
Your beautiful arm resting on the shoulder of <s>Garuḍa</s>, delighting them with Your enchanting form.

children.text: prasādya gīrbhiḥ stuvato munīndrānananyanāthāvatha pārṣadau tau /
children.translated_text: Having pleased the chief sages who were praising You with hymns, and then addressing those two attendants who had no other protector,
You spoke with compassion assumed: 'After three births, come to Me.'

children.text: tvadīyabhṛtyau kila kāśyapāt tau surārivīrāvuditau ditau dvau /
children.translated_text: Those two servants of Yours, born from <s>Kaśyapa</s> and <s>Diti</s>,
became two mighty heroes among the enemies of the gods, like twin <s>Yamas</s> to the world,

children.text: hiraṇyapūrvaḥ kaśipuḥ kilaikaḥ puro hiraṇyākṣa iti pratītaḥ /
children.translated_text: engaging in terrible deeds of creating havoc at twilight.
One was <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, the other known as <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>;
both, blinded by their own predispositions, angrily obstructed the entire world, which is Yours, O Lord.

children.text: bhavatpriyāṃ kṣmāṃ salile nimajjya cacāra garvād vinadan gadāvān //
children.translated_text: That <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, the great lord of <s>asuras</s>, rushing to battle without finding an equal foe,

children.text: tato jaleśāt sadṛśaṃ bhavantaṃ niśamya babhrāma gaveṣayaṃstvām /
children.translated_text: plunged Your beloved Earth into the waters and roamed about arrogantly, bellowing, club in hand.

children.text: bhaktaikadṛśyaḥ sa kṛpānidhe! tvaṃ nirundhi rogān marudālayeśa! //
children.translated_text: Then, hearing from the Lord of Waters that You were his match, he roamed about searching for You.
O Treasury of Compassion, You who are visible only to the devoted! Ward off my diseases, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>!
<s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>, by nature devoted to the creation of beings,
seeing the earth sinking untimely into the waters,
took refuge in the Creator, whose heart was pleased by the service of Your feet,
together with the sages in <s>Satyaloka</s>.
'Alas! I create beings, but the earth is submerged! O Lotus-Born One, provide an abode for the creatures!' —
thus when <s>Manu</s> spoke to him,
<s>Brahmā</s>, O Lotus-Eyed One, meditated upon Your two feet.

children.text: hā hā vibho! jalamahaṃ nyapibaṃ purastād
children.translated_text: 'Alas, alas, O Lord! I drank up the waters before,
yet even now the earth sinks — what shall I do?'
Thus, as he took refuge at Your two feet,
from his nostril You emerged in the form of a tiny boar.
Having sprung forth, the size of a thumb at first,
You then swelled to the size of an elephant.
Beholding You thus in the sky, of such a form,
<s>Brahmā</s>, along with his sons, was struck with great wonder.
'Who is this one of inconceivable glory, risen from my nostril?
Could this be the <s>māyā</s> of the Unconquered One?' —
while the Creator pondered thus, You, now mountain-sized,
instantly roared a most terrible roar.
Hearing that thunderous sound of Yours, the people dwelling in austerity
and the sages established in <s>Satya</s> (truth) praised You.
Gladdened in heart by those hymns of praise, roaring again,
You descended into the great waters in Your immense form.
With bristling, upward-rising, tawny-dark hair,
with tail raised aloft and fearsome downward-facing snout,
swiftly scattering the clouds, with rolling eyes,
You descended upon the heads of the praising sages.
Then, entering the depths of the water, teeming with crocodiles,
swarming with whales, with turbid garlands of waves,
with a terrifying roar, causing the denizens of <s>Rasātala</s>
to tremble, You searched for the Earth.
Then seeing the Earth, placed at the edge of <s>Rasātala</s>
by that wicked <s>daitya</s>, O Lord, You, the false boar,
disregarding the oncoming shields of the enemies of the gods,
with the tip of Your tusk, playfully lifted up the Earth.
Then, raising the Earth with the tip of Your tooth,
looking as if adorned with sprouts of <s>mustā</s> grass clinging to Your tusks, with an exceedingly robust body,
rising from the ocean with its violently churning waters —
O Lord in the form of the sporting Boar (<s>Krīḍāvarāha</s>)! Protect me from disease!
O Bestower of Boons! Meanwhile, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, intent on searching for You,
roaming in the <s>Sāṃvarta</s> (dissolution) waters, measuring his own shin-depth,
the sage <s>Nārada</s>, clever in deception, went to him, sent by You,
and slowly spoke, pleasing the <s>Danuja</s> while disparaging Your strength.
'That trickster <s>Viṣṇu</s> is stealing your Earth,
O Lord! Alas, alas! What is this?' — thus addressed by him,

children.text: nadan kvāsau kvāsāviti sa muninā darśitaptho
children.translated_text: roaring 'Where is he? Where is he?', shown the way by the sage,
he reached You as You were rising from the waters bearing the Earth.

children.text: aho āraṇyo'yaṃ mṛga iti hasantaṃ bahutarair
children.translated_text: 'Ho! This is a wild forest beast!' — laughing thus and assailing You
with many abusive words, that son of <s>Diti</s> — disregarding him, O <s>Bhagavān</s>,

children.text: mahīṃ dṛṣṭvā daṃṣṭrāśirasi cakitāṃ svena mahasā
children.translated_text: seeing the Earth trembling on the tip of Your tusk, frightened by his own might,
You placed her upon the ocean and swiftly engaged in battle.
The <s>daitya</s> had club in hand, and You too grasped Your upraised club;
playing at combat, the sky resounding with the clash upon clash,
while the host of gods gathered swiftly, eager to witness the battle —
'Destroy him before twilight!' — thus <s>Brahmā</s> urged You, O Lord of the World.
In that clash of clubs, when Your club, O Lord, from the blow of the <s>Diti</s>-son's
club, suddenly fell to the ground — oh my!
with a gentle smile on Your face, You recalled the terrible <s>Sudarśana</s> discus,
capable of annihilating the entire <s>Danuja</s> race, and placed it in Your palm — and You shone!
Then, when the <s>daitya</s>, in fury like Death itself, hurled his trident,
You shattered it with the stroke of the discus held in Your hand.

children.text: samāruṣṭo muṣṭyā sa khalu vitudaṃstvāṃ samatamod
children.translated_text: He climbed upon You, pounding You with his fists, and was greatly pleased with himself,
releasing his <s>māyā</s> powers upon You — those that delude the entire world.
When his web of <s>māyā</s> was scattered by the falling of sparks from Your discus's radiance,
then, with dense fury blinding his mind,
as the <s>asura</s> struck with the heaviest fist-blows,
You killed him with the edge of Your palm at the base of his ear.
That great-bodied one, struck down by the lotus of Your hand,
with blood flowing from his mouth, fell — his slaying praised by the sages.
Then, their hearts radiant with the overflowing wave of joy,
the chief sages praised You with abundant hymns, O Jewel of Sacrifice.
'The <s>Vedic</s> meters are in Your skin, and the <s>kuśa</s> grass in Your hair; in Your eyes is <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter);
the four chief priests are in Your hooves; the ladle (<s>sruk</s>) is in Your mouth; and <s>iḍā</s> (oblation) in Your belly;

children.text: grahā jihvāyāṃ te parapuruṣa! karṇe ca camasā
children.translated_text: the sacrificial cups (<s>graha</s>) are on Your tongue, O Supreme Being; and the <s>camasa</s> cups in Your ears;
O Lord! <s>Soma</s> is Your virility, O Bestower of Boons; and the <s>upasad</s> rites are in Your throat.'
Delighted in mind by these and other praises uttered by the chief sages,
shining with that most majestic form and most spotless fame,
having reached Your own abode, O Slayer of <s>Madhu</s>, dwelling in the bliss of joy —
ward off all my diseases, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>!
That <s>Manu</s>, born from the body of <s>Brahmā</s>, remembering Your pair of feet,

children.text: nijamantaramantarāyahīnaṃ caritaṃ te kathayan sukhaṃ nināya //
children.translated_text: spent his time happily, narrating Your deeds, free from obstacles, during his own <s>Manvantara</s>.
At the proper time, the one named <s>Kardama</s>, born from the shadow of <s>Brahmā</s>,
at his word, possessed of zeal for creation, naturally charming, worshipped You, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, for ten thousand years.
Upon <s>Garuḍa</s>, beautiful like a dark rain-cloud, with a sporting lotus in Your hand-lotuses,

children.text: hasitollasitānanaṃ vibho! tvaṃ vapurāviṣkuruṣe sma kardamāya //
children.translated_text: with a smiling, radiant face, O Lord, You revealed Your form to <s>Kardama</s>.

children.text: stuvate pulakāvṛtāya tasmai manuputrīṃ dayitāṃ navāpi putrīḥ /
children.translated_text: To him, covered with horripilation and praising You, You promised a beloved wife from <s>Manu</s>'s daughters, and nine daughters,

children.text: kapilaṃ ca sutaṃ svameva paścāt svagatiṃ cāpyanugṛhya nirgato'bhūḥ //
children.translated_text: and <s>Kapila</s> as a son, Your very own Self; and later, granting him Your own state, You departed.

children.text: sa manuḥ śatarūpayā mahiṣyā guṇavatyā sutayā ca devahūtyā /
children.translated_text: That <s>Manu</s>, with his queen <s>Śatarūpā</s> and his virtuous daughter <s>Devahūti</s>,
instructed by <s>Nārada</s> who was inspired by You, approached <s>Kardama</s>, who was awaiting his arrival.
And <s>Kardama</s>, having received <s>Devahūti</s>, offered by <s>Manu</s>, that jewel among young women —
though delighted by worship of You, he bestowed his favor upon her through steadfast service. //
Then, by the power of worshipping You, when the aerial chariot was made for the sake of his beloved's desire,
he, his soul renewed, sported in the celestial paths with <s>Devahūti</s>, amidst a multitude of women. //

children.text: śatavarṣamatha vyatītya so'yaṃ nava kanyāḥ samavāpya dhanyarūpāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, after a hundred years had passed, having obtained nine daughters of blessed form,
though ready to depart for the forest, being devoted to his wife's welfare and eager for Your worship, he remained. //
Then, O Lord, when <s>Devahūti</s> was devoted to Your service at her husband's word,
You were born as <s>Kapila</s>, to proclaim the knowledge of the supreme Self to all beings. //
When <s>Kardama</s>, pleased, was departing for the forest, You taught the essence of all doctrines to Your mother.

children.text: kapilātmaka! vāyumadireś! tvaritaṃ tvaṃ paripāhi māṃ gadaughāt //
children.translated_text: O You of <s>Kapila</s>'s form! O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Quickly protect me from the multitude of diseases! //
The mind attached to the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature) creates bondage; when detached from them,
it brings liberation; <s>bhaktiyoga</s> (the yoga of devotion) indeed arrests attachment.
Devotion, attainable through association with the great, is itself the goal to be achieved here —
thus You, in the form of <s>Kapila</s>, declared to <s>Devahūti</s>. //
<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), <s>Mahat</s> (cosmic intellect), <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), the <s>Mātrās</s> (subtle elements), the gross elements too,
the heart, the ten sense-organs, and <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self) as the twenty-fifth —
one who knows these distinctions is liberated from <s>Prakṛti</s> —
thus You, in the form of <s>Kapila</s>, declared to <s>Devahūti</s>. //
This <s>Puruṣa</s> (Self) is not affected by the multitudes of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) belonging to <s>Prakṛti</s>,

children.text: yadi tu sajati tasyāṃ tadguṇāstaṃ bhajeran /
children.translated_text: but if he associates with her, her qualities would possess him.
Through devotion to Me and contemplation of reality, she too is transcended —
thus You, in the form of <s>Kapila</s>, declared to <s>Devahūti</s>. //
One of pure mind, having undertaken postures and other [disciplines], should meditate upon My form,
mounted upon <s>Garuḍa</s>, adorned with divine ornaments and weapons,
of a radiance surpassing the <s>Tamāla</s> tree, constantly and regularly —
thus You, in the form of <s>Kapila</s>, declared to <s>Devahūti</s>. //
Through hearing of the plays of My qualities and attributes, through songs of praise and the like,
a flow of mind toward Me, like the current of the celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), arises —
that becomes supreme devotion, which indeed conquers death —
thus You, in the form of <s>Kapila</s>, declared to <s>Devahūti</s>. //
Alas! One who nourishes his family daily with wealth accumulated through much violence,
enslaved by his wife, doting on children,
such a householder, attached, without devotion to Me, enters into torment —
thus You, in the form of <s>Kapila</s>, declared to <s>Devahūti</s>. //
Afflicted in a woman's womb, though awakened [to consciousness], untimely
losing awareness at birth, overcoming childhood with its pains,
alas, he is deluded again in the time of youth —
thus You, in the form of <s>Kapila</s>, declared to <s>Devahūti</s>. //
The righteous householder who worships the ancestors and the hosts of gods
also falls in time, going by the southern path.
But action dedicated to Me leads to the northern path —
thus You, in the form of <s>Kapila</s>, declared to <s>Devahūti</s>. //
Thus, O Lord, having blessed <s>Devahūti</s>, who fully understood what was to be known,
and who offered praises, You departed with assemblies of <s>yogins</s>.
She too, of purified mind, was liberated through <s>bhaktiyoga</s> (devotion),
and You too abide in the northeast as a <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford) for the welfare of people. //
O Supreme One! What need of many words? You firmly declare
devotion to Your lotus feet, which dispels all fears and leads to all desires.

children.text: vadasi khalu dṛḍhaṃ tvaṃ tvad vidhūyāmayān me
children.translated_text: Dispelling my ailments, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>!
bestow devotion to You upon me! //
<s>Dakṣa</s>, the son of <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), having obtained <s>Prasūti</s>, the daughter of <s>Manu</s>'s son <s>Manas</s>,
begot sixteen daughters.

children.text: dharme trayodaśa dadau piṛṣu svadhāṃ ca
children.translated_text: Thirteen he gave to <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Svadhā</s> to the ancestors,
<s>Svāhā</s> to the fire-god, and <s>Satī</s> to <s>Giriśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), Your own portion. //
<s>Mūrti</s>, the wife of <s>Dharma</s>, gave birth to You,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, companion of <s>Nara</s>, of exalted glory.
At whose birth, the hosts of gods, delighted, sounding musical instruments,
showered forth heaps of flowers and sang praises. //
The demon <s>Sahasrakavaca</s> (Thousand-armored), encased in armors
obtainable only through a thousand years of austerity and a thousand years of battle —
You two, performing austerity and battle in alternation,
slew that [demon], left with but a single armor, along with <s>Lalim</s>. //
Practicing and teaching the <s>dharma</s> of liberation,
You, together with Your brother, dwelt in the hermitage of <s>Badarikā</s>.
<s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), unable to bear the power of Your tranquility and austerity,
dispatched <s>Māra</s> (the tempter), accompanied by celestial maidens. //
<s>Kāma</s> (the god of love), allied with Spring and the Malaya breeze,
with the arrow-glances of beautiful women and their blossoming charms,
struck again and again — but seeing You unmoved,
became afraid and addressed You, who wore a gentle smile. //
'Fear not, O <s>Aṅgaja</s> (Love), <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring), and celestial maidens!
Dwell here in My mind!' — so saying,
You, as they praised You all around in wonder,
revealed to them Your own attendant maidens of bashful eyes. //
<s>Madana</s> (Love) and the others, who had come to bewitch You,
were themselves bewildered by the fragrance of Your handmaidens.
And all of them accepted from You, though with modesty,
that <s>Urvaśī</s>, who humbles the pride of all heaven-dwellers. //

children.text: dṛṣṭvorvaśīṃ tvaṃ kathāṃ ca niśamya śakraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Urvaśī</s> and hearing the tale, <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>)
became agitated, reflecting on Your greatness.
Thus, this incarnation, more serene and beautiful [than others] —
yet superior to You, O Boon-granter, is You Yourself in the form of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! //
<s>Dakṣa</s>, blinded by passion through excessive indulgence in creation,
was not sufficiently respectful to You — and grievously, his hostility continued,
whereby he obstructed <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), who is verily Your own form,
and at the <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), signaling enmity, he dishonored his own daughter. //
His sacrifice destroyed by the enraged Lord (<s>Śiva</s>), his head severed,
then, having obtained life again from <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) who was propitiated by the gods,
his excellent sacrifice completed by You, he again attained peace.
O You who bring tranquility! O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Protect me! //
Of King <s>Uttānapāda</s>, the son of <s>Manu</s>,
the wife <s>Suruci</s> was exceedingly beloved.
The other, named <s>Sunīti</s>, not favored by her husband,
being without refuge, took shelter in You alone always. //
Seeing <s>Suruci</s>'s son on the father's lap, <s>Dhruva</s>, the son of <s>Sunīti</s>,
was about to climb up there,
but the child was sharply repelled by <s>Suruci</s> —
for indeed, jealousy is hard to abandon for those who have turned away from You. //
While the father, deluded by You, looked on, enslaved to his wife,
the boy, struck by harsh words, went far away to his own mother.
She too, [knowing that] for mortals the only means of crossing the course of one's own <s>karma</s>
is Your feet alone as refuge, so she told her child. //
Hearing this, he too, with mind resolved upon worshipping You,
proud [of spirit], departed from the city at merely five years of age.
Having been shown the path of <s>mantras</s> by <s>Nārada</s> whom he had met,
he worshipped You through austerity in the <s>Madhuvana</s> (Madhu forest). //
When the father, with a sorrowful heart, was consoled in mind
by the glorious <s>Nārada</s> who had come to the city,
the boy, with his mind offered to You, through gradually intensifying
severe austerity, passed five months. //
Then, when all the quarters were stifled by the power of his austerity,
You, entreated by the gods, arose with a heart melting with compassion.
Before him whose mind had dissolved into the nectar of contemplating Your form,
You appeared, O Lord, mounted upon <s>Garuḍa</s>! //
Him, tossing in waves of joy at beholding You,
as if immersed through his eyes in the nectar of Your beauty,
wishing to praise You — perceiving this, You touched his cheek
with the edge [of Your conch], with such tender care. //
Thereupon, as he praised You with words brilliant with awakened knowledge,
You addressed him, understanding the desire in his heart:
'Having enjoyed kingship for a long time, attain thereafter, O <s>Dhruva</s>,
the supreme abode, from which there is no return.' //
When You had spoken thus and departed, that prince,
having gladdened all the people, returned to the city.
He rejoiced for a long time, his desires fulfilled by Your grace,
and when his father retired to the forest, he bore the burden of kingship with devotion. //
O Lord, when his superior [brother] was slain by a <s>Yakṣa</s>,
he, engaged in battle with the <s>Yakṣas</s>, was dissuaded by <s>Manu</s>.
From <s>Dhanada</s> (<s>Kubera</s>), whose heart was pleased through peace,
that great soul chose only firm devotion to You. //
At the end, borne in a celestial chariot brought by Your attendants,
together with his mother, he sits joyfully in <s>Dhruva</s>'s station (the Pole Star).
Thus You, whose mind is ever devoted to protecting Your own servants —
O Lord of <s>Vātālaya</s> (<s>Guruvāyūr</s>)! Remove the multitude of my ailments! //
Born indeed in the lineage of <s>Dhruva</s>, of lofty fame,
to <s>Aṅga</s> was born a son named <s>Vena</s>.
That best of kings, his mind troubled by [<s>Vena</s>'s] faults,
with his thoughts fixed on Your feet, departed to the forest. //
Though wicked, <s>Vena</s> was installed for the protection of the earth
by the citizens and others; of cruel valor,
proclaiming his own might above all,
he abolished Your sacrificial rites throughout the realm. //
When the assembly of ascetics came to offer counsel,
[he declared:] 'There is no lord of the world other than me, the intoxicated one!' —
intent on words blaspheming You, by those great sages
<s>Vena</s> was reduced to the fate of a moth in the fire of their curse. //
After his destruction, the chief sages, fearful of wicked people,
long preserved his body through his mother's [care].
When sin was expelled [by churning his leg], and then when the arm-staff was churned,
from the churned arm, You manifested! //
Renowned as <s>Pṛthu</s>, Your future abundant valor
praised by the <s>Sūta</s> and others as instructed by the sages,
You leveled with Your own bow the earth, whose prosperity
had been swallowed by the distress of <s>Vena</s> and which had been overwhelmed. //
Furthermore, with calves being the chief [beings] of each class,
by the gods and others, into proper and beautiful vessels,
food and other desired things —
You, of fragrant form, milked [the earth] freely. //
When You, the three-aboded, undertook with friends
the hundredth <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice),
<s>Śatamakha</s> (<s>Indra</s>), envious, coming in lowly disguise,
stole the horse and was defeated by Your son. //
When <s>Devendra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) repeatedly stole the horse,
[Your son] wished to offer him into the fire before the assembly of great sages.
When <s>Kamalabhava</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) prevented it, at the completion of the sacrifice,
You, the destroyer of <s>Madhu</s>, beheld Yourself directly. //
Having obtained the boon granted [by You] — devotion alone —
established on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, O Lord, at some time,
while imparting beneficial teachings to an assembly of sages engaged in a <s>satra</s> (sacrificial session),
You beheld the sages headed by <s>Sanaka</s> before You. //
Holding the knowledge expounded by <s>Sanaka</s> and the others,
You attained Your own Self, dwelling in the forest's end.
O Lord of such a form as <s>Pṛthu</s>! Swiftly
pacify the multitude of my diseases, O Dweller in <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! //
<s>Prācīnabarhi</s>, the grandson of <s>Pṛthu</s>, devoted to great works of <s>dharma</s>, in the maiden <s>Śatadruti</s>,
begot sons named <s>Pracetas</s>, of good minds, like sprouts of Your compassion. //

children.text: pituḥ sisṛkṣāniratasya śāsanād bhavattapasyāniratā daśāpi te /
children.translated_text: At the command of their father, who was devoted to creation, those ten, devoted to austerity for You,
reaching the western ocean and its shore, beheld a captivating lake. //
Then <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), having arrived at this <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford) of Yours, honored by seeing Your devotees,
appearing before the <s>Pracetases</s>, taught them a hymn to You, being most devoted. //
Chanting that hymn, they worshipped You within the waters for ten thousand years.
Through the taste of bliss in You, for them such time passed like <s>Dhruva</s>'s [lifetime] — without swiftness. //
By their exceedingly growing austerities, even their father, though devoted to sacrificial violence, was purified,
and he too, his true Self revealed by <s>Nārada</s> who came to his home, attained oneness with You. //
Then, by the power of compassion alone, You appeared before the <s>Pracetases</s>, riding upon <s>Garuḍa</s>,
Your splendor heightened by the radiance of the <s>Sudarśana</s> discus and other excellent weapons in Your eight arms. //
To the <s>Pracetases</s>, though they had not even asked, You, out of sheer compassion, gave boons.
'Even mere thought of Me brings welfare to embodied beings; and this hymn of praise to <s>Rudra</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) too fulfills desires.' //

children.text: avāpya kāntāṃ tanayāṃ mahīruhāṃ tayā ramadhvaṃ daśalakṣavatsarīm /
children.translated_text: 'Obtaining a wife, the daughter of the trees, sport with her for ten hundred thousand years.',

children.text: suto'stu dakṣo nanu tatkṣaṇācca māṃ prayāsyatheti nyagado mudaiva tān //
children.translated_text: 'A son named <s>Dakṣa</s> shall be born, and instantly you shall come to Me' — thus You spoke to them with joy. //

children.text: tataśca te bhūtalarodhinastarūn krūdhā dahanto druhiṇena vāritāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thereafter, they, burning with anger the trees that obstructed the earth, were restrained by <s>Druhiṇa</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>),

children.text: drumaiśca dattāṃ tanayāmavāpya tāṃ tvaduktakālaṃ sukhino'bhiremire //
children.translated_text: and having obtained the daughter given by the trees, they rejoiced happily for the time You had specified. //

children.text: avāpya dakṣaṃ ca sutaṃ kṛtādhvarāḥ pracetaso nāradalabdhayā dhiyā /
children.translated_text: Having obtained <s>Dakṣa</s> as a son, the <s>Pracetases</s>, having performed sacrifices, through the wisdom obtained from <s>Nārada</s>,
You who thus opened the door to the abode of bliss — O Lord! O Master of <s>Vātālaya</s> (Guruvāyūr)! Protect me!
From <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, the king born of <s>Priyavrata</s>'s dear son, arose <s>Nābhi</s>,
who beheld You, the bestower of desires, in the midst of the sacred fire, having performed the <s>yajña</s>-rites for Your pleasure alone.
Praised there by the foremost sages, when the king besought a son equal to Yourself,
You, O Universal Form, declaring 'I Myself shall be born,' vanished into the sacred grass (<s>barhis</s>).
Then, from <s>Nābhi</s>'s beloved queen <s>Merudevī</s>, You were partially born, bearing the name <s>Ṛṣabha</s>,
Your extraordinary qualities and prowess delighting all people universally.

children.text: tvayi trilokībhṛti rājybhāraṃ nidhāya nābhiḥ saha merudevyā /
children.translated_text: Depositing the burden of sovereignty upon You, the bearer of the three worlds,

children.text: tapovanaṃ prāpya bhavanniṣevī gataḥ kilānandapadaṃ padaṃ te //
children.translated_text: <s>Nābhi</s> together with <s>Merudevī</s>, attaining a penance-grove and devoted to You, reached Your abode of bliss.
When <s>Indra</s>, enraged at Your superiority, did not send rain upon this land of <s>Ajanābha</s>,

children.text: yadā tadā tvaṃ nijayogaśaktyā svavarṣamenad vyadadhāḥ suvarṣam //
children.translated_text: then You, by the power of Your own <s>yoga</s>, made this land well-rained and abundant.
Then, though of a disposition inclined to self-delight, marrying <s>Jayantī</s> — the lovely one given by the conquered <s>Indra</s> —

children.text: ajījanat tatra śataṃ tanūjān yeṣāṃ kṣitīṣo bharato'grajanmā //
children.translated_text: You begot there a hundred sons, of whom <s>Bharata</s> was the first-born prince.
Nine became great <s>yogins</s>, nine others governed the regions of <s>Bhāratavarṣa</s>,
and eighty-one remaining sons of Yours, through the power of <s>tapas</s> (austerity), attained the status of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Having taught Your sons, in the midst of great sages, the path of liberation endowed with detachment and devotion,
You Yourself adopted the way of a <s>paramahaṃsa</s>, conducting Yourself as one dull-witted, mad, and possessed.
Though the Supreme Self, You wandered instructing others, rejected by all,
free from any agitation, traversing the entire earth, absorbed in the bliss of the undiminished Self.

children.text: śayuvrataṃ gomṛgakākacaryāṃ ciraṃ carannāpya paraṃ svarūpam /
children.translated_text: Long practising the vow of lying down [like a beast], the conduct of cows, deer, and crows, and attaining the supreme essential nature,

children.text: davāhṛtāṅgaḥ kuṭakācale tvaṃ tāpān mamāpākuru vātanātha! //
children.translated_text: Your body was consumed by a forest fire on Mount <s>Kuṭaka</s> — O Lord of <s>Vātālaya</s>, remove my afflictions!
In the central region of the earth, in the land called <s>Ilāvṛta</s>,
which is frequented only by women, with <s>Gaurī</s> foremost among them,
worshipped by <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) with <s>mantras</s> and hymns of praise,
I take refuge in You, O Supreme Lord, in the form of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>.
In the land called <s>Bhadrāśva</s>, the region east of <s>Ilāvṛta</s>,
hymned by the sages named <s>Bhadraśravas</s>,
skilled in retrieving the <s>Vedas</s> hidden at the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age) —
I meditate upon You, O Lord, in the form of <s>Hayaśīrṣa</s> (the Horse-headed one).
I meditate upon You in the southern land, the region of <s>Harivarṣa</s>,
attended by <s>Prahlāda</s> and other chief devotees,
lofty, tranquil, and of resplendent white form, bestowing pure
knowledge alone — upon You, O Lord, as <s>Narahari</s> (Man-Lion)!
In the western land, in beautiful <s>Ketumāla</s>,
with limbs beautiful with a playfully charming, gently smiling special grace,
attended by <s>Lakṣmī</s> and the sons of <s>Prajāpati</s>,
I worship You, who have assumed the form of <s>Kāmadeva</s> for her delight.
In the delightful northern land indeed called <s>Ramyaka</s>,
worshipped by <s>Manu</s>, the lord of that region, with devoted service,
affectionate solely toward devotees, shining in hearts free of envy —
I worship You, O Lord of the world, in the form of <s>Matsya</s> (the Fish)!
In the region called <s>Hiraṇmaya</s>, the northern one,
seated, in the form of a <s>kūrma</s> (tortoise) industrious in holding up the mountain,
the foremost of the assembly of the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors), <s>Aryamā</s>, worships Him —
I worship that You, O Lord, O one whose essence is supreme consciousness!
Moreover, in the northern <s>Kurus</s>, attended by the beloved <s>Dharaṇī</s> (Earth),
worshipped with distinguished categories of exalted <s>mantras</s> and hymns,
of most majestic stature, with the dense [cosmic sphere] grazed by the tip of Your tusks —
protect me, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, in the form of the Great <s>Varāha</s> (Boar), praised by the wise and honored in sacrifice!
In the southern direction, in the land called <s>Kimpuruṣa</s>,
attended by <s>Hanumān</s>, who possesses firm devotion,
of supremely wondrous beauty that delights <s>Sītā</s>,
You, in the form of <s>Rāma</s>, shine resplendently — protect me, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>!
Together with <s>Śrī Nārada</s>, worshipped by the chief [sages] of the <s>Bhārata</s> land,
with hymns of <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and praise,
protecting the virtuous here until the end of the <s>kalpa</s> —
O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, friend of <s>Nara</s>, protect me, O All-pervading One!
In <s>Plākṣa</s> [continent], they worship You in the form of the Sun; in <s>Śālmala</s>, in the form of the Moon;
in the continent called <s>Kuśa</s>, they worship You in the form of Fire;
in <s>Krauñca</s>, in the form of Water; in <s>Śāka</s>, in the form of Wind;
and in the continent called <s>Puṣkara</s>, O Lord, the people worship You in the form of <s>Brahman</s>.
By all — <s>Dhruva</s> and others, by the hosts of stars and planets —
superimposed upon the limbs from the tail onward,
You, in the form of <s>Śiśumāra</s> (the Celestial Dolphin), are worshipped by the great ones;
at the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight prayers), ward off hell from me, O Lord who reclines on the ocean!
In the region at the base of the netherworld, You in the form of <s>Śeṣa</s>,
with a thousand heads resplendent with a single gently swaying earring,
clad in dark-blue garments, bearing a plough, attended by serpent-maidens —
I worship You. Remove my ailments, O Lord of the Guru's abode (<s>Guruvāyūr</s>)!

children.text: ajāmilo nāma mahīsuraḥ purā caran vibho! dharmapathān gṛhāśramī /
children.translated_text: There was formerly a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Ajāmila</s>, O all-pervading Lord, a householder following the paths of <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: gurorgirā kānanametya dṛṣṭavān sughṛṣṭaśīlāṃ kulaṭāṃ madākulām //
children.translated_text: who, going to the forest at his preceptor's word, beheld a wanton woman of corrupt character, besotted with passion.

children.text: svataḥ praśānto'pi tadāhṛtāśayaḥ svadharmamutsṛja tayā samāraman /
children.translated_text: Though naturally tranquil, his mind was seized by her; abandoning his own <s>dharma</s>, he sported with her;

children.text: adharmakārī daśamī bhavan punardadhau bhavannāmayute sute ratim //
children.translated_text: becoming a doer of <s>adharma</s>, in his tenth [decade] he then placed his affection upon a son named after You.
At the time of death, seeing with terror three fearsome servants of <s>Yamarāja</s>,
merely from the force of a slight residual memory of You from former times, he called out to his son named <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Even though of wicked disposition, merely from the glory of the syllables of Your name that issued from him at that moment,
Your attendants — four-armed, clad in yellow garments, and captivating — appeared before him.

children.text: amuṃ ca sampāśya vikarṣato bhaṭān vimuñcatetyārurudhurbalādamī /
children.translated_text: And seeing those soldiers dragging him away with nooses, these [attendants] of Yours forcefully restrained them, crying 'Release him!'

children.text: nivāritāste ca bhavajjanaistadā tadīyapāpaṃ nikhilaṃ nyavedayan //
children.translated_text: When they were thus checked by Your servants, those [messengers of <s>Yama</s>] then enumerated all of his sins.

children.text: bhavantu pāpāni kathaṃ tu niṣkṛte kṛte'pi bho daṇḍanamasti paṇḍitāḥ! /
children.translated_text: 'Let there be sins — but when atonement has been performed, O wise ones, is there [still] punishment?'

children.text: na niṣkṛtiḥ kiīṃ viditā bhavādṛśāmiti prabho! tvatpuruṣā babhāṣire //
children.translated_text: 'Is not the [true] atonement known to ones such as you?' — thus, O Lord, Your servants spoke.

children.text: śrutismṛtibhyāṃ vihitā vratādayaḥ punanti pāpaṃ na lunanti vāsanām /
children.translated_text: 'The observances prescribed by <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> purify sins but do not destroy the latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>);

children.text: anantasevā tu nikṛntati dvayīmiti prabho! tvatpuruṣā babhāṣire //
children.translated_text: but the service of the Infinite (<s>Ananta</s>) cuts both' — thus, O Lord, Your servants spoke.

children.text: anena bho! janmasahasrakoṭibhiḥ kṛteṣu pāpeṣvapi niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtā /
children.translated_text: 'By this one, even for sins committed over billions of births, atonement has been made,

children.text: tadagrahīnnāma bhayākulo hareriti prabho! tvatpuruṣā babhāṣire //
children.translated_text: for he uttered the name of <s>Hari</s>, though seized with fear' — thus, O Lord, Your servants spoke.
'The chanting of <s>Mukunda</s>'s name by humans, even done unknowingly, burns heaps of sin — such is its greatness;

children.text: yathāgniredhāṃsi yathauṣedhaṃ gadāniti prabho! tvatpuruṣā babhāṣire //
children.translated_text: as fire [burns] fuel, as medicine [cures] disease' — thus, O Lord, Your servants spoke.
Thus spoken to, when <s>Yama</s>'s soldiers withdrew and the host of Your soldiers too vanished,

children.text: bhavatsmṛtiṃ kañcana kālamācaran bhavatpadaṃ prāpi bhavadbhaṭairasau //
children.translated_text: he, practicing remembrance of You for some time, was led by Your attendants to Your abode.
<s>Yama</s>, alarmed by the report of his own servants, loudly instructed

children.text: svakīyabhṛtyānaśiśikṣaduccakaiḥ sa deva! vātālaynātha! pāhi mām //
children.translated_text: his attendants: 'Do not approach the devotees of His feet!' — O Lord! O Master of <s>Vātālaya</s>! Protect me!
O Lord, the later <s>Dakṣa</s> too, [born as] <s>Prācetas</s>,
desiring the increase of creation, performed worship of You.
You then appeared before him, resplendent with eight arms,

children.text: tasmai varaṃ daditha tāṃ ca vadhūmasiknīm //
children.translated_text: and granted him a boon, along with the dark maiden (<s>Asiknī</s>) as his bride.
His sons — ten thousand, O Lord, and then a thousand more —
attained Your path through the words of <s>Śrī Nārada</s>.
[<s>Dakṣa</s>], unable to bear their not dwelling in one place, cursed the sage;
but [<s>Nārada</s>], the foremost of devotees, regarded that sage's [curse] as a mere favor.
Thereafter, through sixty daughters, [<s>Dakṣa</s>] produced hosts of lineages;
and his great-grandson's son was <s>Viśvarūpa</s>,
who, armored by a hymn to You, made <s>Indra</s> victorious in battle —
O Lord, Your glory is indeed all-conquering!
Formerly, in the land of <s>Śūrasena</s>, King <s>Citraketu</s>,
childless, obtained a single son through the power of sage <s>Aṅgiras</s>;
but when that son was slain by the hosts of co-wives,
he was overcome by delusion, helplessly, through Your <s>māyā</s> (divine illusion).
<s>Nārada</s>, the compassionate one, together with <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
came to him and showed the <s>jīva</s> (soul) of his son,

children.text: kasyāsmi putra iti tasya girā vimohaṃ
children.translated_text: who said 'Whose son am I?' — and by those words, [<s>Citraketu</s>'s] delusion
was abandoned, and [<s>Nārada</s>] engaged the king in the practice of worshipping You.
Having received a hymn and a <s>mantra</s> from <s>Nārada</s>,
he performed austerities for the pleasure of You in Your <s>Śeṣa</s> form;
indeed, having attained the lordship of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> within seven nights,
his mind filled with supreme eagerness, he worshipped You.
To him, with a form of thousand heads white as lotus-stalks,
surrounded by hosts of <s>Siddhas</s> offering praise —
You appeared before long, and pleased by his hymns,
having bestowed the knowledge of the Self, and having blessed him, You vanished.
And he too, the crest-jewel of Your devotees, for a hundred thousand times a hundred thousand
years, with a joyful mind, freely in the worlds,
made Your host of virtues resound with beautiful women,
and wandered gracefully, free from the stain of attachment.
Impelled by You for the complete dissolution of attachment,
he, upon reaching Mount <s>Rūpya</s> (Silver Mountain), in a great assembly,
fearlessly, with his beloved upon his lap, mocked
