<s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the enemy of <s>Kāma</s> — and was cursed by <s>Umā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>).
Undisturbed, without seeking release from the curse,
having assumed the form of the demon <s>Vṛtra</s>, he fought against the king of the gods (<s>Indra</s>);
through devotion and the narration of the truth of the Self, even in battle, in wondrous fashion,
he dispelled even his enemy's delusion and attained Your abode.
<s>Diti</s>, though intent upon slaying <s>Indra</s>, through devotion to You
obtained instead those very <s>Maruts</s> as friends of <s>Indra</s>;
Your worship bestows good even upon one of wicked intent —
such are You — protect me, O Lord of <s>Pavanālaya</s> (Guruvāyūr)!
When <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> was slain by You, O Lord, in the form of the supreme Boar,
his twin brother, his resolve weakened by the sharp grief of anguish —
<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, in the assembly of the enemies of the gods,
indeed undertook a vow for Your destruction, O Slayer of <s>Mura</s>!

children.text: vidhātāraṃ ghoraṃ sa khalu tapasitvā nacirataḥ
children.translated_text: He, performing terrible austerities, before long made <s>Brahmā</s>
appear directly before him, and [obtained] the boon of death not at the hands of gods, men, beasts, and the like;
and having obtained the boon, arrogant, he afflicted this world — whose master is You —
and seizing heaven from <s>Indra</s>, disregarded You.

children.text: nihantuṃ tvāṃ bhūyastava padamavāptasya ca ripor-
children.translated_text: When the enemy, who had again come to Your abode to slay You,
looked outside, You hid within his heart in a subtle form;
roaring loudly, searching even at the ends of all the worlds,

children.text: bhiyā yātaṃ matvā sa khalu jitakāśī nivavṛte //
children.translated_text: he, thinking You had fled in fear, returned, claiming victory.
Then was born to him a son, <s>Prahlāda</s>, who while still in the womb,
from the sage bearing the <s>vīṇā</s> (<s>Nārada</s>), had absorbed the glory of devotion to You.

children.text: sa vai jātyā daityaḥ śiśurapi sametya tvayi ratiṃ
children.translated_text: He, though a <s>Daitya</s> (demon) by birth, even as a child, having developed love for You,
became, O Bestower of boons, the supreme exemplar among Your devotees.
Seeing in his own son the servitude to Your feet — a laughing-stock among the enemies of the gods —
that fate-driven [father] had the boy instructed by preceptors for a long time;
but [<s>Prahlāda</s>] rejected all that was taught by the preceptors, [regarding it as] firmly
leading to misfortune, and grew through devotion to Your feet alone.
When asked by his father, 'What is the best of all you have learned?'
and the son replied that devotion to You is the supreme [thing], [<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>'s] composure was shattered;
raging at the preceptors and denouncing [<s>Prahlāda</s>'s] nature as innate [and incorrigible],
he contrived means to kill this one who had taken refuge at Your feet.
Though pierced by spears, greatly trampled by the hosts of directional elephants,
bitten by great serpents, and shaken by starvation and poison,
and thrown from the summit of a mountain — alas, O Supreme Self, O All-pervading Lord!
because his self was placed in You, he experienced no suffering whatsoever.
Then his father, filled with apprehension and exceedingly wicked,
at the preceptor's advice, indeed bound [<s>Prahlāda</s>] in that house with the nooses of <s>Varuṇa</s>;
and in the preceptor's absence, [<s>Prahlāda</s>] taught the sons of the demons, his companions,
the truth of devotion to You — the supreme knowledge.
The father, hearing that the entire group of boys was devoted to Your praise,
blind with fury, said to him: 'O disgrace of the family! Who is your strength?'

children.text: balaṃ me vaikuṇṭhastava ca jagatāṃ cāpi sa balaṃ
children.translated_text: '<s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) is my strength and Yours and of the entire universe;
He alone is all the three worlds' — thus the resolute boy declared.
'Ha! Where is He? Where is He? — that <s>Hari</s> who is the Self of the whole world!' —
thus spoke the son of <s>Diti</s>, striking the pillar with his drawn sword.

children.text: ataḥ paścād viṣṇo! na hi vaditumīśo'smi sahasā
children.translated_text: After this, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>! I am unable to speak in haste;
O Compassionate One! O Soul of the universe! O Dweller in <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Be gracious to me! //
As <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> struck the pillar, there arose a sound — shattering the ears,
shaking the hollow of the cosmic egg — a terrible roar of Yours!

children.text: śrutvā yaṃ kila daityarājahṛdaye pūrvaṃ kadāpyaśrutaṃ
children.translated_text: Hearing which — a sound never before heard — in the heart of the demon-king,
a certain trembling arose, and even the Lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>) was shaken from his seat. //
While the demon cast his eyes in all directions, full of great fury, from the pillar

children.text: sambhūtaṃ na mṛgātmakaṃ na manujākāraṃ vapuste vibho! /
children.translated_text: there appeared Your form, O Lord — neither beast nor human in shape.
'What is this? How terrifying! How wondrous!' — as the demon's mind was bewildered,
You manifested in full, with blazing white, terrible mane-hairs bristling and a towering body. //
With eyes rolling, fierce, of the hue of molten gold, with the mane and crest-hair
trembling and pressing against the sky — may this form of Yours prevail!
With a mouth like a vast, yawning cave, a great tongue darting terribly like a sword,
revealing a pair of supremely great tusks, blazing [with fury]. //
With a jaw fearsome with rising folds and wrinkles, with a short but very thick
neck, with cruel rays of claws protruding from hundreds of massive arms, terrible and far-reaching,
with a thunderous roar rivaling dense clouds that reach to the sky, driving away
all hosts of rivals — I bow to that <s>Narasiṃha</s> (Man-Lion) form of Yours! //
'Surely this <s>Viṣṇu</s> — I shall slay him!' — the lord of demons rushed at You, wielding his terrible mace,
and You seized him with Your two mighty arms.
The hero, having slipped free, grasping his sword and shield, exerting himself in wondrous ways,
turning about, again rushed at You — who were poised to devour the worlds — ah! //

children.text: bhrāmyantaṃ ditihādhamaṃ punarapi prodgṛhya dorbhyāṃ javād
children.translated_text: Seizing again that vilest son of <s>Diti</s> as he whirled about, swiftly with both arms,
casting him down upon the thighs at the doorway, and tearing open his chest with Your claws,
ripping apart [his body], with torrents of blood gushing from within — celebrating with a roar
like the annihilator of many worlds, You cried out again and again, 'Drink! Drink!' //
Having quickly cast aside the slain [demon], as Your body rose up, drenched in waves of blood,
and as You devoured the entire host of demons,
the earth reeled, the multitude of oceans trembled, the mountains swayed,
the sky-farers fled upward — all creation, moving and unmoving, alas, was thrown into dire distress. //
With a form terrifying with flesh and entrails, wearing a garland of dreadful intestines,
You in the midst of the assembly, with fury unspent, with an irresistible and dreadful roar —

children.text: abhyetuṃ na śaśaka ko'pi bhuvane dūre sthitā bhīravaḥ
children.translated_text: no one in the world could dare approach You; standing afar in terror,
all — <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) and the others — each offered hymns of praise. //
When Your fury's splendor remained still undiminished, by <s>Brahmā</s>'s command the boy
<s>Prahlāda</s>, bowing at Your feet without fear — You, overwhelmed by the weight of compassion,
became pacified; You placed Your hand upon his head. And then, as he praised You with hymns,
even though he was free from desire, You granted him a boon, and [bestowed] grace upon the world. //
O Lord, who enacted such ferocious deeds! Whose entire glory is clearly sung in
the <s>Śrī Tāpanīya Upaniṣad</s>! Whose form is of supreme purity!
Who is thus unsurpassed by all — who indeed could surpass You?

children.text: prahlādapriya! he marutpurapate! sarvāmayāt pāhi mām //
children.translated_text: O Beloved of <s>Prahlāda</s>! O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Protect me from all disease! //
<s>Indradyumna</s>, the sovereign of the <s>Pāṇḍya</s> kingdom, devoted to You in soul, once upon <s>Candana</s> mountain,
absorbed in Your worship, did not notice even <s>Agastya</s> who had arrived, desirous of hospitality. //

children.text: kumbhodbhūtaḥ saṃbhṛtakrodhabhāraḥ stabdhātmā tvaṃ hastibhūyaṃ bhajeti /
children.translated_text: The Pot-born one (<s>Agastya</s>), filled with accumulated anger, [said:] 'You stubborn one! Become an elephant!' —

children.text: śaptvāthainaṃ pratyagāt so'pi lebhe hastīndratvaṃ tvatsmṛtivyaktidhanyam //
children.translated_text: having thus cursed him, he departed. And that [king] obtained the state of lord of elephants, blessed with the clear memory of You. //
On <s>Trikūṭa</s> mountain, situated in the midst of the Milk Ocean, in the region of the mountain's slopes, this lord of the herd, with his females,

children.text: sarvān jantūnatyavartiṣṭa śaktyā tvadbhaktānāṃ kutra notkarṣalābhaḥ //
children.translated_text: surpassed all creatures by his might — where indeed is the attainment of excellence not [found] among Your devotees? //

children.text: stena sthemnā divyadehatvaśaktyā so'yaṃ khedānaprajānan kadācit /
children.translated_text: With that same strength, with the power of his divine body, this [elephant], not knowing weariness at any time,

children.text: śailaprānte gharmatāntaḥ sarasyāṃ yūthaiḥ sārdhaṃ tvatpraṇunno'bhireme //
children.translated_text: on the mountain slopes, parched by heat, impelled by You, sported in a lake with his herd. //
Meanwhile, <s>Hūhū</s>, a <s>Gandharva</s>, also cursed by the sage <s>Devala</s>, having become a crocodile dwelling in that very water,

children.text: jagrāhainaṃ hastinaṃ pādadeśe śāntyarthaṃ hi śrāntido'si svakānām //
children.translated_text: seized that elephant by the foot — for indeed You bestow rest upon Your own. //

children.text: tvatsevāyā vaibhavād durnirodhaṃ yudhyantaṃ taṃ vatsarāṇāṃ sahasram /
children.translated_text: By the power of his devotion to You, the elephant-hero fought irresistibly for a thousand years;

children.text: prāpte kāle tvatpadaikāgryasiddhyai nakrākrāntaṃ hastivīraṃ vyadhāstvam //
children.translated_text: when the time came for the perfection of his single-pointed focus on Your feet, You ordained that the elephant-hero be seized by the crocodile. //
With devotion and knowledge from former lives made manifest by his distress, worshipping [You] with lotuses lifted by his trunk,
he recited that supreme hymn, practiced in previous births, fixed on the attributeless Self, O Supreme Self! //
Hearing that hymn established in the attributeless [<s>Brahman</s>], when <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and the others withdrew saying 'This is not [addressed to] me,'

children.text: sarvātmā tvaṃ bhūrikāruṇyavegāt tārkṣyārūḍhaḥ prekṣito'bhūḥ purastāt //
children.translated_text: You, the Self of all, propelled by the force of great compassion, mounted upon <s>Garuḍa</s>, appeared before [him]! //

children.text: hastīndraṃ taṃ hastapadmena dhṛtvā cakreṇa tvaṃ nakravaryaṃ vyadārīḥ /
children.translated_text: Seizing that lord of elephants with Your lotus-hand, with Your discus You tore apart the chief of crocodiles;

children.text: gandharve'smin muktaśāpe sa hastī tvatsārūpyaṃ prāpya dedīpyate sma //
children.translated_text: when this <s>Gandharva</s> was freed from the curse, that elephant, having attained <s>sārūpya</s> (likeness of form with You), shone resplendently. //

children.text: etad vṛttaṃ tvāṃ ca māṃ ca prage yo gāyet so'yaṃ bhūyase śreyase syāt /
children.translated_text: 'Whoever sings at dawn of this event, of You and of me — he shall attain the greatest good' —

children.text: ityuktvainaṃ tena sārdhaṃ gatastvaṃ dhiṣṇyaṃ viṣṇo! pāhi vātālayeśa! //
children.translated_text: having thus spoken, You went with him to Your abode, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>! O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, protect me! //

children.text: durvāsāḥ suravanitāptadivyamālyaṃ śakrāya svayamupadāya tatra bhūjaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Durvāsas</s>, having given <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) a divine garland obtained from a celestial nymph — when his elephant trod upon it, he cursed <s>Śakra</s>;
what forbearance can be expected of those born from portions of deities other than You? //
When, by the curse, the lord of the gods aged visibly, and the gods too, conquered by the demons, lost their splendor,

children.text: śarvādyāḥ kamalajametya sarvadevā nirvāṇaprabhava! samaṃ bhavantamāpuḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) and the others, approaching the Lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>), together with all the gods, came to You, O Source of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>! //

children.text: brahmādyairnutamahimā ciraṃ tadānīṃ prāduḥṣan varada! puraḥ pareṇa dhāmnā /
children.translated_text: Your glory being praised by <s>Brahmā</s> and the others for a long time, You then manifested before them, O Boon-granter! with supreme radiance,

children.text: he devā! ditijakulairvidhāya sandhiṃ pīyūṣaṃ parimathateti paryaśāstvam //
children.translated_text: [and said:] 'O gods! Making a truce with the clan of <s>Daityas</s>, churn [the ocean] for the nectar!' — thus You instructed. //

children.text: sandhānaṃ kṛtavati dānavaiḥ suraudhe manthānaṃ nayati madena mandarādrim /
children.translated_text: When the gods made an alliance with the <s>Dānavas</s> (demons), and while the host of gods was transporting Mount <s>Mandara</s> as the churning rod with great effort,

children.text: bhraṣṭe'smin badaramivodvahan khagendre sadystvaṃ vinihitavān payaḥ payodhau //
children.translated_text: when it fell, You, bearing it as easily as a berry upon <s>Garuḍa</s>, instantly placed it in the Milk Ocean. //

children.text: ādhāya drutamatha vāsukiṃ varatrāṃ pāthodhau vinihitasarvabījajāle /
children.translated_text: Then, quickly placing <s>Vāsuki</s> (the serpent-king) as the rope, in the ocean in which all the seeds [of creation] had been deposited,

children.text: prārabdhe mathanavidhau surāsuraistairvyājāt tvaṃ bhujagamukhe'karoḥ surārīn //
children.translated_text: when the churning commenced by gods and demons, by a stratagem You placed the enemies of the gods at the serpent's mouth. //

children.text: kṣubdhādrau kṣubhitajalodare tadānīṃ dugdhābdhau gurutarabhārato nimagne /
children.translated_text: When the agitated mountain was submerged in the churning waters of the Milk Ocean, sinking under its extreme weight,

children.text: deveṣu vyathitatameṣu tatpriyaiṣī prāṇaiṣīḥ kamaṭhatanuṃ kaṭhorapṛṣṭhām //
children.translated_text: and the gods were most distressed — You, desiring their welfare, assumed the body of a tortoise (<s>Kūrma</s>) with a hard back. //
O <s>Viṣṇu</s>! With a shell harder than adamant, extending a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in breadth,

children.text: ambhodheḥ kuharagatena varṣmaṇā tvaṃ nirmagnaṃ kṣitidharanāthamunninetha //
children.translated_text: and with a body filling the abyss of the ocean, You raised up the sunken lord of mountains. //

children.text: unmagne jhaṭiti tadā dharādharendre nirmethurdṛḍhamiha sammadena sarve /
children.translated_text: When the lord of mountains suddenly emerged, all churned with vigor and great delight;
and entering both groups [of gods and demons] through the serpent-king, dispelling their exhaustion, You invigorated them. //
As the great mountain spun with unbridled velocity, You, with one steady lotus-hand placed upon it [to stabilize it] —
in that state of unwavering [support], <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and the others, delighted, showered You with flowers in their joy. //

children.text: daityaudhe bhujagamukhānilena tapte tenaiva tridaśakule'pi kiñcidārte /
children.translated_text: When the host of demons was scorched by the fiery breath from the serpent's mouths, and the host of gods too was somewhat afflicted by it,

children.text: kāruṇyāt tava kila deva! vārivāhāḥ prāvarṣannamaragaṇān na daityasaṅghān //
children.translated_text: out of compassion, O Lord! the rain clouds rained upon the divine host alone, not upon the demon-hordes. //
From the ocean there first emerged the <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison, blazing with flickering flames;
<s>Śiva</s>, having quelled the dismay of the gods with comforting words of praise, drank that [poison] for Your sake. //
As the gods and demons churned, <s>Surabhi</s> (the wish-granting cow) was born — You assigned her to the sages, O Lord of the three realms!
Then came the horse-jewel, then the elephant-jewel, the wish-granting tree, and the <s>Apsarases</s> — these [went] to the gods. //

children.text: jagadīśa! bhavatparā tadānīṃ kamanīyā kamalā babhūva devī /
children.translated_text: O Lord of the world! At that time, devoted to You, the beautiful Goddess <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) appeared,

children.text: amalāmavalokya yāṃ vilokaḥ sakalo'pi spṛhayāmbabhūva lokaḥ //
children.translated_text: and beholding her, spotless, the entire world — all the people — was filled with longing. //

children.text: tvayi dattahṛdde tadaiva devyai tridaśendro maṇipīṭhikāṃ vyatārīt /
children.translated_text: When her heart was given to You, <s>Indra</s> offered a jeweled throne to the Goddess;
the sages, with all the sacred substances brought for the anointing, consecrated her with <s>Vedic</s> hymns. //
Her vine-like body adorned by Your gentle side-glances following the flow of the anointing waters,
the gods and others adorned her with jeweled earrings, a yellow garment, necklaces, and the like. //
Bearing a bridal garland humming with clinging bees, adorning the pitcher-like [fullness of her] breasts,
her steps jingling sweetly, she approached You with bashful, playful grace. //
Examining all the gods — <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the rest — though possessed of virtues, yet not free from the slightest faults,

children.text: avamṛśya sadaiva sarvaramye nihitā tvayyanayāpi divyamālā //
children.translated_text: she placed her divine garland upon You alone, who are ever all-charming — and so did she bestow herself. //
With Your chest You eagerly embraced her — the mother of the worlds, of undivided devotion;
by the prosperity of her glance playing upon Your chest, the universe was nourished. //

children.text: atimohanavibhramā tadānīṃ madayantī khalu vāruṇī nirāgāt /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vāruṇī</s> (the goddess of wine), of exceedingly bewitching allure, emerged, intoxicating [all];
since she belongs to the realm of <s>tamas</s> (darkness), You gave her, with great honor, to the great demons. //
Then You, beautiful as a young rain-cloud, rose from the ocean as <s>Dhanvantari</s>,

children.text: amṛtaṃ kalaśe vahan karābhyāmakhilārtiṃ hara mārutālayeśa! //
children.translated_text: carrying the nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) in a vessel in Your hands — remove all suffering, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! //
As You emerged, when the demons snatched the nectar from Your hands,
You reassured the helpless gods,
and concealed [the nectar], O Lord! By Your own power,
the demons, ready for battle with their fellows, fell into quarrels. //
Then You assumed a dark-complexioned, youthful female form
with high, swelling breasts;
and all of them, abandoning the quarrel over the nectar-pot,
overcome by desire, thronged around the pitcher of Your bosom. //
'Who are you, O doe-eyed one? Distribute this nectar among us!' —
thus these [demons], overpowered by rising passion, beseeched [You].
'How can you trust me? I am a wanton woman, O <s>Daityas</s>!' —
thus speaking, You still made them perfectly trusting. //
When they, in delight, handed over the nectar-vessel — You, that [enchanting woman],
saying 'Bear with my mischief,'
having seated gods and demons in separate rows,
distributed that nectar with playful, graceful movements. //
'She is partial to us' — thus, while those demons
sat quietly, You completed [the distribution of] nectar to the gods.
Then You, subject to Your devotees, assuming Your true form,
cut down <s>Svarbhānu</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>) who had half-drunk the nectar. //
Having given those others the appropriate fruit of [attempting to] steal the nectar from You,

children.text: dattvā gate tvayi suraiḥ khalu te vyagṛhṇan /
children.translated_text: when You departed, the gods surely seized them.
Then, in the terrible battle that ensued, when the divine host was bewildered
by <s>Bali</s>'s demonic <s>māyā</s> (illusion) — You appeared here. //
You struck down <s>Kālanemi</s> and <s>Māli</s> and their followers,
and <s>Śakra</s> slew <s>Bali</s>, <s>Jambha</s>, and <s>Vala</s> together with the <s>Pākas</s>.
When <s>Namuci</s>, difficult to slay whether wet or dry, was severed
with foam — by the counsel of <s>Nārada</s> — You ended that battle. //
Hearing of that female form You had assumed to beguile the demons,
<s>Maheśvara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), curious to behold it,

children.text: bhūtaiḥ samaṃ girijayā ca gataḥ padaṃ te
children.translated_text: came with his <s>bhūtas</s> (attendants) and <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) to Your abode;
having praised [You], he expressed his desire — and then You vanished. //
In the pleasure-garden, [You appeared], enchantingly beautiful, with eyes rolling playfully
from the sport of ball-throwing,
and beholding You with garment slipping — by the force of <s>Manobhū</s> (the Love God),
He, the enemy of <s>Anaṅga</s> (<s>Śiva</s>, destroyer of Kāma), O Lord! embraced You. //
When [the form] again fled, the Lord (<s>Śiva</s>), pursuing [it], his loss of seminal energy [causing]
the blossoming of ultimate spiritual insight,
honored by You, spoke of Your greatness to the Goddess (<s>Pārvatī</s>) —
such as You are, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, protect me! //
Although <s>Bali</s>, the great soul, was slain by <s>Śakra</s> in battle,
his body was revived by <s>Śukra</s> (the preceptor of the demons), and his ardor increased through sacrificial rites.
Valiant, [he made] the three worlds — wherein the gods cowered in fear — subject to his will,
unafraid of Your discus and other [weapons]. //
<s>Aditi</s>, distressed at seeing her sons' suffering,
took refuge in her husband <s>Kaśyapa</s>
that worship of You, known as the <s>Payovrata</s> (milk-vow), was performed —
she observed it for twelve days, filled with devotion to You.
At its conclusion, when her mind was absorbed in You,
You appeared of Your own accord, dark-complexioned and four-armed.
To her as she bowed, [You said] 'I shall become your son;
but my vision must be kept secret' — thus speaking, You departed.
When <s>Kaśyapa</s> was engaged in <s>tapas</s> (austerity), You then
entered the womb of <s>Aditi</s>, praised by <s>Brahmā</s> (the Creator).
She gave birth to You, who displayed a resplendent divine Vaiṣṇava form,
on the sacred day of the twelfth of <s>Śravaṇa</s>.
Upon that holy hermitage, showered with rains of flowers,
while the hosts of gods were filled with joy and sounded their instruments,
with folded hands, [crying] 'Victory! Victory!' — to Your parents, You,
in that very instant, assumed the form of a most precocious <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student).
Thereupon, invested [with the sacred thread] by <s>Prajāpati</s> and others, and worshipped
with the <s>mauñjī</s> (girdle), staff, deerskin, rosary, and the like,
blazing in form, O Lord, having performed the fire-rites,
You set forth toward the abode of <s>Bali</s>, who was performing the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice).
As if revealing beforehand through Your body the magnitude appropriate to Your future greatness,
You went, making the earth tremble;
carrying the parasol as if to ward off the heat of Your adversary,
and the staff as if to subdue the hosts of <s>Dānavas</s>.
When You arrived at that <s>Aśvamedha</s> sacrificial hall on the northern bank
of the <s>Narmadā</s>, those whose eyes were arrested by Your radiance
wondered: 'Is this the sun? Or fire? Or the yogi <s>Sanatkumāra</s>?
Who is this?' — thus doubted <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) and others.
Swiftly brought forward by the <s>Bhṛgus</s> who were overwhelmed by Your splendor,
the <s>asura</s> (<s>Bali</s>), his limbs covered with horripilation,
approached You with devotion, the meritorious one, washed Your feet,
and bore that water — a <s>tīrtha</s> (holy water) of <s>tīrthas</s> — upon his head.
By virtue of being born in the lineage of <s>Prahlāda</s>, through sacrifices and trust in <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
even this son of <s>Diti</s> obtained this [privilege] —
that the water from Your feet, which is cherished upon the head of <s>Giriśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) —
may You, O Lord, O dweller of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, protect [me]!
With joy, the <s>Daitya</s>, from beholding the radiance of Your form, in every way
worshipping You, O Unconquered One, making an <s>añjali</s> (gesture of reverence), spoke:

children.text: mattaḥ kiṃ te samabhilaṣitaṃ viprasūno! vada tvaṃ
children.translated_text: 'What do you desire from me, O son of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>? Tell me!

children.text: vittaṃ bhaktaṃ bhavanamavanīṃ vāpi sarvaṃ pradāsye //
children.translated_text: Wealth, food, a dwelling, land — I shall give you everything.'
Hearing <s>Bali</s>'s generous words, though filled with compassion,
yet intending to subdue his pride, praising the <s>Daitya</s> lineage,
You asked for land measured by three steps of Your feet —

children.text: sarvaṃ dehīti tu nigadite kasya hāsyaṃ na vā syāt //
children.translated_text: when he said 'Give everything,' who would not have laughed?

children.text: viśveśaṃ māṃ tripadamiha kiṃ yācase bāliśastvaṃ
children.translated_text: 'You are foolish! Why do you ask me, the lord of the universe, for only three steps?

children.text: sarvāṃ bhūmiṃ vṛṇu kimamunetyālapat tvāṃ sa dṛpyan /
children.translated_text: Ask for all the land — what use is so little?' — thus he spoke to You, puffed up with pride.
Because of that very pride, being unable to fulfill [the promise of] three steps, he faced mocking words
and bondage — though undeserving — for the sake of deep pacification.

children.text: pādatrayyā yadi na mudito viṣṭapairnāpi tuṣye-
children.translated_text: 'If I am not satisfied with three steps, I would not be content even with all the worlds' —
when You spoke thus, O Boon-granter, and he was ready to give the water [of gift],
the preceptor of the <s>Daityas</s> (<s>Śukrācārya</s>), prompted by You who wished to test [<s>Bali</s>],
plainly declared: 'Do not give! Do not give! This is <s>Hari</s>!'

children.text: yācatyevaṃ yadi sa bhagavān pūrṇakāmo'smi so'haṃ
children.translated_text: 'If he is the Lord Himself who asks thus, then I am fulfilled in my desires;
I shall certainly give' — speaking thus firmly, the <s>Daitya</s>, though cursed by <s>Kāvya</s> (<s>Śukra</s>),
with his beloved <s>Vindhyāvalī</s> offering the foot-washing water to You —

children.text: citraṃ citraṃ sakalamapi sa prārpayat toyapūrvam //
children.translated_text: wonderful, wonderful! — he offered You everything, preceded by the water.
Without doubt, when the lord of <s>Diti</s>'s clan was making that complete offering to You,
the sages along with the gods released a shower of flowers.

children.text: divyaṃ rūpaṃ tava ca tadidaṃ paśyatāṃ viśvabhājām-
children.translated_text: And that divine form of Yours, beheld by all the beings of the universe,
grew higher and higher, making the entire cosmic egg seem small.
The lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>, seeing Your toe reach his own abode,
washed it with the water from his <s>kuṇḍī</s> (water pot); that water purified all the worlds.
With the overflow of joy, in that great celebration, among the sky-dwellers,
<s>Jāmbavān</s>, full of devotion, beating a drum, traversed the world.
Then the <s>Daityas</s>, without their lord's permission, having begun to fight,
met with defeat at the hands of Your followers accompanied by the gods.

children.text: kālātmāyaṃ vasati purato yadvaśāt prāg jitāḥ smaḥ
children.translated_text: 'This one is Time itself, standing before us; by his power we were defeated before;

children.text: kiṃ vo yuddhairiti baligirā te'tha pātālamāpuḥ //
children.translated_text: what use are your battles?' — by <s>Bali</s>'s words, they then went to <s>Pātāla</s>.
To the <s>Daitya</s>, bound in fetters by <s>Garuḍa</s> (the king of birds), You spoke loudly:

children.text: stārtīyīkaṃ diśa mama padaṃ kiṃ na viśveśvaro'si /
children.translated_text: 'Give Me the third step! Am I not the Lord of the universe?'
'Place Your foot upon my head, O Lord' — thus he spoke without trembling;
and <s>Prahlāda</s> himself, having come there, honoring him, praised You.
'All this was done for the crushing of your pride, O <s>Daitya</s>! You are perfected by your merits;
a world shall be yours; you shall conquer the three heavens and become the next <s>Indra</s>.',

children.text: matsāyujyaṃ bhaja ca punarityanvagṛhṇā baliṃ taṃ
children.translated_text: 'And attain union with Me hereafter' — thus You blessed that <s>Bali</s>.
The best of sacrifices, continued by the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — protect [me], O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>!
Formerly, when the great <s>asura</s> <s>Hayagrīva</s>, at an unexpected dissolution at the end of the sixth <s>Manvantara</s>,
stole the Vedas from the mouth of <s>Brahmā</s> as he was about to fall asleep, You assumed the form of a fish.
When <s>Satyavrata</s>, the ruler of the <s>Dramiḍa</s> (Dravidian) land, was performing <s>tarpaṇa</s> (water oblation)
in the river water, You appeared in his cupped hands — a tiny shining fish.

children.text: kṣiptaṃ jale tvāṃ cakitaṃ vilokya ninye'nbupātraṇa muniḥ svageham /
children.translated_text: Seeing You frightened when cast into the water, the sage carried You home in a water vessel;

children.text: svalpairahobhiḥ kalaśīṃ ca kūpaṃ vāpīṃ saraścānaśiṣe vibho! tvam //
children.translated_text: within a few days, O Lord, You outgrew the pot, then the well, then the tank, and then the lake.
By the power of <s>yoga</s>, at Your own command, the sage then took You to the ocean;
when asked by him, who wished to witness the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic dissolution), You departed saying: 'Wait for seven days.'
When the day foretold by You arrived, and the surface of the earth was flooded with torrents of rain,
the chief sage, along with the seven <s>ṛṣis</s>, tossing about in the boundless waters, sought refuge in You.
Having obtained the vessel in the form of the Earth, made obedient to Your command,
they boarded it; and when they trembled and shook, You appeared again from the ocean, magnificent.
Beholding Your form, a fish of a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in length,

children.text: nirīkṣya tuṣṭā munayastvaduktyā tvattuṅgaśṛṅge taraṇiṃ babandhuḥ //
children.translated_text: blazing with supreme radiance, the sages, delighted, by Your instruction tied the vessel to Your lofty horn.
Drawing the ship bearing the assembly of sages, showing them the divisions of the entire universe,

children.text: saṃstūyamāno nṛvareṇa tena jṅānaṃ paraṃ copadiśannacārīḥ //
children.translated_text: praised by that king of men (<s>Satyavrata</s>), You imparted to him the supreme knowledge.

children.text: kalpāvadhau sapta munīn purovat prastāpya satyavratabhūmipaṃ tam /
children.translated_text: At the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, having restored the seven sages as before and appointed that King <s>Satyavrata</s>
as the <s>Manu</s> named <s>Vaivasvata</s>, You rushed against <s>Hayagrīva</s> in fury.

children.text: svatuṅgaśṛṅgakṣatavakṣasaṃ taṃ nipātya daityaṃ nigamān gṛhītvā /
children.translated_text: Striking down that <s>Daitya</s>, whose chest was pierced by Your lofty horn, seizing the Vedas,
and giving them to <s>Brahmā</s>, who was delighted at heart — O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, protect [me]!
In the lineage of the <s>Manu</s> named <s>Vaivasvata</s>, from his son <s>Nābhāga</s>, was born
<s>Ambarīṣa</s>, the son of the king named <s>Nābhāga</s>;
though he was the beloved lord of the earth surrounded by the seven oceans, he found delight
among Your devotees and in You, his mind always immersed [in You].
As he performed everything for Your pleasure,
by devotion alone, O God, You bestowed Your grace upon him before long,
so that even without his asking, for his protection,
You extended Your discus (<s>Sudarśana</s>) of a thousand spokes.
He maintained the <s>Dvādaśī-vrata</s> (twelfth-day vow) for Your worship
for a year, in the <s>Madhuvana</s> (grove) near the <s>Yamunā</s>;
together with his gentle-minded wife, spreading a great
worship, distributing sixty million cattle to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Then, on the day of breaking the fast, at the conclusion of Your worship,
the sage <s>Durvāsas</s> arrived at his abode.
Invited by the king to dine, that sage, inclined to others' afflictions,
went slowly to the <s>Yamunā</s>, intending to perform his observances.
The king, distressed that the hour for breaking the fast was passing,
broke the fast with water alone, being devoted to You.
When the sage returned and, perceiving this through divine sight,
furious, with his matted locks bristling in anger, he conjured forth a <s>Kṛtyā</s> (destructive spirit).
Beholding that <s>Kṛtyā</s>, sword in hand, burning the world,
approaching him, the king did not move a step.
Your <s>Sudarśana</s> (discus), seeing the threat to Your devotee,
pursued the sage [as if he were] a moth before the fire of the <s>Kṛtyā</s>.
Running through all the worlds in fear, seeing
Your discus everywhere, he went to <s>Brahmā</s>;
'Who can transgress the wheel of Time?' — thus rejected,
he went to <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), who also simply bowed to You.
Coming again to Your abode, to the bowing sage
You said: 'I am indeed the servant of My devotees, O sage!
Knowledge and austerity are honored only when accompanied by humility;
go, seek the refuge of <s>Ambarīṣa</s> himself!' O Infinite One!
Thereupon, having approached, the sage grasped the king's feet,
and the king, withdrawing, recalled Your weapon.
When the discus departed, the sage bestowed upon him all blessings,
praising Your devotion and [declaring] that even when an offense is committed, there is compassion.
The king, having awaited the sage for one full year, subsisting on grain alone,
having hospitably fed that <s>ṛṣi</s> and sent him off pleased,

children.text: bhuktvā svayaṃ tvayi tato'pi dṛḍhaṃ rato'bhūt
children.translated_text: having himself eaten, became thereafter even more firmly devoted to You

children.text: sāyujyamāpa ca sa māṃ pavaneśa! pāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: and attained <s>sāyujya</s> (complete union [with You]). May he, O Lord of the Wind's abode, protect me!
Entreated by the gods for the destruction of ten-headed [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>], at [the site of] <s>Ṛśyaśṛṅga</s> in <s>Kosala</s>,
when King <s>Daśaratha</s>, having performed the <s>Putrīyā Iṣṭi</s> (sacrifice for sons), offered the supreme <s>pāyasa</s> (rice pudding),

children.text: tadbhuktyā tatpurandhrīṣvapi tisṛṣu samaṃ jātagarbhāsu jāto
children.translated_text: by the partaking of that [pudding] by his three queens, all of whom became pregnant, You were born
as <s>Rāma</s>, along with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and also <s>Bharata</s>, and the one named <s>Śatrughna</s>.
Bearing a bow, accompanying the sage <s>Kauśika</s> (<s>Viśvāmitra</s>) to protect his supreme sacrifice,
You went at Your father's word, accompanied by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, Your journey's fatigue dispelled by the stories told by the sage.

children.text: n ṇāṃ trāṇāya bāṇairmunivacanabalāt tāṭakāṃ pāṭayitvā
children.translated_text: For the protection of the sages, by the power of the sage's word, slaying <s>Tāṭakā</s> with arrows,
and receiving from him the arsenal of divine weapons, You went, O God, to the sage's grove called <s>Siddhāśrama</s>.
Driving away <s>Mārīca</s>, striking down other <s>rākṣasas</s> at the head of the sacrifice with arrows,

children.text: kalyāṃ kurvannahalyāṃ pathi padarajasā prāpya vaidehageham /
children.translated_text: purifying <s>Ahalyā</s> on the way with the dust of Your feet, reaching the palace of the king of <s>Videha</s>,
breaking the bow of <s>Śiva</s> (the crescent-crested one), and winning the daughter of the Earth — <s>Sītā</s>, who is <s>Indirā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) herself —

children.text: rāyaṃ prātiṣṭhathāstvaṃ tribhirapi ca samaṃ bhrātṛvīraiḥ sadāraiḥ //
children.translated_text: You returned home with Your three brother-heroes and their brides.
When the blind-with-rage jewel of the <s>Bhṛgu</s> lineage (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) confronted You, You transferred his power to Yourself;

children.text: yāte yāto'syayodhyāṃ sukhamiha nivasan kāntayā kāntamūrte! /
children.translated_text: when he departed, You went to <s>Ayodhyā</s> and lived happily there with Your beloved, O one of beautiful form!
Then one day, when <s>Śatrughna</s> had gone along with <s>Bharata</s> to the maternal uncle's residence,
the coronation ordered by Your father was obstructed by the daughter of the king of <s>Kekaya</s> (<s>Kaikeyī</s>).
At Your father's word, wishing to go to the forest, accompanied by Your younger brother's wife (<s>Sītā</s>) and bearing a bow,
having turned back the citizens on the way, reaching the abode of <s>Guha</s>, wearing matted locks and bark garments,
crossing the <s>Gaṅgā</s> by boat, on the path bowing to <s>Bharadvāja</s>,
and at his word, You dwelt most happily on the great mountain <s>Citrakūṭa</s>.

children.text: śrutvā putrārtikhinnaṃ khalu bharatamukhāt svargayātaṃ svatātaṃ
children.translated_text: Having learned from <s>Bharata</s>'s mouth that Your father, grieving for his son, had departed to heaven,

children.text: tapto dattvāmbu tasmai nidadhitha bharate pādukāṃ medinīṃ ca /
children.translated_text: stricken with sorrow, having offered water to him, You entrusted to <s>Bharata</s> Your sandals and the [rule of the] earth.

children.text: atriṃ natvātha gatvā vanamativipulāṃ daṇḍakāṃ caṇḍakāyaṃ
children.translated_text: Bowing to <s>Atri</s>, and then going to the vast <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, slaying

children.text: hatvā daityaṃ virādhaṃ sugatimakalayaścāru bhoḥ! śārabhaṅgīm //
children.translated_text: the fierce-bodied <s>Daitya</s> <s>Virādha</s> and granting him liberation — and beautifully [visiting] <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>!
Bowing to <s>Agastya</s>, who gifted You a complete set of arrows and quiver, to the ascetics

children.text: pratyaśrauṣīḥ priyaiṣī tadanu ca muninā vaiṣṇave divyacāpe /
children.translated_text: You gave Your promise of protection; then, when the sage presented You with the divine Vaiṣṇava bow

children.text: brahmāstre cāpi datte pathi pitṛsuhṛdaṃ dīkṣya jaṭāyuṃ
children.translated_text: and the <s>Brahmāstra</s> as well, and on the way befriending <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, Your father's friend,

children.text: modād godātaṭānte pariramasi purā pañcavatyāṃ vadhūṭyā //
children.translated_text: You sported with joy on the banks of the <s>Godāvarī</s> at <s>Pañcavaṭī</s> with Your bride.
When <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> arrived and, unable to bear her passion for You, the mountain of love, made her advances,

children.text: tāṃ saumitrau visṛjya prabalatamaruṣā tena nirlunanāsām /
children.translated_text: You sent her to <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>), who in fierce rage cut off her nose;

children.text: dṛṣṭvaināṃ ruṣṭacittaṃ kharamabhipatitaṃ duṣaṇaṃ ca trimūrdhaṃ
children.translated_text: seeing her [thus], the enraged <s>Khara</s> who attacked, along with <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> and the three-headed <s>Triśiras</s>,
You slew along with more than fourteen thousand <s>rākṣasas</s> in an instant, without breaking a sweat.
By the report from his sister, the agitated ten-faced (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) dispatched <s>Mārīca</s> in the form of a magical deer;
coveted by the lotus-eyed one (<s>Sītā</s>), You pursued it and killed it with a blow of an arrow.
drawn out by the cry of <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> seized Your consort, Your divine brother's wife;
though pained, You felt a certain inner joy at having found the means for his destruction.
Searching further for Your slender wife, the ten-faced one having carried her off — when <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, declaring 'He stole Your wife, but he shall die by me,'

children.text: tyuktvā yāte jaṭāyau divamatha suhṛdaḥ prātanoḥ pretakāryam /
children.translated_text: departed to heaven, You then performed the funeral rites for that friend.

children.text: gṛhṇānaṃ taṃ kabandhaṃ jaghanitha śabarīṃ prekṣya pampātaṭe tvaṃ
children.translated_text: You slew <s>Kabandha</s> as he seized You; then, seeing <s>Śabarī</s>, on the bank of <s>Pampā</s>,
You reached the Son of the Wind (<s>Hanumān</s>), with a greatly gladdened heart — protect me, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>!
Then, brought into friendship with <s>Sugrīva</s>, having hurled the body of <s>Dundubhi</s> far

children.text: kṣiptvāṅguṣṭhena bhūyo lulavitha yugapat patriṇā sapta sālān /
children.translated_text: with Your thumb, You then pierced seven <s>sāla</s> trees simultaneously with a single arrow.
Having killed <s>Vālin</s>, of matchless strength and intent on slaying <s>Sugrīva</s>, by stratagem,
You spent the rainy season at the edge of the <s>Mataṅga</s> hermitage, restless with the pain of separation.
When <s>Sugrīva</s>, admonished by Your brother, approached fearfully, and the assembled armies
of monkeys were deployed in all directions, swiftly bowing to search for Your beloved —
You joyfully placed the message and the signet ring in the hand of the Son of the Wind;

children.text: mārge mārge mamārge kapibhirapi tadī tvatpriyā saprayāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: in every path, the monkeys searched with great effort for Your beloved.
By the words of <s>Sampāti</s>, whose swift wings grew upon hearing news of You,
having crossed the ocean, inside the city, beholding <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter and giving the ring,
destroying the garden, fierce in battle when annihilating the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, enduring captivity, seeing the ten-faced one,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā pluṣṭvā ca laṅkāṃ jhaṭiti sa hanumān mauliratnaṃ dadau te //
children.translated_text: and then burning <s>Laṅkā</s>, that <s>Hanumān</s> swiftly brought you the crest-jewel.
You, with the powerful armies of monkeys led by <s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Aṅgada</s>,
having conquered the earth with Your circle of forces, approached the other shore of the ocean, favored by the brother of the lord of the night-stalkers (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>).
Hearing in private from him the intelligence about the enemy, angered that Your petition was treated as worthless,
You obtained a passage through the middle of the ocean by the blazing power of the <s>Āgneyāstra</s> (fire-weapon), the ocean trembling and speaking humbly.
Having built a bridge with mountain-masses brought by the monkeys from the shores of the ocean, You marched forth,
and Your armies crushed the <s>Rākṣasas</s> with fangs, claws, mountain-peaks, rocks, and <s>sāla</s>-tree weapons.

children.text: vyākurvan sanujastvaṃ samarabhuvi paraṃ vikramaṃ śakrajetrā
children.translated_text: You and Your brother displayed supreme valor on the battlefield, when the conqueror of <s>Indra</s>
swiftly bound You with the <s>Nāgāstra</s> (serpent-weapon), and You were freed by <s>Garuḍa</s> and the winds of the lord of birds.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, his life failing from the blow of the <s>Śakti</s> weapon, was revived by smelling the herb-mountain
brought by the Son of the Wind, and he slew <s>Meghanāda</s> (<s>Indrajit</s>), who prided himself on his stratagems.
When the <s>māyā</s>-attacks were confounding, with the <s>Stambhana</s> (paralyzing weapon) overcome by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>'s advice, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>
arrived, shaking the earth's surface, devouring entire armies — You destroyed him.
Wielding the chariot and armor sent by <s>Indra</s>, fighting <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,
shattering his streaming [heads] with the <s>Brahmāstra</s>, and receiving <s>Sītā</s> purified by fire —
O Lord! with the monkey armies, their battle-dead revived by the showers of the <s>Śreṇī</s> tree, unscathed,

children.text: laṅkābhartrā ca sākaṃ nijanagaramagāḥ sapriyaḥ puṣpakeṇa //
children.translated_text: together with the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> (<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>), You returned to Your own city with Your beloved in the <s>Puṣpaka</s> (flying chariot).
Pleased by divine consecrations, You delighted with <s>Maithilī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) for more than ten thousand years;

children.text: maithilyāṃ pāpavācā śiva śiva kila tāṃ garbhiṇīmabhyahāsīḥ /
children.translated_text: alas, alas, because of slanderous talk, You abandoned her even while she was pregnant!
Having <s>Śatrughna</s> slay the demon <s>Lavaṇa</s>, You also killed the <s>Śūdra</s> ascetic;

children.text: tāvad vālmīkigehe kṛtavasatirupāsūta sīta sutau te //
children.translated_text: meanwhile <s>Sītā</s>, dwelling in <s>Vālmīki</s>'s hermitage, gave birth to Your two sons.
When the sweet composition of <s>Vālmīki</s>, sung by Your sons, was recited at the sacrificial enclosure by his command,

children.text: sītāṃ tvayyāsukāme kṣitimaviśadasau tvaṃ ca kālārthito'bhūḥ /
children.translated_text: and <s>Sītā</s>, when You desired her back, entered the earth — and You too were summoned by Time.
The slaying of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> being the pretext, You Yourself, together with all Your servants drowned in the <s>Sarayū</s>,

children.text: sākaṃ nākaṃ prayāto nijapadamagamo deva! vaikuṇṭhamādyam //
children.translated_text: went to heaven, and attained Your own state — O Lord, the primal <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>!
This mortal incarnation of Yours was surely for the instruction of mortals:
that even the anguish of separation and the abandonment of the innocent may come about through excessive attachment to righteousness and desire.

children.text: no cet svātmānubhūteḥ kvanu tava manaso vikriyā cakrapāṇe!
children.translated_text: Otherwise, how could there be any perturbation of mind for You, who are Self-experience itself, O Discus-Wielder!

children.text: sa tvaṃ sattvaikamūrte! pavanapurapate! vyādhunu vyādhitāpān //
children.translated_text: O You whose sole form is pure <s>sattva</s>! O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Shake off the afflictions of disease!

children.text: atreḥ putratayā purā tvamanasūyāyāṃ hi dattābhidho
children.translated_text: In ancient times, born as <s>Atri</s>'s son, named <s>Datta</s> (<s>Dattātreya</s>),
from <s>Anasūyā</s>, You wandered freely, carefree, with disciples rendered idle and slothful, with Your beloved,
seen by <s>Kārtavīryārjuna</s>, the most devoted king of the <s>Haihaya</s> dynasty, to whom You granted boons

children.text: naṣṭaiśvaryamukhān pradāya daditha svenaiva cānte vadham //
children.translated_text: including lost sovereignty — and You also granted him his own death at Your hands in the end.
Then, to make true the boon given to <s>Arjuna</s>, and because all the royal clans

children.text: brahmadveṣi tadākhilaṃ nṛpakulaṃ hantuṃ ca bhūmerbharam /
children.translated_text: bowed only to his power and were hostile to <s>Brahmins</s>, and to relieve the Earth's burden —

children.text: sañjāto jamadagnito bhṛgukule tvaṃ reṇukāyāṃ hare!
children.translated_text: You were born in the <s>Bhṛgu</s> lineage from <s>Jamadagni</s> and <s>Reṇukā</s>, O <s>Hari</s>!
Named <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>), the youngest among their sons, You brought delight to Your parents.
Having mastered the entire collection of <s>Vedas</s> by age fourteen, when the <s>Gandharva</s> king

children.text: gāsatāṃ kila mātaraṃ prati pituḥ krodhākulasyājñayā /
children.translated_text: committed a slight offense against Your mother, at the command of Your wrathful father,
with brothers who obeyed the father's command, You cut off her head; then, from Your pacified father,

children.text: teṣāṃ jīvanayogamāpitha varaṃ mātā ca te'dād varam //
children.translated_text: You obtained the boon of restoring their lives, and Your mother also gave You a boon.
Your father, for Your mother's joy, having brought the celestial cow from <s>Indra</s>'s abode, then from his own hermitage
You departed, and at <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s word, on the <s>Himālaya</s>, You worshipped the Lord of <s>Gaurī</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
obtaining from him the battle-axe (<s>paraśu</s>) and great weapons and missiles for slaying the demons as he instructed,
You gained the sage <s>Akṛtavraṇa</s> as a friend and returned to Your hermitage.
<s>Kārtavīryārjuna</s>, coming in the course of a hunt, was honored by Your father
with splendid hospitality obtained from the wish-fulfilling cow; but upon returning home, by the advice of a wicked minister,

children.text: gāṃ kretuṃ sacivaṃ nyayuṅkta kudhiyā tenāpi rundhanmuni-
children.translated_text: he foolishly sent a servant to seize the cow; and that servant, obstructing the sage
and provoking his wrath, was slain along with his army by the enraged cow — and the calf was taken.
Then, Your anger roused by the words of Your father who was revived by <s>Śukra</s>, together with Your friend,
bearing the bow, battle-axe, and arrows bestowed by the meditated-upon <s>Mahodara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
mounting a chariot complete with horses and charioteer, You entered <s>Māhiṣmatī</s> city,
and when the king did not return the calf despite Your words, You commenced battle.
With ten thousand sons, seventeen <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> armies, great generals,
and hosts of numerous allies, the battle raged fiercely;
instantly, Your battle-axe and arrows shattered all the remaining armies;
the surviving sons, terrified and routed, the <s>Haihaya</s> king himself rushed at You.
Playfully holding back the waters of the <s>Narmadā</s>, dispelling the pride of the Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>,
repelling the many weapons and missiles hurled by his glorious thousand arms —

children.text: cakre tvayyatha vaiṣṇave'pi vikale buddhvā hariṃ tvāṃ mudā
children.translated_text: when even the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> discus faltered against You, understanding You to be <s>Hari</s> Himself, with joy

children.text: dhyāyantaṃ chitasrvadoṣamavadhīḥ so'gāt paraṃ te padam //
children.translated_text: meditating on You, all faults severed, he was slain by You and attained Your supreme abode.
Again, when the enraged sons of the <s>Haihaya</s> killed Your father, beholding the heart

children.text: māghnānāṃ hṛdayaṃ nirīkṣya bahuśo ghorāṃ pratijñāṃ vahan /
children.translated_text: of <s>Reṇukā</s> struck many times by them, bearing a terrible vow,
summoning through meditation a chariot and weapons, You made the <s>Kṣatriyas</s> who had wronged <s>Brahmins</s> —
cutting them down with the axe, piercing them with arrows in all quarters — making the earth devoid of <s>Kṣatriyas</s>.
Having revived Your father, conquering the royal clans twenty-one times,
having satisfied the fathers with the great blood-lake of <s>Samantapañcaka</s>,

children.text: yajñe kṣmāmapi kāśyapādiṣu diśan sālvena yudhyan punaḥ
children.translated_text: bestowing the earth to <s>Kaśyapa</s> and others in a sacrifice, and fighting <s>Sālva</s> again —
told by the young sages that '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> will slay him,' You desisted from battle.
Laying down Your weapons on <s>Mahendra</s> mountain and performing austerities, seeing the earth
submerged up to <s>Gokarṇa</s> by the ocean, and implored by ascetics,
meditating, You frightened the ocean with the <s>āgneya</s> (fire) weapon dipped in the sacrificial fire, and by hurling the ladle,
having driven him back and reclaimed <s>Kerala</s> — O <s>Bhṛgupati</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>)! O Lord of the Wind! Protect me!

children.text: sāndrānanandatano! hare! nanu purā daivāsure saṅgare
children.translated_text: O <s>Hari</s>, O embodiment of concentrated bliss! In the great battle between the gods and <s>Asuras</s> long ago,

children.text: tvatkṛttā api karmaśeṣavaśato ye te na yātā gatim /
children.translated_text: those who, though slain by You, did not attain final liberation due to residual <s>karma</s>,
born on earth as sons of <s>Diti</s>, with their burden sorely oppressing
the Earth — she, together with the gods who had come before, took refuge in <s>Brahmā</s>.
'Alas, alas! This Earth, crushed by the great burden of the wicked, about to fall into the ocean —

children.text: etāṃ pālaya hanta me vivaśatāṃ saṃpṛccha devānimān /
children.translated_text: protect her! Alas, behold my helplessness! Ask these gods!' —
beholding the Earth uttering such copious and helpless lamentations, <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: devānāṃ vadanāni vīkṣya parito dadhyau bhavantaṃ hare! //
children.translated_text: looking around at the faces of the gods, meditated upon You, O <s>Hari</s>!

children.text: ūce cāmbujabhūramūnayi surāḥ! satyaṃ dharitryā vaco
children.translated_text: And the Lotus-Born One said: 'Listen, O gods! The words of the Earth are true;

children.text: nanvasyā bhavatāṃ ca rakṣaṇavidhau dakṣo hi lakṣmīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: indeed, for the protection of her and of you, the Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) is capable.
Let all of us, with <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) at the fore, go from here to the Milk Ocean,

children.text: natvā taṃ stumahe javāditi yuyaḥ sākaṃ tavāketanam //
children.translated_text: and bowing to Him, let us praise Him swiftly!' — and they went together to Your banner-ground.
When they, having reached the shore of the Milk Ocean, gentle with cool breezes, assembled,
single-minded in meditation on Your feet — then the Lotus-Born One
heard Your words in his heart, and gladdening all, he spoke:
'The Supreme Self Himself has commanded me — now hear those words.'
'I know the wretched state of the gods and the Earth, beset by terrible kings;
to remove them, I shall take birth in the <s>Yādava</s> clan with My entire Self.
Let the gods be born in the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> clan as partial incarnations, and let the divine women descend to earth
for My service' — thus Your words were conveyed by the Lotus-Born One.

children.text: śrutvā karṇarasāyanaṃ tava vacaḥ sarveṣu nirvāpita-
children.translated_text: Having heard Your words, a nectar to the ears, when all, their hearts soothed,
O Lord, had departed, their souls satiated with the nectar of Your compassion,
in the renowned city of <s>Mathurā</s>, abounding in the merit of Your presence,
the king born of <s>Śūra</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>) married the blessed daughter of <s>Devaka</s> (<s>Devakī</s>).
After the wedding, her brother <s>Kaṃsa</s>, honoring the couple

children.text: nnetau sūtatayā gataḥ pathi rathe vyomotthayā tvadgirā /
children.translated_text: and acting as charioteer, on the road, by a voice from the sky — Your voice —
was told: 'Her eighth son, most wicked, shall slay you!' — and the terrified one

children.text: sattrāsāt sa tu hantumantikagatāḥ tanvīṃ kṛpāṇīmadhāt //
children.translated_text: drew his sword upon his sister, who was brought near for killing.
That evil-minded one, seizing her by the hair, was long soothed by <s>Vasudeva</s> (<s>Śauri</s>);

children.text: no muñcan punarātmajārpaṇagirā prīto'tha yāto gṛhān /
children.translated_text: not releasing her, he was finally pleased by the promise to surrender the children, and went home.
Though the first-born, Your elder brother (<s>Balarāma</s>), was thus surrendered, <s>Kaṃsa</s> did not kill him out of affection;

children.text: duṣṭānāmapi deva! puṣṭakaruṇā dṛṣṭā hi dhīrekadā //
children.translated_text: even in the wicked, O Lord, a fullness of compassion is sometimes seen!

children.text: tāvat tvanmanasaiva nāradamuniḥ proce sa bhojeśvaraṃ
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, by Your will, the sage <s>Nārada</s> addressed that Lord of the <s>Bhojas</s> (<s>Kaṃsa</s>):

children.text: yūyaṃ nanvasurāḥ surāśca yadavo jānāsi kiṃ na prabho! /
children.translated_text: 'You all are indeed <s>Asuras</s>, and the <s>Yādavas</s> are gods — don't you know this, O lord?
That trickster <s>Hari</s> will be born for your destruction, at the prayer of the gods' —
hearing this, he shook the <s>Yādavas</s> and killed the sons of <s>Vasudeva</s>.
When the seventh pregnancy had been achieved by the Serpent-Lord (<s>Śeṣa</s>), transferred by Your prompting through <s>Māyā</s>

children.text: nīte mādhava! rohiṇīṃ tvamapi bhoḥ! saccitsukhaikātmakaḥ /
children.translated_text: to <s>Rohiṇī</s>, O <s>Mādhava</s>, You too — who are being-consciousness-bliss itself —

children.text: devakyā jaṭharaṃ viveśitha vibho! saṃstūyamānaḥ suraiḥ
children.translated_text: entered the womb of <s>Devakī</s>, O Lord, praised by the gods;

children.text: sa tvaṃ kṛṣṇa! vidhūya rogapaṭalīṃ bhaktiṃ parāṃ dehi me //
children.translated_text: O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! Dispelling the multitude of diseases, grant me supreme devotion!
O <s>Bhagavān</s> of the form of bliss! At Your incarnation,
as brilliant rays streamed from Your radiant limbs,
the rainy season, as if covering the sky with dense dark clouds of Your
splendor, shone beautifully.
While the directions were cooled by the rains of clouds,
and the good people, having attained their hopes, were overcome with joy,
at midnight, at the rising of the moon,
You appeared here, O remover of the afflictions of the three worlds.
Even with a body resembling that of an infant, bearing divine splendor,
shining with upraised crown, bracelets, armlets, and necklace,
radiant with conch, discus, mace, and lotus —
dark as a cloud, You illumined the birth-chamber.
With <s>Lakṣmī</s>, playfully reclining on Your chest, her bliss-borne gentle
side-glances slow and languid —
You seemed to sweep away the inauspicious misfortune
of that dwelling, caused by the wicked <s>Kaṃsa</s> — You shone, O <s>Vāsudeva</s>!
<s>Vasudeva</s> (<s>Śauri</s>), beholding with his own eyes that form,
far beyond even the minds of the steadiest circles of sages,
wet with tears of joy, hair standing on end, voice choked with emotion,
praised You, whose sight was like the nectar of the <s>makara</s> fish.
'O Lord! Be gracious, O Supreme Being! O scythe that cuts the creeper of suffering!
O Equal-eyed One! O You who sport in the arts!
Remove our sorrows with Your side-glances heavy with compassion!' —
thus by him, delighted, You were praised at length.
And by Your mother, whose body-creeper was drenched with tears from her eyes,
whose qualities were praised in hymns, You, the abode of compassion —
Having awakened the memory of the pair of former births in them both,
at Your mother's word, You assumed the guise of a human infant.
Then, impelled by You, that son of <s>Śūra</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>), in order to carry out
the exchange with <s>Nanda</s>'s newborn daughter,
took You upon his hands — You who were held in his heart, O noble one,
beautiful as a young <s>haṃsa</s> (swan) cygnet seated upon a red lotus.
Then <s>Yoganidrā</s> (divine sleep) arose in the cowherd's dwelling,
and caused the townspeople to become enveloped in slumber;
by Your will — what is wonderful in this? — the doors,
though tightly fastened, opened of their own accord, even being inanimate.
Then, with <s>Śeṣa</s> warding off the rain with his many hoods
and freely lighting the path with his jewels,

children.text: tvāṃ dhārayan sa khalu dhanyatamaḥ pratasthe
children.translated_text: he (<s>Vasudeva</s>), bearing You — he, the most fortunate of all — set forth.
You are that very Lord — O Master, destroy the force of my ailments!
Bearing You, he — the chief of the <s>Yadu</s> clan — going forth,
saw the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), her waters surging toward the sky;
but that mass of water — truly a magical illusion —
in an instant subsided to the depth of a footstep.
Entering the cowherds' settlement, where the cowherd women were asleep,
with the gates left open, and a newly crying baby girl [lay there],
he placed You upon the birthing-bed, and from that place,
carrying the substitute girl, he swiftly returned to his own city.
Then, when the sleep-spell was broken by the crying of Your [substitute] sister,
the soldiers, rushing out and reporting the news of the birth, brought sorrow [to <s>Kaṃsa</s>];
the lord of the <s>Bhojas</s> (<s>Kaṃsa</s>), with his locks disheveled, coming hastily —
as if pleased — saw a baby girl in his sister's arms.
'Surely this must be the <s>māyā</s> (illusion) of the deceitful slayer of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>)!' —
thinking thus, he snatched the infant girl, clasped in his sister's arms,
as an elephant plucks a lotus-stalk from among lotuses,
and this one dashed Your sister, the Unborn One (<s>Māyā</s>), upon the stone slab.
Then, like a worshipper of Yours suddenly freed from the noose of death,
she, having swiftly assumed another form,
rising upward without touching the ground, radiant with eight arms bearing
great weapons — she shone, traveling through the sky!

children.text: nṛśaṃsatara! kaṃsa! te kimu mayā viniṣpiṣṭayā
children.translated_text: 'O most cruel <s>Kaṃsa</s>! What use to you is my being crushed?

children.text: babhūva bhavadantakaḥ kvacana cintyatāṃ te hitam /
children.translated_text: Your destroyer has been born somewhere — consider what is good for you!'

children.text: iti tvadanujā vibho! khalamudīrya taṃ jagmuṣī
children.translated_text: Thus, O Lord, Your sister, having addressed that wicked one and departing,
she, worshipped by the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>, took up her abodes on earth.
Thereupon again, following the words of the unborn one, [<s>Kaṃsa</s>] the king sent forth
the proud demons <s>Pralamba</s>, <s>Baka</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, and others,
who, desiring Your death, fearlessly roamed the world,
slayers of young children — for what is difficult for the merciless?
Then, in the cowherd's dwelling, O <s>Mukunda</s>, as You lay upon the birthing-bed of <s>Nanda</s>'s beloved,
crying a little and stirring Your tiny feet,
when the women, awakened, announced the birth of a son,
what can I say of the joy — ah, the whole of <s>Gokula</s> was in a tumult of delight!
Ah, by <s>Yaśodā</s>, who first drank in with her gaze
You — captivating her heart with Your fresh, tender beauty — nearby,

children.text: punaḥ stanabharaṃ nijaṃ sapadi pāyayantyā mudā
children.translated_text: and then joyfully suckled You at her brimming breast,
with a touch of Your enchanting body — the meritorious in the world were surpassed!
Desiring Your welfare, the cowherd <s>Nanda</s>,
overflowing with joy — what did he not give to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families?

children.text: tathaiva paśupālakāḥ kimu na maṅgalaṃ tenire
children.translated_text: And likewise the cowherds — what auspicious rite did they not perform?
O Auspiciousness of the three worlds! Protect me here from disease!
Thereupon, <s>Nanda</s>, the abode of abundant good fortune, having gone to the king's city for the payment of taxes,
was seen by Your father (<s>Vasudeva</s>), who was aware of <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s allies' preparations.

children.text: ayi sakhe! tava bālakajanma māṃ sukhayate'dya nijātmajajanmavat /
children.translated_text: 'O friend! The birth of your boy delights me today as much as the birth of my own son' —

children.text: iti bhavatpitṛtāṃ vrajanāyake samadhiropya śaśaṃsa tamādarāt //
children.translated_text: thus, bestowing upon the leader of <s>Vraja</s> the status of Your father, he spoke to him with affection.

children.text: iha ca santyanimittaśatāni te kaṭakasīmne tato laghu gamyatām /
children.translated_text: 'There are hundreds of ill omens here for you; return quickly to the border of your settlement' —

children.text: iti ca tadvacasā vrajanāyako bhavadapāyabhiyā drutamāyayau //
children.translated_text: thus, by his words, the chief of <s>Vraja</s>, fearing danger to You, returned swiftly.

children.text: avasare khalu tatra ca kācana vrajapade madhurākṛtiraṅganā /
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, in the settlement of <s>Vraja</s>, a certain woman of sweet form,
with tresses adorned by fluttering bees, came near You, O deceptive infant!

children.text: sapasi sā hṛtabālakacetanā niśicarānvayajā kila pūtanā /
children.translated_text: She was <s>Pūtanā</s>, born of a <s>Rākṣasa</s> lineage, a stealer of children's lives;
while the cowherd women were briefly deliberating 'Who among us is this?', she took You up.
Prevented from stopping her by the cowherd women whose hearts were captivated by her graceful, charming demeanor,
she, seated inside the house, offered her breast to You, the Deceptive One.
Climbing fearlessly upon her lap, You, angered by her stealing of children,
sucked fiercely at the orbs of her breasts — like a great <s>āmra</s> (mango) fruit — tainted with terrible poison.

children.text: asubhireva samaṃ dhayati tvayi stanamasau stanitopamanisvanā /
children.translated_text: As You sucked the breast along with her very life-breath, she, with a cry like thunder,

children.text: nirapatad bhayadāyi nijaṃ vapuḥ pratigatā pravisārya bhujāvubhau //
children.translated_text: fell down, reverting to her own terrifying form, stretching out both arms.
When the cowherds were bewildered by seeing and hearing of the fearsome form emitting dreadful sounds,
the <s>gopīs</s> seized You who were playing upon her chest, in the cowherd settlement.
O Auspiciousness of the world! Protected in many ways by the young women through Your very names alone,
O Lord of the Temple of Wind (<s>Guruvāyūr</s>)! Make me, who am ailing, Your servant!
The chief of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Nanda</s>), hearing <s>Śauri</s>'s (<s>Vasudeva</s>'s) words and returning along the road, fearful at heart,

children.text: niṣpiṣṭaniśśeṣataruṃ nirīkṣya kañcit padārthaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatastvām //
children.translated_text: seeing a completely shattered tree, took refuge in You, [recognizing] some [supernatural] cause.
Hearing the account from the <s>gopīs</s>' words, all the cowherds too, blinded by fear and wonder,
carried Your-felled ghastly demoness-body far away, and cut it up with axes.
From her body, whose breast had been purified by Your sucking, there arose a smoke rising very high,
which raised doubts: 'Is it <s>agaru</s> (aloe-wood) among these? Or sandalwood? Or <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium)?'

children.text: madaṅgasaṅgasya phalaṃ na dūraṃ kṣaṇena tāvad bhavatāmapi syāt /
children.translated_text: 'The fruit of contact with My body is not far — it could arise even for you all in an instant!' —
thus proclaiming to the cowherd women, You made <s>Pūtanā</s> fragrant.

children.text: citraṃ piśācyā na hataḥ kumāraścitraṃ puraivākathi śauriṇedam /
children.translated_text: 'Wonderful that the boy was not killed by the demoness! Wonderful that <s>Śauri</s> spoke of this beforehand!' —

children.text: iti praśaṃsan kila gopaloko bhavanmukhālokarase nyamāṅkṣīt //
children.translated_text: thus praising, the cowherd folk became immersed in the delight of gazing upon Your face.
Day by day, with ever-increasing splendor and hundreds of undiminished auspicious signs, this <s>Vraja</s>,
through Your dwelling [there], O <s>Vāsudeva</s>, shone all around, dense with joy.
In the homes, the charming women, engrossed in mutual conversation about Your tender beauty and smiles,
coming together to behold You after their household duties, rejoiced exceedingly each day.

children.text: aho kumāro mayi dattadṛṣṭiḥ smitaḥ kṛtaṃ māṃ prati vatsakena /
children.translated_text: 'The baby looked at me! He smiled at me, the little darling!

children.text: ehyehi māmityupasārya pāṇiṃ tvayāśa! kiṃ kiṃ na kṛtaṃ vadhūbhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Come here, come to me!' — stretching out her hands — O Lord, what did the cowherd women not do for You!
Out of eagerness to touch Your body, passed from hand to hand by the cowherd women,
You were like a garland of fresh coppery lotus blossoms, swinging and dangling beautifully.

children.text: nipāyayantī stanamaṅkagaṃ tvāṃ vilokayantī vadanaṃ hasantī /
children.translated_text: Nursing You at her breast upon her lap, gazing at Your face, smiling —

children.text: daśāṃ yaśodā katamāṃ na bheje sa tādṛśaḥ pāhi hare! gadānmām //
children.translated_text: what state of bliss did <s>Yaśodā</s> not attain! O <s>Hari</s>, of such [glory] are You — protect me from ailments!
Once, on Your birth-<s>nakṣatra</s> (star) day, O Lord, the chieftainess of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Yaśodā</s>),

children.text: mahānasastvāṃ savidhe nidhāya sā mahānasādau vavṛte vrajeśvarī //
children.translated_text: having invited kinswomen and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, placed You nearby and busied herself in the kitchen.
Then, from near You, mixed with the alarmed cries of the boys appointed to protect You,
there was distinctly heard the crackling, splintering sound of wood.
Then the cowherd women, whose heavy breasts heaved with the exertion of alarm at hearing that,
beheld You inside, surrounded on all sides by the splintering of terrible, shattered wood.

children.text: śiśoraho kiṃ kimabhūditi drutaṃ pradhāvya nandaḥ paśupāśca bhūsurāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What, what has happened to the child!' — rushing quickly, <s>Nanda</s>, the cowherds, and the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>
saw You held by <s>Yaśodā</s>, and were reassured, their eyes moist with tears.

children.text: kasko nu kautaskuta eṣa vismayo viśaṅkaṭaṃ yacchakaṭaṃ vipāṭitam /
children.translated_text: 'By whom, from what, and how has this wonder happened — that the massive cart has been shattered to pieces,

children.text: na kāraṇaṃ kiñcidiheti te sthitāḥ svanāsikādattakarāstvadīkṣakāḥ //
children.translated_text: and there is no cause whatsoever here?' — so they stood, placing fingers on their noses, gazing at You.
'This baby, wanting the breast, while crying with his swinging lotus-feet, struck [the cart] —

children.text: mayā mayā dṛṣṭamano viparyagāditīśa! te pālakabālakā jaguḥ //
children.translated_text: by me, by me it was seen — no, it happened the other way!' — thus, O Lord, Your guardian-boys declared.
At that time, the words of the boys — incomprehensible in their fear — asserting
something highly improbable for children, were deemed impossible by those unaware of Your power, though somewhat suspected by those who had witnessed [the slaying of] <s>Pūtanā</s>.

children.text: pravālatāmraṃ kimidaṃ padaṃ kṣataṃ sarojaramyau nu karau virojitau /
children.translated_text: 'Is this coral-red foot injured? Are these lotus-lovely hands bruised?' —
thus, with surging waves of compassion, the women touched Your limbs.

children.text: aye sutaṃ dehi jagatpateḥ kṛpātaraṅgapātāt paripātamadya me /
children.translated_text: 'Give me the child, O Lord of the world! By the falling of the wave of mercy, protect [him] today for me!' —

children.text: iti sma saṅgṛhya pitā tvadaṅgukaṃ guhurmuhuḥ śliṣyati jītakaṇṭakaḥ //
children.translated_text: thus, the father (<s>Nanda</s>), taking Your body, embraced [You] again and again, his hair standing on end.

children.text: anonilīnaḥ kila hantumāgataḥ surārirevaṃ bhavatā vihiṃsitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The demon, who had come to kill [You] by hiding within [the cart], was thus destroyed by You;

children.text: rajo'pi nodṛṣṭamamuṣya tat kathaṃ sa śuddhasattve tvayi līnavān dhruvam //
children.translated_text: not even a trace of his dust was seen — how then? He surely dissolved into You, who are of pure <s>sattva</s> (goodness).
Then, worshipped by the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> there, having especially received auspicious blessings,

children.text: vrajaṃ nijairbālyarasairvimohayan marutpurādhīśa! rujāṃ jahīhi me //
children.translated_text: enchanting <s>Vraja</s> with Your childhood delights — O Lord of <s>Marutpura</s> (Guruvāyūr), remove my ailments!
One day, O Lord of <s>Marutpura</s> (Guruvāyūr), when Your mother,
unable to bear the [suddenly] increasing heaviness [of Your body],
placed You on the bed, wondering 'What is this?' —
she ceased her activity, seized by apprehension in the house.
Meanwhile, from afar, the fearsome roaring sounds,
the spreading clouds of dust filling all directions —
[heralded] a demon foremost among <s>Daityas</s>, in the form of a whirlwind, called <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>,
who swept away You, the stealer of all hearts.
When the sight of the cowherd folk was blocked by the wild, thick darkness of dust,
and they were unable to see anything at all,
'Alas, what has befallen the child!' — the mother, coming near You and not finding You,
wept bitterly.
Meanwhile, that foremost demon too, his form weakened,
his speed diminished from bearing Your weight,
shrank; and thereafter, when the dust-storm subsided,
in the settlement there resounded the cry of Your mother.
Hearing the weeping, upon reaching the house,
while the clans of <s>Nanda</s> and other cowherds wailed, piteous —
the demon, [though] desiring release, could not release You, the bestower of complete liberation,
and fell from the sky.
Then the cowherds, bewildered with crying,
saw upon the surface of a great boulder outside
the enormous body of that [demon] lying fallen — and upon his chest,
You — perfectly unharmed and laughing merrily!
Upon the body of that wicked demon, whose limbs were crushed from the fall upon the rock,
whose life had departed — laughing boldly,
striking [him] with Your lotus-hands — the cowherds, approaching You,
took [You up] as if [lifting] a sapphire from a great mountain.
Seized one by one, with unbounded joy,
embraced and kissed by <s>Nanda</s> and the other cowherds,
falling from the lotus-hands of the cowherd women who hesitated out of fear of [wanting to] take [You] —
I bow to You!
'What more can we do? <s>Govinda</s> alone, the remover of the afflictions of those who bow,
may He protect our son!' —
thus, at that time, by Your mother, father, and their dear ones,
You Yourself were invoked, O Lord, for Your own protection!
Having thus shaken off this wind-bodied demon,

children.text: vātodbhavān mama gadān kimu no dhunoṣi /
children.translated_text: will You not shake off my ailments born of wind (<s>vāta</s>)?
Or what shall I do? O Lord of the Wind-Temple (<s>Guruvāyūr</s>),
I beseech You again and again for the complete removal of all diseases!

children.text: gūḍhaṃ vasudevagirā kartuṃ te niṣkriyasya saṃskārān /
children.translated_text: Secretly, at <s>Vasudeva</s>'s request, to perform Your <s>saṃskāras</s> (rites of passage),
the sage <s>Garga</s>, who knew the truth of the constellations by heart, went to Your home, O Lord.
<s>Nanda</s>, his heart gladdened, honoring this foremost among the self-controlled,
spoke with a gentle smile, eager to have Your <s>saṃskāras</s> performed.
Explaining that 'This must be done secretly, O noble one, because of your being the family priest of the <s>Yadu</s> dynasty,'
<s>Garga</s>, his hair bristling with joy, performed the naming ceremony for You along with Your elder brother.

children.text: kathamasya nāma kurve sahasranāmno hyanantanāmno vā /
children.translated_text: 'How can I name this one who has a thousand names, or rather infinite names?'

children.text: iti nūnaṃ gargamuścakre tava nāma nāma rahasi vibho! //
children.translated_text: thus indeed <s>Garga</s> performed Your naming ceremony in secret, O Lord! //
From the roots 'kṛṣ' (existence) and 'ṇa' (bliss), he expressed Your nature as existence and bliss itself,

children.text: jagadaghakarṣitvaṃ vā kathayadṛṣiḥ kṛṣṇanāma te vyatanot //
children.translated_text: or, declaring Your nature as the drawer-away of the world's sins, the sage bestowed upon You the name <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. //
Assigning also other variant names, including <s>Rāma</s> and others for the elder brother,
the sage spoke of You as of superhuman power, without revealing [this] to the father. //

children.text: snihyati yatsava putre suhyati sa na māyikaiḥ punaḥ śokaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who is affectionate toward Your son shall not suffer from illusory sorrows again;

children.text: druhyati yaḥ sa tu naśyedityavadat te mahattvamṛṣivaryaḥ //
children.translated_text: but he who is hostile shall surely perish' — thus the foremost sage declared Your greatness. //
'He will conquer many demons, lead His own kinsmen to the spotless abode;
You shall hear of His immaculate fame' — thus the sage spoke of Your glories. //
'By this one alone you shall cross all difficulties; having performed the rites, be steadfast!
He is verily <s>Hari</s>!' — though not speaking [so openly], the sage described You in these and similar ways. //
When <s>Garga</s> had then departed, You, who delighted <s>Nanda</s> and others, were celebrated by all.
O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, compassionate toward my affliction, remove [my disease]! //
O <s>Sabala</s> (accompanied by <s>Balarāma</s>)! O <s>Murāri</s> (slayer of <s>Mura</s>)! Adorning various parts of the dwelling
with the motions of Your hands and knees, You two,
with lotus-feet set in motion, the sweet tinkling of charming anklets
delighting the ears, moved about beautifully with speed. //
Softly, softly smiling, with emerging teeth,
with hair falling over Your faces, Your lotus-feet visible,
with bangles slipping from the ends of Your gliding arms —
You stole the minds of all the world's people who beheld You. //
As the crowd followed with eyes agitated by curiosity,
making some [indistinct] sounds, babbling, running about,
Your lotus-faces turned back, glancing over Your shoulders —
what delight did You not create, O <s>Vāsudeva</s>! //
Falling during Your swift movements, getting up, smeared with mud,
worshipped with smiles from above by the stainless sages in heaven,
then quickly seized by the two mothers with compassion,

children.text: muhurapi parirabdhau drāg yuvāṃ cumbitau ca //
children.translated_text: You two were embraced again and again and kissed swiftly. //
Holding You on her lap, her breasts overflowing with milk,
<s>Yaśodā</s>, of wavering mind, giving You the breast — blessed among the blessed!
O master of divine disguise as a cowherd! Amidst [the nursing], seeing Your face
with the sprout of an innocent smile, charming with its tooth-buds, she was overjoyed. //
Then, walking on Your feet, together with other children,
playing in the rows of dwellings, full of childish mischief,
chasing after house-parrots, cats, and calves,
You were restrained somehow by the cowherds, [themselves] laughing. //
Wherever You went, together with <s>Haladhra</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>),
there and there the <s>Gopīs</s> (cowherd women), their eyes falling helplessly [upon You],
abandoning their household duties, forgetting their children and servants,
O <s>Murahara</s> (slayer of <s>Mura</s>), were constantly and exceedingly agitated. //
Desiring ever-fresh butter given by the <s>Gopīs</s>,
singing sweetly, dancing tenderly somewhere,
eating the ghee offered by the compassionate young women,
somewhere You drank freshly heated milk. //
'Let the begging that was done at <s>Bali</s>'s house remain there —
here before these helpless women I shall not beg again!' —

children.text: iti vihitamatiḥ kiṃ deva! santyajya yācñāṃ
children.translated_text: having resolved thus, O Lord, abandoning begging,
You stole curd and ghee by charming thievery! //
At Your theft of curd and ghee, in the hearts of the cowherd women

children.text: mabhajata hṛdi roṣo nāvakāśaṃ na śokaḥ /
children.translated_text: there was no room for anger, nor for grief.
Having stolen their hearts too, You plunged them into an ocean of joy —
O that One, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, pacify my diseases! //

children.text: śākhāgre'tha vidhuṃ vilokya phalamityambāṃ ca tātaṃ muhuḥ
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the moon at a treetop and [taking it for] a fruit, and repeatedly
asking mother and father — and when, at their words, You raised Your arms,

children.text: citraṃ deva! śaśī sa te karamagāt kiṃ brūmahe sampata-
children.translated_text: wonder, O Lord! — that moon came into Your hand! And what shall we say — with the entire
host of luminous spheres filling Your whole body, You assumed Your <s>Virāṭ</s> (cosmic) form. //
'What, what is this indeed!' — while the father, seized with alarm,
was submerged for a moment in the cosmic ocean by You,
then spreading again the <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) that causes the delusion of [seeing You as] a child —
