O You who are bliss-consciousness! O You who are the universe! Protect me from disease! //

children.text: ayi deva! purā kila tvayi svayamuttānaśaye stanandhaye /
children.translated_text: O Lord! Once, long ago, when You, an infant at the breast, were lying on Your back,
when Your mouth opened wide in a yawn, the cowherd woman beheld the universe [within]. //

children.text: punarapyatha bālakaiḥ samaṃ tvayi līlānirate jagatpate! /
children.translated_text: Then again, when You, O Lord of the universe, were at play with the [cowherd] boys,
the children, angry at being cheated of their collection of fruits, told [<s>Yaśodā</s>] that You had eaten mud. //
O Lord! For You who, at the time of dissolution, devour earth, water, and all else,

children.text: mṛdupāśanato rujā bhavediti bhītā jananī cukopa sā ///
children.translated_text: eating a little mud could cause no harm — yet the frightened mother grew angry. //

children.text: ayi durvinayātmaka! tvayā kimu mṛtsā bata vatsa! bhakṣitā /
children.translated_text: 'O naughty child! Have you really eaten mud, dear child?'

children.text: iti mātṛgiraṃ ciraṃ vibho! vitathāṃ tvaṃ pratijajñiṣe hasan //
children.translated_text: To such words of the mother, O Lord, You denied it for a long time, laughing. //

children.text: ayi te sakalairviniścite vimatiśced vadanaṃ vidāryatām /
children.translated_text: 'If all have established this, then if you disagree, let the mouth be opened!' —
thus scolded by the mother, You opened Your mouth, [radiant] like a blossoming lotus. //

children.text: ayi mṛllavadarśanotsukāṃ jananīṃ tāṃ bahu tarpayanniva /
children.translated_text: As if greatly satisfying the mother, who was eager to see a lump of mud,
You showed not merely the entire earth, but all the worlds as well! //

children.text: kuhacid vanamambudhiḥ kvacit kvacidabhraṃ kuhacid rasātalam /
children.translated_text: Here a forest, there an ocean, somewhere clouds, somewhere the netherworld,

children.text: manujā danujāḥ kvacit surā dadṛśe kiṃ na tadā tvadānane //
children.translated_text: humans, demons somewhere, gods — what was not seen then in Your mouth? //
And again [she saw] the One reclining on the Milk-Ocean, the One dwelling in supreme <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>,

children.text: svapuraśca nijārbhakātmakaṃ katidhā tvāṃ na dadarśa sā mukhe //
children.translated_text: and in Her own city, [You] in the form of Her own infant — in how many forms did she not see You in that mouth! //
In the open interior of Your mouth, a world expanding — and within that again, a similar mouth —
clearly beheld by her — You revealed, alas, the infinite regression of the worlds! //

children.text: dhṛtatattvadhiyaṃ tadā kṣaṇaṃ jananīṃ tāṃ praṇayena mohayan /
children.translated_text: Then, for a moment deluding with affection that mother who had grasped the truth,
You clung to her [saying] 'Mother, give me the breast!' — O wondrous child! O Lord! Protect me! //
One day, when Your mother was churning curd,
You, greedy for breast-milk, approaching, climbed onto her lap and drank from both breasts. //
While You had half-drunk from the breast-buds, Your lotus-face sweet with a tender smile,

children.text: dugdhamīśa! dahane parisnutaṃ dhartumāśu jananī jagāma te //
children.translated_text: O Lord! The milk on the fire overflowed — and Your mother hastened to attend to it. //
Your mind overwhelmed by a great burden of anger born from the interruption of the half-tasted nectar,

children.text: manthadaṇḍamupagṛhya pāṭitaṃ hanta deva! dadhibhājanaṃ tvayā //
children.translated_text: seizing the churning rod — alas, O Lord! — You shattered the curd-pot! //
Hearing the high-pitched crash just then, the mother hurried back,

children.text: tvadyaśovisaravad dadarśa sā sadya eva dadhi visṛtaṃ kṣitau //
children.translated_text: and she beheld the curd spilled upon the ground, spread like Your fame. //
Not seeing You, searched for as the <s>Vedas</s> search for [the Supreme] along the paths,
the [blessed] woman found You at the mortar, giving away fresh butter to a monkey. //
Seizing You — whose lotus-face shone with the semblance of fear — quickly,
she, her face reddened with anger, before her friends, took up a cord for binding [You]. //
She who desired to bind that very One whom the righteous seek as the [supreme] bond —

children.text: sā niyujya raśanāguṇān bahūn vdyaṅgulonamakhilaṃ kilaikṣata //
children.translated_text: she, joining many lengths of cord, found all of it two fingers short! //
Seeing her, perspiring, her body exhausted, observed by her astonished and smiling friends,
You, O <s>Hari</s>, though eternally free in Your being, alas, out of compassion consented to bondage! //

children.text: sthīyatāṃ ciramulūkhale khaletyāgatā bhavanameva sā yadā /
children.translated_text: 'Stay long at the mortar, O rascal!' — when she, having said this, had gone back into the house,
You, intoxicated by the butter offered [earlier], stood in the opening between the mortar [and a pair of trees]. //

children.text: yadyapāśasugamo bhavān vibho! saṃyataḥ kimu sapāśayānayā /
children.translated_text: O Lord, if You are easily approachable through the bond [of love], why were You bound by her with a cord?

children.text: evamādi divijairabhiṣṭuto vātanātha! paripāhi māṃ gadāt //
children.translated_text: Thus and in other ways praised by the celestials — O Lord of the wind-abode (<s>Guruvāyūr</s>), protect me from disease! //
With joy, the celestial women, with noble exultation, praising You as '<s>Dāmodara</s>' (bound at the belly),
You, of tender belly, clinging freely to the mortar, beheld nearby two <s>Arjuna</s> trees. //

children.text: kuberasūnurnalakūbarābhidhaḥ paro maṇigrīva iti prathāṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: One was the son of <s>Kubera</s>, named <s>Nalakūbara</s>; the other was celebrated as <s>Maṇigrīva</s>.
Intoxicated by the wealth obtained through the worship of <s>Maheśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), they had long sported, turned away from You. //
At the celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), those two, frenzied with drink, sporting naked amidst many women

children.text: vivāsasau keliparau sa nārado bhavatpadaikapravaṇo niraikṣata //
children.translated_text: who sang of the celestial river — <s>Nārada</s>, devoted solely to Your feet, observed them. //
Though seeing before him [<s>Nārada</s>], who out of modesty for [observing] the beloved had put on clothes,

children.text: imau bhavadbhaktyupaśāntisiddhaye munirjagau śāntimṛte kutaḥ sukham //
children.translated_text: those two, blind with intoxication — the sage declared [to them]: 'For the attainment of devotion to <s>Hari</s> and tranquility — without peace, whence happiness?' //

children.text: yuvāmavāptau kakubhātmatāṃ ciraṃ hariṃ nirīkṣyātha padaṃ svamāpnutam /
children.translated_text: 'You two shall long remain in the form of <s>Arjuna</s> trees, and having beheld <s>Hari</s>, you shall attain your own state' —

children.text: itīritau tau bhavadīkṣaṇaspṛhāṃ gatau vrajānte kakubhau babhūvatuḥ //
children.translated_text: thus addressed, those two, [now] with a longing to see You, became <s>Arjuna</s> trees at the edge of <s>Vraja</s>. //
That pair of <s>Indra</s>'s trees, by You who approached untiringly, moving slowly,
blocked diagonally by the mortar, were shaken and finally, long-decayed, toppled. //

children.text: abhāji śākhidvitayaṃ yadā tvayā tadaiva tadgarbhatalānnireyuṣā /
children.translated_text: When the pair of trees was felled by You, at that very moment, emerging from within their trunks,

children.text: mahātviṣā yakṣayugena tatkṣaṇādabhāji govinda! bhavānapi stavaiḥ //
children.translated_text: by a <s>Yakṣa</s> pair of great splendor, You too, O <s>Govinda</s>, were praised with hymns. //

children.text: ihānyabhakto'pi sameṣyati kramād bhavantametau khalu rudrasevakau /
children.translated_text: 'Here, even one devoted to another [deity] shall gradually come to You; these two, being servants of <s>Rudra</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: muniprasādād bhavadaṅghrimāgatau gatau vṛṇānau khalu bhaktimuttamām //
children.translated_text: by the sage's grace having reached Your feet, departed, choosing supreme devotion.' //
Then, when the cowherd settlement was shaken by the terrible crash of the trees being uprooted,
You, the bestower of liberation, were freed by <s>Nanda</s>, looking at Your mother's embarrassed face. //
'The boy who was between the trees — by the power of <s>Hari</s>, is now unharmed!' —

children.text: iti bravāṇairgamito gṛhaṃ bhavān marutpurādhīśvara! pāhi māṃ gadāt //
children.translated_text: thus saying, [the cowherds] took You home. O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, protect me from disease! //
The cowherds, unaware of Your power, [seeing] the falling of the trees and other [omens] in the settlement,
suspecting a multitude of evil portents, made up their minds to move elsewhere. //
Thereupon, the chief cowherd named <s>Upananda</s>, impelled by You indeed,

children.text: itiḥ pratīcyāṃ vipinaṃ manojñaṃ bṛndāvanaṃ nāma virājatīti //
children.translated_text: spoke: 'To the west shines a charming forest called <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.' //

children.text: bṛhadvanaṃ tat khalu nandamukhyā vidhāya gauṣṭhīnamatha kṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: That great forest — <s>Nanda</s> and the chief [cowherds], having assembled the cattle-settlement in a moment,
accompanied by heavy carts upon which Your mother sat with You, set forth. //
The path's length was not noticed by the women, who drank in
Your delightful words of amusement, amid the exceedingly charming sounds and the clatter of the hooves of the herds of cattle. //
Beholding <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, O Lord — its thriving clusters of blossoming <s>Kunda</s> and other trees,
You were delighted, its beauty enhanced by the luxuriance of verdant lawns like floors of emerald. //
When all the cowherds were happily settled in the freshly arranged separate dwellings,
You, mingling with the bands of cowherd boys, went about beholding the forest's beauty. //
You beheld the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), whose waters flowed pure along winding courses,
whose pleasant murmurs were made by [the calls of] swans, her face ever-smiling with lotuses. //
Captivating with the hundred cries of peacocks, mottled with the gleam of gems,
touching the world of <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) with its lofty peaks — You also beheld Mount <s>Govardhana</s>. //

children.text: samaṃ tato gopakumārakaistvaṃ samantato yatra vanāntamāgāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, together with the cowherd boys, wherever You went to the forest's edge,
from all sides You beheld the winding daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), as if she alone were passionate [for You]. //
In such a forest, suitable for pasturing, eagerly engaged in tending the herds of calves,

children.text: caran sarāmo'tha kumārakaistvaṃ samīragehādhipa! pāhi rogāt //
children.translated_text: wandering with <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) and the boys — O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, protect me from disease! //
In beautiful <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, humming with swarms of restless bees,
eagerly tending the calves together with the cowherd boys,
O Lord! O <s>Śrīman</s>! Companion of <s>Haladhra</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>)! You roamed about, carrying
a ball, a flute, and a staff — Your bodily radiance a feast for the eyes. //
When Your pair of feet — which protect the world and are caressed by the lotus-hands of <s>Lakṣmī</s> —
trod upon the sacred ground of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
what indeed did not shine forth, filled with prosperity? Trees, creepers,
waters, earth, mountains, fields, and all else, O Lord of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>)! //
On the shining meadows, in the cool-breezy forest's edge,
on the broad banks of the <s>Yamunā</s>, on the summit of Mount <s>Govardhana</s>,
the melodious sound of Your flute, as You herded the calves,
One day, You spotted a demon in the form of a calf. //
Observing from afar its tail swishing with excitement, its neck turned in some peculiar way,
watching for an opportunity,
then seizing it by the legs, whirling it about again and again with great force,
You hurled it onto a great tree, destroying its life. //
When that great demon, wicked by nature, fell — in that instant,
the forest was shattered, the trees crushed by the force of his fall;
in the sky, hosts of assembled celestials, with showers of flowers,

children.text: śirasi bhavato harṣād varṣanti nāma tadā hare! //
children.translated_text: rained [blossoms] upon Your head in delight, O <s>Hari</s>! //
'Whence this exceedingly fragrant cascade of flowers falling upon the head from above?' —
when asked thus by the boys, You playfully replied:
'It is simply that the cluster of flowers which went upward from the tree-tops when the demon was flung,
is surely now coming back down slowly.' //
On another day, once again, in the fierce heat of the scorching afternoon,
You and the others went to drink the waters of the <s>Yamunā</s>, daughter of the Sun.
They beheld a heron with outstretched wings — enormous, [previously] overlooked,
like another <s>Kailāsa</s> mountain set against the mountain-hued background. //
While the cowherd boys were drinking water, that [heron] rushed at You
and swallowed [You] — then, burning with fire-like [heat], quickly vomited [You] out.

children.text: dalayitumagāt troṭyāḥ koṭyā tadā yu bhavān vibho!
children.translated_text: When it came to tear [You apart] with the sharp tip of its beak, then You, O Lord!
O destroyer of the wicked! seizing its two beaks, tore it apart. //

children.text: sapadi sahajāṃ sandraṣṭuṃ vā mṛtāṃ khalu pūtanā-
children.translated_text: Perhaps to see at once its kinsman <s>Pūtanā</s>, already dead,
or to go ahead and await [the demon] <s>Agha</s> as well,
when that crane (<s>Baka</s>) had gone to the abode of Death — the divine host
showered celestial flowers; from <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, You returned home. //
Hearing from afar the sweet sound of [Your] flute, the young women
swiftly approached and beheld [You] with rising delight;
producing joy in the hearts of [Your] mothers — O <s>Śauri</s>! O You who are celebrated
as dwelling in the temple of the Wind-God (<s>Guruvāyūr</s>)! Remove my afflictions! //
Once, O Lord! together with the cowherd boys, You,
having resolved early in the morning to eat in the forest,
surrounded by many groups of calves,
set forth with provisions. //
From Your two lotus-feet, the dust that rose up,
purifying the three worlds,
the great sages with their horripilating bodies
gathered up, celebrating the festival of beholding You. //
As You, O Lord! together with the boys, were letting the cattle graze
on ground thick with fresh grass,
<s>Aghāsura</s>, in order to [bring] ruin, blocked the path —
terrifying, in the form of a reclining serpent. //
Its mouth, wide open like the cave of a great mountain,
spread far in the forest,
and the boys, out of playful curiosity, entered the mouth and belly,
while You were still at some distance. //
When the cowherd group along with the calves entered the serpent's belly unawares,
[the serpent's] body seething [with heat],
You too, though knowing this, entered, O Lord!
to rescue quickly the helpless companions. //
By You, who expanded Your body within the throat,
as the great serpent thrashed about with its breath obstructed,
You swiftly burst open its neck
and emerged, releasing the cowherds and cattle. //
A great radiance — ah, a vast light — born from the great demon,
waited momentarily in the sky to merge with You.
When You emerged, it instantly dissolved [into You],
and in the celestial vault, the gods danced and sang. //
Followed with wonder by the Lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>) and other gods,
You then returned with the boys.
Later in the day, when noontime arrived,
You, with Your companions, celebrated a feast. //
Placing the horn and the flute at Your hip,
holding a morsel of food in Your lotus-hand,
making the boys laugh with playful words,
You ate, praised with joy by the hosts of celestials. //
'Your happy eating here among the cowherd assembly
seems dearer [to You] than the sacrificial food in the celestial assembly' —
thus praised by the lords of the gods, O Lord of the worlds!
O Dweller of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Protect me from disease! //
Having witnessed in You a greatness unseen in Your other incarnations,
upon the liberation of <s>Agha</s>,
<s>Brahmā</s>, desiring to test [You], went out of sight
and carried away the calves, extending his <s>māyā</s> (power of illusion). //
When the calves were not seen and the cowherd group was helpless — wishing
to bring them back, as though following <s>Brahmā</s>'s intention,
You, with the morsel of food still half-eaten, went then —
and the Lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>) hid the boys who had [already] eaten as well. //
Then You Yourself became the calves, and You became the groups of cowherds,
assuming the forms of their sling-baskets, vessels, flutes, and horn-sticks.
Sporting as before in the forests for a long time, in the evening,
You, by Your <s>māyā</s>, multiplied, entered <s>Vraja</s> (the settlement). //
Carrying Yourself in the forms of sling-baskets, horn-sticks, and the like,
You again Yourself [assumed] the forms of cattle, calves, and boys.
By the mothers, in the form of cows, and by the cowherd wives in motherly form,
You were welcomed with surpassing delight. //
For they, due to the force of natural identification, regarding some soul as their own,
thinking 'this is my son,' bearing a full measure of affection —
having now obtained You Yourself, the Supreme Self, as their son,
the women and the cows experienced an immeasurable joy! //
Thus, with an ever-expanding fullness of delight at every moment,
Your manifold forms cherished by all the cowherd folk —
even Your elder brother (<s>Balarāma</s>) came to realize [the truth] at the year's end;
indeed, the difference between You two — <s>Brahmā</s> and [the universal] Self — is great! //
When, at the end of the year, <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>Druhiṇa</s>), confused, his discrimination blunted,
saw fresh new-and-old calf-herders,
You revealed [Yourself as] newly-manifested [forms], adorned with diadems, armlets, and the like,
four-armed, of the hue of rain-laden clouds. //
Each one individually was caressed in the lap of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>),
reclining on the couch of the lord of serpents (<s>Śeṣa</s>), delightful to behold,
with eyes playfully half-closed, attended upon by <s>Sanaka</s> and other <s>yogis</s> —
the Lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>) beheld [all these forms] of Yours. //
Beholding Your innumerable <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>-forms,
and seeing himself as a servant everywhere, the Creator (<s>Brahmā</s>),
his heart plunged into [Your] <s>māyā</s>, was utterly bewildered — until
You alone remained, with the half-eaten morsel in Your hand. //
Then, with his pride destroyed, having bowed to You, the Lord of the universe, again and again,

children.text: natvā ca nūtavati dhātari dhāma yāte /
children.translated_text: and when <s>Brahmā</s>, having praised [You], departed to his abode,
You, entering the settlement with the joyful boys —
O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! O Lord! Protect me from disease! //

children.text: atītya bālyaṃ jagatāṃ pate! tvamupetya paugaṇḍavayo manojñam /
children.translated_text: O Lord of the worlds! Having passed beyond infancy, reaching the charming age of boyhood (<s>paugaṇḍa</s>),
setting aside the tending of calves with delight, You commenced the herding of cows. //
This activity of Yours is indeed consistent with the purpose [of Your incarnation], O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>!
You descended for the protection of cows and the earth — that very [purpose] You began to fulfill, O Lord! //

children.text: kadāpi rāmeṇa samaṃ vanānte vanaśriyaṃ vīkṣya caran sukhena /
children.translated_text: Once, while wandering happily with <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) at the forest's edge, beholding the beauty of the woods,

children.text: śrīdāmanāmnaḥ svasakhasya vācā modādagā dhenukakānanaṃ tvam //
children.translated_text: at the words of Your companion named <s>Śrīdāman</s>, You joyfully went to the <s>Dhenuka</s> forest. //

children.text: uttālatālīnivahe tvaduktyā balena dhūte'tha balena dorbhyām /
children.translated_text: When the thick grove of palm trees was shaken by <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) with [his] strength, at Your command, by the force of his arms,
a gentle and also fierce [thing] fell before [You] — a shower of fruits, and also the demon <s>Dhenuka</s>. //

children.text: samudyato dhainukapālane'haṃ vadhaṃ kathaṃ dhainukamadya kurve /
children.translated_text: 'I am engaged in protecting cows (<s>dhenu</s>) — how can I today kill <s>Dhenuka</s> (the cow-shaped demon)?' —
thinking thus, surely, You had the elder brother (<s>Balarāma</s>) slay [that demon], destroyer of the obstruction of the gods. //
His servants too, who had come in the form of jackals — together with the elder brother,

children.text: jambūphalānīva tadā nirāsthastāleṣu khelan bhagavan! nirāsthaḥ //
children.translated_text: You tossed them, nonchalantly, onto the palm trees like <s>jambū</s> fruits, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! //
As You were destroying the host of jackals, <s>Varuṇa</s>, at that time, because of the shared name,
became terrified — I believe he established the <s>Vedically</s> renowned name 'jackal' (<s>jambuka</s>) [as fearsome]. //
'The fruit of Your incarnation has been born today, O <s>Murāri</s> (Slayer of <s>Mura</s>)!' — thus praised by the gods,

children.text: satyaṃ phalaṃ jātamiheti hāsī bālaiḥ samaṃ tālaphalānyabhuṅkthāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, fruit has been born here!' — laughing thus, You ate the palm fruits together with the boys. //

children.text: madhudravasrunti bṛhanti tāni phalāni medobharabhṛnti bhuktvā /
children.translated_text: Having eaten those large fruits dripping with honey, heavy with their rich contents,

children.text: tṛptaiśca dṛptairbhavanaṃ phalaughaṃ vahadbhirāgāḥ khalu bālakaistvam //
children.translated_text: You returned home with the boys — satisfied and exuberant — carrying loads of fruits. //

children.text: hato hato dhenuka ityupetya phalānyadadbhirmadhurāṇi lokaiḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Dhenuka</s> is slain! <s>Dhenuka</s> is slain!' — thus [exclaimed] the people who came offering sweet fruits;

children.text: jayeti jīveti nuto vibho! tvaṃ marutpurādhīśvara! pāhi rogāt //
children.translated_text: 'Victory! Long live [the Lord]!' — thus praised, O Lord! O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Protect me from disease! //
In former times, the sage <s>Saubhari</s>, devoted to Your service, performing austerities submerged in the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>) for twelve years,

children.text: mīnavrāte snehavān bhogalole tārkṣyaṃ sākṣādaikṣatāgre kadācit //
children.translated_text: once, while being affectionate toward a school of fish that was indulging in pleasures, beheld <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) directly before him. //

children.text: tvadvāhaṃ taṃ sakṣudhaṃ tṛkṣasūnuṃ mīnaṃ kañcijjakṣataṃ lakṣayan saḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing Your mount, the son of <s>Tṛkṣa</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), hungry, devouring a certain fish,

children.text: taptaścitte śaptavānatra cet tvaṃ jantūn bhoktā jīvitaṃ cāpi bhoktā //
children.translated_text: he, pained in his heart, cursed [<s>Garuḍa</s>]: 'If you devour creatures here, you shall forfeit your life as well.' //

children.text: tasmin kāle kāliyaḥ kṣveladarpāt sarpārāte kalpitaṃ bhāgamśnan /
children.translated_text: At that time, <s>Kāliya</s>, proud of his venom, eating the share allotted to the enemy of serpents (<s>Garuḍa</s>),

children.text: tena krodhāt tvat padāmbhojabhājā pakṣakṣiptastaddurāpaṃ payo'gāt //
children.translated_text: was struck by the wing of <s>Garuḍa</s>, devoted to Your lotus feet; then [<s>Kāliya</s>] went to that inaccessible water [of the <s>Yamunā</s>]. //

children.text: ghore tasmin sūrajānīravāse tīre vṛkṣā vikṣatāḥ kṣvelavegāt /
children.translated_text: In that terrible dwelling of the son of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), on the banks, the trees were withered by the force of the venom,

children.text: pakṣivrātāḥ peturabhre patantaḥ kāruṇyārdraṃ tvanmanastena jātam //
children.translated_text: flocks of birds fell from the sky as they flew over — and Your mind became moist with compassion. //

children.text: kāle tasminnekadā sīrapāṇiṃ muktvā yāte yāmunaṃ kānanāntam /
children.translated_text: At that time, one day, when the Plough-bearer (<s>Balarāma</s>) had gone to the far end of the <s>Yamunā</s> forest,
the cows and cowherds, parched by the terrible heat of fierce summer, drank the poisonous water, with You [among them]. //

children.text: naśyajjīvān vicyutān kṣmātale tān viśvān paśyannacyuta! tvaṃ dayārdraḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing all those whose lives were fading, fallen upon the ground, O <s>Acyuta</s>! You, tender with compassion,
approaching near, You instantly revived them with Your gracious glances raining nectar-water. //

children.text: kiṃ kiṃ jāto harṣavarṣātirekaḥ sarvāṅgeṣvityutthitā gopasaṅghāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What is this? An excess of shower of joy in all the limbs!' — thus the cowherd groups arose,

children.text: dṛṣṭvāgre tvāṃ tvatkṛtaṃ tad vidantasrvāmāliṅgan dṛṣṭanānāprabhāvāḥ //
children.translated_text: and seeing You before them, recognizing that it was Your doing, they embraced You, having witnessed Your manifold powers. //

children.text: gāvaścaivaṃ labdhajīvāḥ kṣaṇena sphītānandāstvāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā purastāt /
children.translated_text: The cows too, having recovered their lives in an instant, filled with abundant joy upon seeing You before them,
quickly surrounded You on all sides, releasing tears of joy, lowing softly. //

children.text: romāñco'yaṃ sarvato naḥ śarīre bhūyasyantaḥ kācidānandamūrchā /
children.translated_text: 'This horripilation is throughout our bodies; within, there is a certain swoon of bliss;
wondrous is this power of the venom, O <s>Mukunda</s>!' — thus addressed by the cowherds, You were praised and honored. //
Thus, Your devotees, even those whose lives had departed, You restore and free from disease with Your gentle sidelong glances;
being of such boundless compassion, O Dweller of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Protect me from disease! //

children.text: atha vāriṇi ghorataraṃ phaṇinaṃ prativārayituṃ kṛtadhīrbhagavan! /
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! having resolved to confront the most terrible serpent in the waters,
You swiftly climbed a <s>Kadamba</s> tree on the bank, its leaves withered by the poisonous fumes. //
Ascending it with Your lotus-feet, lovely in hue like fresh sprouts,
You leaped far into the deep water, with its terribly churning waves. //
Under Your weight — You who bear the burden of the three worlds — the river,

children.text: parimajjayati sma dhanuḥśataṃ taṭinī jhaṭiti sphuṭaghoṣavatī //
children.translated_text: its waters surging and swelling, suddenly flooded a hundred bow-lengths, with a loud roar. //
Then, in all directions and intermediate quarters, with the tumultuous sound of waters agitated and churned within,
the lord of serpents emerged from the waters, his mind blinded by unabated fury, approaching You. //
You beheld the serpent before You — bearing showers of virulent poison, with blazing fire-sparks
issuing from thousands of hood-crests — like the dark <s>Añjana</s> mountain with many peaks. //
That great serpent, with the force of its hissing exhalations dripping with terrible venom, with blazing eyes,
bit You, the One of infinite strength, and coiled around You, rendering Your movements indistinct — ah! //
When You could not be seen, and the calves and cowherd boys on the bank became distressed,
and in the homes of <s>Vraja</s> too, seeing a hundred inauspicious omens, the cowherds went to the <s>Yamunā</s>. //
O Lord! When all of them, seeing Your condition, were about to abandon the burden of their lives,
You swiftly freed Yourself from the serpent's coils and emerged with a smile. //

children.text: adhiruhya tataḥ phaṇirājaphaṇān nanṛte bhavatā mṛdupādarucā /
children.translated_text: Then, climbing upon the hoods of the serpent-king, You danced with Your tender, beautiful feet,
with the sweet jingling of anklets and the tinkling of bracelets on Your hands blending [in melody]. //
The cowherds rejoiced, the sages were gratified, the hosts of <s>Indra</s>'s celestials showered flowers —

children.text: tvayi nṛtyati mārutagehapate! paripāhi sa māṃ tvamadāntagadāt //
children.translated_text: as You danced, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Protect me from uncontrolled disease! //
With the circle of Your earrings beautifully swaying, O Lord! You danced long upon the serpent,
while the gods beat drums beautifully in the sky and divine maidens sang.

children.text: namati yadyadamuṣya śiro hare! parivihāya tadunnatamunnatam /
children.translated_text: Whenever a head of his bowed down, O <s>Hari</s>, pushing aside that one, [another] rose up high;
trampling long with the lotus of Your foot, You danced with a captivating clapping of hands.
When his hood-clusters were broken and bent by You, and the waters were reddened with flowing blood,
as the lord of serpents was sinking, his wives bowed at Your feet, O <s>Mādhava</s>!

children.text: ayi puraiva cirāya pariśrutatvadanubhāvavilīnahṛdo hi tāḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, even long before, with their hearts dissolved by hearing of Your greatness,
they praised You, O Lord, spontaneously, with hymns unattainable even by sages.
Your heart overflowed with compassion upon beholding the devotion of the serpent's wives;
the lord of serpents, revived by You, O <s>Acyuta</s>, with body surrendered, bowed down.

children.text: ramaṇakaṃ vraje cāridhimadhyagaṃ phaṇiripurna karoti virodhitām /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ramaṇaka</s>, [an island] in the middle of the ocean, is [your home]; the enemy of serpents (<s>Garuḍa</s>) shall not cause you any hostility there' —
thus greatly honoring Your words, the lord of serpents departed together with his serpent retinue.
Adorned with glowing necklaces and silk garments given by the jewels offered by the serpent's wives,
You were reunited at day's end with Your people on the bank, their joy mixed with tears.

children.text: niśi punastamasā vrajamandiraṃ vrajitumakṣama eva janotkare /
children.translated_text: At night, when the multitude of people were unable to return to the houses of <s>Vraja</s> because of the darkness,
as they slept there, taking refuge at Your feet, a forest fire encircled them from all sides.
Awakening them, who then raised piteous cries of 'Save us! Save us!', those cowherds,

children.text: avitumāśu papātha mahānalaṃ kimiha citramayaṃ khalu te mukham //
children.translated_text: You swiftly swallowed the great fire to protect them — is this any wonder? For Your mouth is indeed that [fire].

children.text: śikhina varṇata eva hi pītatā parilasatyudhanā kriyayāpyasau /
children.translated_text: For even by description of colors, the yellowness of fire shines forth; and by action too, [the analogy holds];

children.text: iti nutaḥ paśupairmuditairvibho! hara hare! duritaiḥ saha me gadān //
children.translated_text: thus praised by the delighted cowherds — O Lord, O <s>Hari</s>, take away my diseases together with my sins!

children.text: rāmasakhaḥ kvāpi dine kāmada! bhagavan! gato bhavān vipinam /
children.translated_text: Accompanied by <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), one day, O fulfiller of desires, O Lord, You went to the forest,
surrounded by the sons of the cowherds and the cows, splendid in Your garments.
Showing <s>Balarāma</s> freely the pure beauty of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
You came playing to the <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> banyan tree with the skilled boys.
Meanwhile, a merciless <s>Daitya</s> named <s>Pralamba</s>, desirous of Your destruction,
in the guise of a cowherd, approached You of long arms.
Though knowing him, as if unaware, having bound friendship with him,
near the banyan tree, You began pair-combat games with groups of skillful cowherd boys.

children.text: gopān vibhajya tanvan saṅghaṃ balabhadrakaṃ bhavatkamapi /
children.translated_text: Dividing the cowherds into two groups — one of <s>Balarāma</s>'s side and one of Yours —
You deemed the <s>Daitya</s>, who feared Your power, to belong to <s>Balarāma</s>'s group, O Lord.
In the contest where the vanquished would carry the victor, [You placed] Your dearest
<s>Śrīdāma</s> in the defeated group — thus demonstrating Your servanthood to Your devotees.

children.text: evaṃ bahuṣu vibhūman! bāleṣu vahatsu vāhyamāneṣu /
children.translated_text: Thus, O All-pervading One, when many boys were carrying [others] and being carried,

children.text: rāmavijitaḥ pralambo jahāra taṃ dūrato bhavadbhītyā //
children.translated_text: <s>Pralamba</s>, defeated by <s>Rāma</s>, carried him far away out of fear of You.

children.text: tvad dūraṃ gamayantaṃ taṃ dṛṛṣṭvā halini vihitagarimabhare /
children.translated_text: Seeing him carrying [<s>Balarāma</s>] far from You, when the weight placed on the wielder of the plough [grew heavy],

children.text: daityaḥ svarūpamāgād yadrūpāt sa hi balo'pi cakito'bhūt //
children.translated_text: the <s>Daitya</s> assumed his true form — at whose sight even <s>Balarāma</s> was startled.
But, seeing Your face from afar above the tall <s>Daitya</s> form, <s>Rāma</s>,
freed from fear, with a firm fist, immediately crushed that exceedingly wicked one.
Having slain the <s>Dānava</s> hero, You embraced the returned <s>Balarāma</s> with love;
at the meeting of you two, the hosts of gods released a shower of flowers upon your heads.
O support of the worlds! Having thus accomplished the destruction of <s>Pralamba</s>,

children.text: kālaṃ vihāya sadyo lolambaruce! hare! hareḥ kleśān //
children.translated_text: without delay, O <s>Hari</s>, You whose radiance is like a swinging garland — take away my diseases!
While You were absorbed in play with the host of boys, delaying [in the aftermath] of the slaying of <s>Pralamba</s>,
the cows, roaming freely,
engrossed in grazing on grass, wandering far and far,
entered a certain forest called <s>Muñja</s> (reed forest).
Having left <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, whose interior is unacquainted with the harshness of summer heat,
those cows, having come out to this [other] forest,
distressed by separation from You, bewildered by the spreading blaze of the harsh summer heat
and the oppressive bushes, stood still.
Then, after searching far with Your companions, O <s>Śauri</s>,
seeing the herd of cattle in distress from having lost their path in the <s>Muñja</s> reed-forest,
when You went swiftly to bring them back from afar —
alas, alas! — a forest fire blazed up on all sides.
As the terrifying fire blazed with dreadful roaring, consuming everything,
with paths blocked, half-scorched, afflicted,
'Alas, O friend of the world! Save us, save us!' — thus all of them,
seeking refuge, approached You alone, the remover of suffering.
'Enough, enough, do not be afraid! Close your eyes from all sides' —
at Your words, when they closed their eyes,
'Where is that forest fire? Where is that <s>Muñja</s> thicket?' —
they suddenly found themselves at the <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> [banyan] region!

children.text: jaya jaya tava māyā keyamīśeti teṣāṃ
children.translated_text: 'Victory, victory! What is this <s>māyā</s> of Yours, O Lord!' — thus by their praises,
laughing aloud, bound in various joyful sports,
You again roamed at the forest's edge, where the summer's effect
was felt only through clusters of blossoming <s>pāṭala</s> and other flowers.
As if turned away from You, bearing a heavy weight of heat,
drying up the inner mud like [the heat of] Your worship,
with an upward-rising flood of intense radiance like Your arms —
You passed the hot season in the <s>Yamunā</s>'s environs.
Then, with masses of clouds whose splendor matched Your body,
with the play of bright, spotless lightning resembling Your yellow garment,
You passed the rainy season that delights all beings of the world,
dwelling freely in the caves of the mountains.
The great king of mountains (<s>Govardhana</s>), with You dwelling in his caverns — the supreme one —
performed hymns of praise with the fresh cries of his flocks of peacocks,
and presenting an offering of flowers from clusters of blooming <s>kuṭaja</s> and <s>kadamba</s>,
he served You with devotion, O God — that <s>Govardhana</s>!
Then, honoring the autumn that had arrived — its waters clear
like the hearts of Your devotees — in the forests,
beautifully herding the cows in the spotless forest-edge and meadows —
O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, grant me bodily well-being!
Your form, tender as a fresh rain-cloud, milking forth love, enchanting all beings,
being the essence of <s>Brahman</s>-truth, pure consciousness, and bliss — beholding it, the women swooned daily.
With minds agitated by love, ever delighting in beholding You from everywhere,
the <s>gopīs</s> could not bear, O <s>Hari</s>, even Your going to the forest at the start of day.
When You went out, the doe-eyed ones, casting their gaze upon You,
with minds fixed on You, hearing the sound of Your flute from afar, they delighted in narrating Your pastimes.
You too, having gone to the forest's interior, standing upon the beautiful, soft ground,
with feet crossed, filled the flute.
That flute-song of Yours, O Lord, agitated the hosts of celestial women like the arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (Love),

children.text: drāvaṇaṃ ca dṛṣadāmapi prabho! tāvakaṃ vyajani veṇukūjitam //
children.translated_text: while the animals, birds, and cattle remained unmoved — and it could melt even stones.
Your fingers dancing on the flute's holes, Your foot-leaf swaying in rhythm —

children.text: tat sthitaṃ tava parokṣamapyaho saṃvicintyā mumuhurvrajāṅganāḥ //
children.translated_text: that posture, even though unseen, when the <s>Vraja</s> women merely imagined it, they swooned.
The sky-roaming women who freely beheld Your limbs, the birds, deer, and cattle,

children.text: tvatpadapraṇayi kānanaṃ ca tā dhanyadhanyamiti nanvamānaya //
children.translated_text: and the forest devoted to Your feet — they considered all these blessed, most blessed!
'When shall I drink the nectar of His lips? Even once, the residue of the taste enjoyed by the flute!'

children.text: dūrato bata kṛtaṃ durāśayetyākulā muhurimāḥ samāmuhan //
children.translated_text: 'Alas, far be such vain hopes!' — thus bewildered, they repeatedly fainted.
Day after day, the women, by the favor arising from the god of Love born of the mind,
bound by helpless passion toward You, O Lord, constantly fell into a state of neglect of their duties.

children.text: rāgastāvajjāyate hi svabhāvānmokṣopāye yatnataḥ syānna vā syāt /
children.translated_text: Passionate attachment arises naturally, whereas the means to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) may or may not come through effort;

children.text: tāsāṃ tvekaṃ tad dvayaṃ labdhamāsīd bhāgyaṃ bhāgyaṃ pāhi māṃ māryteśa! //
children.translated_text: for these [<s>gopīs</s>], both were obtained at once — what fortune, what fortune! Protect me, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>!
With hearts tormented by love, daily, with longing for servitude at Your pair of feet,
the doe-eyed ones worshipped <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), [making] a sand [image] on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: tava nāmakathāratāḥ samaṃ sudṛśaḥ prātarupāgatā nadīm /
children.translated_text: The beautiful women, devoted to the recitation of Your names and stories, came together at dawn to the river,
and worshipped with hundreds of offerings, [praying]: 'May the son of <s>Nanda</s> become our beloved!'
Having observed their vow for a month, seeing those doe-eyed ones, You,
tender with compassion, came to the riverbank with the wish to bless them.
At the conclusion of their observance, having removed their own garments at the bank,
they were absorbed in playing in the <s>Yamunā</s>'s waters — and seeing You before them, they were ashamed.
Then, while the women stood with faces bowed in modesty, You seized their heap of garments nearby

children.text: nihitaṃ parigṛhya bhūruho viṭapaṃ taṃ tarasādhirūḍhavān //
children.translated_text: and quickly climbed up the branch of a tree.

children.text: iha tāvadupetya nīyatāṃ vasanaṃ vaḥ sudṛśo! yathāyatham /
children.translated_text: 'Come here and take your garments, O beautiful ones, each one [her own]' —

children.text: iti narmamṛdusmite tvayi vruvati vyāmumuhe vadhūjanaiḥ //
children.translated_text: when You spoke thus with a gentle, playful smile, the young women were bewildered.

children.text: ayi jīva ciraṃ kiśora! nastava dāsīravaśīkaroṣi kim /
children.translated_text: 'O youth, may you live long! Why do you subdue us who are your servants?
Give us our garments, O lotus-eyed one!' — thus addressed, You merely smiled.

children.text: adhiruhya taṭaṃ kṛtāñjalīḥ pariśuddhāḥ svagatīrnirīkṣya tāḥ /
children.translated_text: When they climbed the bank with folded hands, seeing them purified and devoted to You,
You gave them all their garments, and with joy bestowed Your grace and these words as well:

children.text: viditaṃ nanu vo manīṣitaṃ vaditārastviha yogyamuttaram /
children.translated_text: 'Your heart's desire is known to Me; I shall give a fitting reply in due time —
on moonlit nights, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>' — thus You spoke to the women.
Hearing the honey-dripping words flowing from Your mouth, the doe-eyed ones,

children.text: praṇayādayi vīkṣya vīkṣya te vadanābjaṃ śanakairgṛhaṃ gatāḥ //
children.translated_text: lovingly gazing again and again at the lotus of Your face, slowly returned home.
Having thus blessed the cowherd women, wandering in the forest as before,

children.text: karuṇāśiśiro hare! hara tvarayā me sakalāmayāvalim //
children.translated_text: O <s>Hari</s>, whose head is [cool] with compassion, swiftly take away the whole series of my ailments!

children.text: tataśca bṛndāvanato'tidūrato vanaṃ gatastvaṃ khalu gopagokulaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, from <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, You went to a forest very far away, together with the cowherd hosts and cattle,
bearing within Your heart the desire to bless a group of devotional <s>brāhmaṇa</s> wives.

children.text: tato nirīkṣyāśaraṇe vanāntare kiśoralokaṃ kṣudhitaṃ tṛṣākulam /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the band of youths hungry and distressed with thirst in the pathless forest,

children.text: udūrato yajñaparān dvijān prati vyasarjayo dīdiviyācanāya tān //
children.translated_text: You sent them to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> nearby who were engaged in sacrifice, to beg for food.
When those boys went and, mentioning Your name, asked for cooked rice, O Lord,
those great <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, though established in the Vedas, displayed deafness and said nothing.

children.text: anādarāt khinnadhiyo hi bālakāḥ samāyayuryuktamidaṃ hi yajvasu /
children.translated_text: The boys, disheartened by the disregard, returned — this was fitting for those sacrificers;

children.text: cirādabhaktāḥ khalu te mahīsurāḥ kathaṃ hi bhaktaṃ tvayi taiḥ samarpyate //
children.translated_text: for those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> had long been without devotion — how could they offer food to You?

children.text: nivedayadhvaṃ gṛhiṇījanāya māṃ diśeyurannaṃ karuṇākulā imāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Tell the wives — they, filled with compassion, will give you food' —

children.text: iti smitārdraṃ bhavateritā gatāste dārakā dārajanaṃ yayācire //
children.translated_text: thus, with a gentle smile, at Your urging, the boys went and entreated the wives.

children.text: gṛhītanāmni tvayi sambhramākulāścaturvidhaṃ bhojyarasaṃ pragṛhya tāḥ /
children.translated_text: When Your name was mentioned, the [wives], overcome with excitement, grasping the four kinds of delicacies,
having long held the desire to behold You, even though restrained by their husbands, came swiftly.
With the dancing peacock-feather in Your hair, the gleaming earrings on Your cheeks, the tender gaze,

children.text: nidhāya bāhuṃ suhṛdaṃsasīmani sthitaṃ bhavantaṃ samalokayanta tāḥ //
children.translated_text: with an arm resting on a companion's shoulder — they beheld You thus standing.

children.text: tadā ca kācit tvadupāgamodyatā gṛhītahastā dayitena yajvanā /
children.translated_text: Then, one among them, who was about to come to You but was seized by the hand by her sacrificer-husband,

children.text: tadaiva sañcintya bhavantamañjasā viveśa kaivalpamaho kṛtinyasau //
children.translated_text: instantly meditating upon You, entered <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation) — ah, what a blessed one she was!
Receiving the foods and blessing them, sending them back — those who were reluctant to leave Your bodily presence — home,

children.text: vilokya yajñāya visarjayannimāścakartha bhart napi tāsvagarhaṇān //
children.translated_text: You ensured no reproach fell upon them from their husbands.

children.text: nirūpya doṣaṃ nijamaṅganājane vilokya bhaktiṃ ca punarvicāribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Perceiving their own fault regarding the women, and seeing [their wives'] devotion, those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
upon reflection, having awakened to the truth, praised You. O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, ward off my diseases!
One day, seeing the cowherds engaged in preparing for the worship of <s>Indra</s> with their offerings of abundance,
You, O <s>Śauri</s>, with the intention of shattering <s>Indra</s>'s pride,
though knowing everything, with gentle modesty asked <s>Nanda</s> and the other cowherds:

children.text: napṛcchaḥ ko vāyaṃ janaka! bhavatāmudyama iti //
children.translated_text: 'What is this endeavor of yours, O father?'

children.text: babhāṣe nandastvāṃ suta! nanu vidheyo maghavato
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> replied to You: 'Son, the sacrifice to <s>Indra</s> must be performed

children.text: makho varṣe varṣe sukhayati sa varṣeṇa pṛthivīm /
children.translated_text: year after year; he gladdens the earth with rain;
all that is lived upon on the great earth depends on rain.'
especially our cattle, whose lives depend on grass and water.'

children.text: iti śrutvā vācaṃ piturayi bhavānāha sarasaṃ
children.translated_text: Hearing Your father's words, You spoke charmingly, O Lord:
'Shame on this! It is not true that <s>Indra</s> produces the rain.',

children.text: adṛṣṭaṃ jīvānāṃ sṛjati khalu vṛṣṭiṃ samucitāṃ
children.translated_text: 'It is the unseen <s>karma</s> (fate) of beings that produces appropriate rainfall;
in the great forest, what offering do the trees give to <s>Indra</s>?'

children.text: idaṃ tāvat satyaṃ yadiha paśapo naḥ kuladhanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'This at least is true: if cattle-herding is our family's livelihood,
then the offering should properly be made to the mountain-lord, who supports our livelihood.'
'The earth-deities (<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>) are surely superior even to the gods on the face of the earth,
and therefore they too should be worshipped' — thus You addressed Your own people.
Hearing Your words, held in high esteem, those cowherds,
worshipping the chief <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, gave offerings lavishly to the mountain-lord.
They performed circumambulation most devotedly, offering food with respect,
and You, assuming the form of the mountain, consumed all the offerings before the <s>Ābhīras</s> (cowherds).

children.text: avocaścaivaṃ tān kimiha vitathaṃ me nigaditaṃ
children.translated_text: And You said to them: 'Was anything I said untrue?
This lord of mountains indeed consumes the offering given to him in his own form.

children.text: ayaṃ gotro gotradviṣi ca kupite rakṣitumalaṃ
children.translated_text: This mountain-protector (<s>Gotra</s>) is able to protect all when the mountain-splitter (<s>Indra</s>) is angered' —
thus told, all the inhabitants of <s>Gokula</s> rejoiced.
The dwellers of <s>Vraja</s>, having departed fully satisfied, accompanied by You, returned to <s>Vraja</s>;
but meanwhile, hearing of the disruption of his own sacrifice,
<s>Indra</s>, the king of the gods, though knowing You, his heart overcome by excessive <s>rajas</s>,
could not bear it — even though the affront was arranged by You Yourself.
'Even the slayer of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), having taken on human form, if he promotes insolence among the gods,
then the glory of the celestial assembly is utterly destroyed.',
'Therefore I shall destroy the prosperity of this wretched cowherd' —

children.text: pravṛttastvāṃ jetuṃ sa kila maghavā durmadanidhiḥ //
children.translated_text: thus <s>Indra</s>, that treasury of vile pride, set out to conquer You.
To destroy Your abode, dispatching the doomsday-clouds across the sky,
wielding the thunderbolt, riding upon a cloud-elephant,
he set forth, laughed at inwardly by the other [gods] — by fire, wind, and others;
O Lord of the Three Worlds, does not Your <s>māyā</s> delude all!
'Even if <s>Indra</s> is angry, by the compassion of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the mercy of the mountain,
there is surely no danger for us' — thus reassuring the cowherds,

children.text: aho kiṃ nāyāto giribhiditi sañcintya nivasan
children.translated_text: 'Ah, why has the Mountain-Splitter not yet come?' — thinking thus, You remained.
O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! O Slayer of <s>Mura</s>! Ward off my diseases!
At that very moment, clouds were seen, unbroken, with thunder, uproar, and shaking of all directions,
which in beauty rivaled the radiance of Your limbs, hovering over the settlement of <s>Vraja</s>.
With great hailstones and torrents of rain falling
in every direction, when the circle of cowherds was being battered,
hearing their words — 'Save us, O angry <s>Hari</s>! Save us!' —
You, O Unconquered One, said: 'Fear not!'

children.text: kula iha khalu gotro daivataṃ gotraśatror-
children.translated_text: 'Our family's deity is indeed the mountain-protector (<s>Gotra</s>), and he can ward off

children.text: vihatimiha sa rundhyat ko nuḥ vaḥ saṃśaayo'smin /
children.translated_text: the assault of the Mountain-Splitter (<s>Indra</s>) — what doubt have you in this?'
Thus speaking with a smile, O Lord, <s>Govardhana</s> mountain
You swiftly uprooted from its base with Your two arms, O Child!
Then, when the great mountain had been lifted up,
on a sandy, soft spot, far from the rain-fire,
sheltering the cattle and cowherds with their belongings beneath it,
You held the mountain aloft with Your lotus-palm.
While You held the mountain, with the cowherd girls and Your companions
enjoying play and sportive conversation,
with the cows gathered close, as You scratched them with one hand,
all the cowherds were supremely content.

children.text: atimahān girireṣu tu vāmake karasaroruhi taṃ dharate ciram /
children.translated_text: This immense mountain, held on Your left lotus-hand, borne for a long time —
'What is this wonder? Is it the mountain's own strength?' — thus said the cowherds gazing at You.
'Alas! That impudent boy will set down the mountain when his arm grows weary!' —
thus <s>Indra</s>, harboring contempt for You, poured rain furiously for seven days.

children.text: acalati tvayi deva! padāt padaṃ galitasarvajale ca ghanotkare /
children.translated_text: When You, O Lord, did not move even a step, and all the water had drained from the cloud-masses,
removed by the Wind (<s>Marut</s>), the Lord of the <s>Maruts</s> (<s>Indra</s>), his mind now fearful of You, came running in haste.

children.text: śamamupeyuṣi varṣabhare tadā paśupadhenukule ca vinirgate /
children.translated_text: When the burden of rain had subsided, and the herds of cattle and cowherds had emerged,

children.text: bhuvi vibho! samupāhitabhūdharaḥ pramuditaiḥ paśupaiḥ parirebhiṣe //
children.translated_text: You set down the mountain on the earth, O Lord, and were embraced by the delighted cowherds.

children.text: dharaṇimeva purā dhṛtavānasi kṣitidharoddharaṇe tava kaḥ śramaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You who bore the Earth itself before — what effort is the lifting of a mountain for You?' —

children.text: iti nutastridaśaiḥ kumalāpate! gurupurālaya! pālaya māṃ gadāt //
children.translated_text: thus praised by the gods, O Lord of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>)! O Dweller of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Protect me from disease!
Having witnessed Your power in the lifting of the mountain and such deeds, the cowherd-folk,
regarding You as the Lord of all the universe, <s>Nanda</s> inquired about Your birth-horoscope.

children.text: gargodito nirgadito nijāya vargāya tātena tava prabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The glory of You, as told by <s>Garga</s>, was narrated by Your father to his own people;
their love for You, even greater than before, grew heavy with reverence.
Then <s>Indra</s>, the king of the gods, awakened to the truth by his humiliation, together with the divine cow (<s>Surabhī</s>),

children.text: upetya tuṣtāva sa naṣṭagarvaḥ spṛṣṭvā padābjaṃ maṇimaulinā te //
children.translated_text: approached You, and he, his pride destroyed, praised You, touching Your lotus feet with his jeweled crown.
<s>Surabhī</s>, with love-dripping breasts, bathed You — now bearing the name <s>Govinda</s> — with her milk;
and <s>Indra</s> too, joyful, bathed You with the sacred waters of the divine <s>Gaṅgā</s> brought by <s>Airāvata</s>.
When You, the Lord of the three worlds, were consecrated as Lord of <s>Gokula</s>,

children.text: noke'pi vaikuṇṭhapade'pyalabhyāṃ śriyaṃ prapede bhavataḥ prabhāvāt //
children.translated_text: the cowherd settlement attained a glory unobtainable even in heaven or <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, by Your power.
Once, Your father, bathing in the early morning within the <s>Yamunā</s>, was seized by a servant of <s>Varuṇa</s>

children.text: nītastamānetumagāḥ purīṃ tvaṃ tāṃ vāruṇīṃ kāraṇamartyarūpaḥ //
children.translated_text: and taken away; You went to <s>Varuṇa</s>'s city to bring him back, in the guise of a mortal for a cosmic purpose.

children.text: sasambhramaṃ tena jalādhipena prapūjitastvaṃ pratigṛhya tātam /
children.translated_text: Worshipped hurriedly by that Lord of Waters, You received Your father
and returned home in an instant; Your father told his people about the experience.
Having ascertained You to be <s>Hari</s>, those who were bound by the thirst to behold Your abode —

children.text: nirīkṣya viṣṇo! paramaṃ padaṃ tad durāpamanyaistvamadīdṛśastān //
children.translated_text: O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, You showed them that supreme state, unattainable by others.
In the great ocean of absolute liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>), filled with the overflowing current of supreme bliss,

children.text: ciraṃ nimagnāḥ khalu gopasaṅghāstvayaiva bhūman! punaruddhṛtāste //
children.translated_text: the cowherd-folk were indeed long submerged, and then uplifted again by You alone, O Supreme One!
'Like a berry in the hand — where, O Lord, in any incarnation,
has Your own abode, unattainable [to others], been shown to the devoted?' —

children.text: tadiha paśuparūpī tvaṃ hi sākṣāt parātman!
children.translated_text: Indeed, here in cowherd-form, You, O Supreme Self, are directly manifest!
O Dweller of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Protect me from diseases!
When the period of the vow was over, what You had promised to the <s>gopī</s> women,
You then set about to fulfill — the festival of love (<s>Madanotsava</s>).
In the dense moonlight that cooled all directions,
You filled Your flute at the edge of the <s>Yamunā</s> forest.
With its ascending scales and melodious tonal patterns,
enchanting the entire space between the worlds,
hearing that flute-song of Yours, O Lord, the young women
experienced an indescribable bewilderment of mind.
They — engaged in household duties, attached to their children,
serving their husbands, those lotus-eyed ones —
abandoning all, enchanted by the sound of the flute,
O You of beautiful form! — assembled at the forest's edge.
Some, while adorning their own bodies,
hearing the flute-song, left with ornaments only half put on;
but those who came to You thus half-adorned
appeared even more beautiful to Your eyes.
One, wearing her necklace on her hips

children.text: kāñcīṃ ca kaṇṭhabhuvi deva! samāgatā tvām /
children.translated_text: and her waist-chain on her neck, came to You, O Lord;
the charm of her own hips, O <s>Mukunda</s>,
seemed to speak to You — she who was especially naive and happy.
Another, with her bodice unfastened on her bosom,
unnoticed by the other wives in her bewilderment,
came to You, bearing the overflowing burden of incomparable love,
like a vessel-bearer for the consecration ceremony of the kingdom [of love].
Some, unable even to go forth from their homes,
O Lord, meditating upon You firmly in their hearts,
abandoning their bodies, entered You alone,
the one whose form is the bliss of transcendent consciousness — those most blessed among the blessed!
Though remembering You not as the Supreme Self but as a lover,
those women attained the state of the supreme <s>Paramahaṃsas</s> (liberated sages) in an instant!
If one somehow holds You — the manifest form of the Supreme Self — in one's mind,
one would effortlessly attain immortality.
Surrounded on all sides by the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s> who had come to You,
Your face softened with a gentle smile, gazing with compassionate eyes,
a boundless ocean of beauty, being beheld —
O You who are the sole delight of the entire universe! O Supreme Lord, remove my diseases!
To those beautiful women who had come, helpless under the arrows of <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the Love-god),

children.text: abhivāñchitaṃ vidhātuṃ kṛtamatirapi tā jagātha vāmamiva //
children.translated_text: though resolved to grant their desire, You spoke as if contrarily.
You spoke of the <s>dharma</s> of virtuous wives, so as to let the hosts of sages hovering in the sky hear;

children.text: dharmyaṃ khalu te vacanaṃ karma tu no nirmalasya viśvāsyam //
children.translated_text: Your words were indeed righteous, but the conduct of one who is stainless is [itself] the trustworthy [teaching].

children.text: ākarṇya te pratīpāṃ vāṇīmeṇīdṛśaḥ paraṃ dīnāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing Your contrary words, those doe-eyed women, utterly distressed,
cried for a long time: 'O Ocean of Compassion! Do not, do not forsake us!'
Your mind filled with compassion by their weeping and pleading, O Slayer of <s>Mura</s>,
You proceeded to delight fully in love with them on the banks of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
On the pathways along the moonlit, beautiful banks of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
You sat on a bed prepared from the <s>gopīs</s>' upper garments.
With most sweet, playful conversations, with clasping of hands, and the delights of kissing,
with intense embraces, You enchanted the assembly of women.
On the day of the stealing of garments, what had been promised to those women
regarding the return of their garments — that too, O Lord, You fulfilled for those whose hearts were overcome by passion.
With a sprout of <s>dharma</s> appearing, with a face-lotus bearing a smile gentle as <s>kunda</s> flowers,
O son of <s>Nanda</s>! embracing You, the most beautiful in the three worlds, the young women were delighted.
In separation You are like fire; in union You are all passion (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>);
yet even more fiery in union — this is indeed wondrous!
I worship You, who were eager for the tight embrace of <s>Rādhā</s>'s lofty breasts —
O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Pacify all my ailments!
With You, whose essence is the overflowing nectar of supreme bliss, having experienced
the play of amorous delight, those lotus-eyed women attained a boundless flood of joy and great exhilaration.
'This beloved Lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), the enchanter of all the world's minds, hides in me, in me alone!' —

children.text: itisma sarvāḥ kalitābhimānā nirīkṣya govinda! tirohito'bhūḥ //
children.translated_text: beholding all of them thus seized with pride, O <s>Govinda</s>, You vanished!
O Slayer of <s>Mura</s>, You took with You <s>Rādhā</s> — Your most beloved cowherd-wife, who was free of such pride —

children.text: bhavānupādāya gato vidūraṃ tayā saha svairavihārakārī //
children.translated_text: and went far away with her, engaging in free-spirited sport.

children.text: tirohite'tha tvayi jātatāpāḥ samaṃ sametāḥ kamalāyatākṣyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, when You vanished, the lotus-eyed women, their hearts burning with longing,
gathering together, searched for You in forest after forest and fell into immeasurable despair, O <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text: hā cūta! hā campaka! karṇikāra! hā mallike! mālati! bālavallyaḥ! /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Cūta</s> (mango) tree! O <s>Campaka</s>! O <s>Karṇikāra</s>! O <s>Mallikā</s> (jasmine)! O <s>Mālatī</s>! O young creepers!

children.text: kiṃ vīkṣito no hṛdayaikacora ityādi tāstvatpravaṇā vilepuḥ //
children.translated_text: Have you seen our heart's sole thief?' — thus, devoted to You, they wept.
'Friend, I have seen this lotus-eyed one right before me!' — one, crying out in agitation,

children.text: tvāṃ bhāvanācakṣuṣi vīkṣya kācit tāpaṃ sakhīnāṃ dviguṇīcakāra //
children.translated_text: beholding You with the eye of imagination, doubled the anguish of her companions.
Identified with You, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, they enacted Your very deeds;

children.text: vicitya bhūyo'pi tathaiva mānāt tvayā viyuktāṃ dadṛśuśca rādhām //
children.translated_text: searching further, they likewise found <s>Rādhā</s>, abandoned by You out of pride.

children.text: tataḥ samaṃ tā vipine samantāt tamovatārāvadhi mārgayantyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, all together, searching everywhere in the forest until darkness descended,
gathering again on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, they wept profusely and sang of Your virtues.
When the minds of the women of <s>Vraja</s> were thus overwhelmed with anguish,
O sole Ocean of Compassion — You, whose enchanting form enchants even the enchanter of the three worlds, appeared with a gentle smile!

children.text: sandigdhasandharśanamātmakāntaṃ tvāṃ vīkṣya tanvyaḥ sahasā tadānīm /
children.translated_text: Beholding You, their beloved, whose appearance had been uncertain, those slender women at that moment

children.text: kiṃ kiṃ na cakruḥ pramadātibhārāt sa tvaṃ gadāt pālaya māruteśa! //
children.translated_text: — what did they not do in their excess of joy! — O You! Protect me from disease, O Lord of the Winds!
Upon seeing You, O Lotus-Eyed One, the <s>gopī</s>-women, overwhelmed with ecstasy,
as if drenched in a stream of nectar, stood motionless before You.

children.text: tadanu kācana tvatkarāmbujaṃ sapadi gṛhṇatī nirviśaṅkitam /
children.translated_text: Then one among them, unhesitatingly seizing Your lotus-hand —

children.text: ghanapayodhare sannidhāya sā pulakasaṃvṛtā tasthuṣī ciram //
children.translated_text: she, covered with horripilation, stood long near Your cloud-like, full chest.

children.text: tava vibho! purā komalaṃ bhujaṃ nijagalāntare paryaveṣṭayat /
children.translated_text: O Lord! A certain one wrapped Your tender arm around her own neck,
as if restraining the vital breath rising in her throat — so overjoyed was she.

children.text: apagatatrapā kāpi kāminī tava mukhāmbujāt pūgacarvitam /
children.translated_text: Some shameless lover-woman received the betel-chewing from Your lotus-face,

children.text: pratigṛhayya tad vaktrapaṅkaje nidadhatī gatā pūrṇakāmatām //
children.translated_text: and placing it in her own lotus-mouth, attained the fullness of desire.

children.text: vikaruṇo vane saṃvihāya māmapagato'si kā tvāmi spṛśet /
children.translated_text: 'You went away heartlessly, abandoning me in the forest — who [else] would touch You?' —

children.text: iti saroṣayā tavadekayā sajalalocanaṃ vīkṣito bhavān //
children.translated_text: thus by one [<s>gopī</s>], with anger, You were gazed upon with tear-filled eyes.
Thus, accompanied by the joy-overwhelmed cowherd women, having arrived at the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
You shone, seated upon a seat fashioned from their soft bodice-cloths, radiant with saffron.

children.text: katividhā kṛpā ke'pi sarvato dhṛtadayodayāḥ kecidāśrite /
children.translated_text: 'How manifold is [Your] compassion! Some are always full of mercy toward all; some only toward those who take refuge;
and some are thus [merciful] even toward ones like us' — so were You addressed by the cowherd women.

children.text: ayi kumārikā! naiva śaṅkyatāṃ kaṭhinatā mayi premakātare /
children.translated_text: 'O young maidens! Do not suspect any hardheartedness in me, who am overcome with love;

children.text: mayi yu cetaso vo'nuvṛttaye kṛtamidaṃ mayetyucivān bhavān //
children.translated_text: all this was done by me for the sake of winning your hearts' attention' — thus You spoke.

children.text: ayi niśamyatāṃ jīvavallabhāḥ! priyatamo jano nedṛśo mama /
children.translated_text: 'O life-beloved ones! Listen — no person is dearer to me than you;
therefore, let us sport here in these delightful nights without obstruction' — thus was Your speech, O Lord!
Thus, with these words and more, You sported with the cowherd women rich in delight,

children.text: kalitakautuko rāsakhelane gurupurīpate! pāhi māṃ gadāt //
children.translated_text: full of eagerness in the <s>Rāsa</s> dance — O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, protect me from disease!
With a peacock-feather plume held in Your tresses, with swinging <s>makara</s> (crocodile) earrings,
adorned with necklaces, garlands, and forest-flower wreaths, with a dense fragrance of body-ointment,
wearing a yellow garment with a tinkling girdle, with radiant gem-studded anklets —
we contemplate Your form adorned for the <s>Rāsa</s> dance, O Lord!
When the circle of young women had donned their ornaments, with bodice-clad rounded breasts,
with gem earrings swinging on their cheeks, in the complete circle [of dancers],
moving between each pair of beautiful women, O Consort of <s>Indirā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>),
You then commenced the charming <s>Rāsa</s> dance, O Lotus-eyed One!
O <s>Vāsudeva</s>! The radiant fragrance of the <s>Rāsa</s> dance being celebrated here,
having learned of it from afar through <s>Nārada</s>'s report, filled with curiosity,
surrounded by hundreds of <s>Apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs) lovely in attire, ornaments, and graceful play,
the host of gods came down simultaneously from heaven, alighting swiftly in the sky.
With the arrangement of melody, donation [of beats], and rhythm created by the flute-song,
the enchanting, gentle foot-falls creating the beat — charming to behold,
with bangles jingling on the hands, and lotus-hands now and then draped over shoulders,
with garments swaying on rounded hips — worship the splendor of the <s>Rāsa</s> dance!
With the sweet high-pitched melody of the harmonious singing done with devotion,
in the dance, with the gem-ornaments and necklaces swaying on the gracefully moving limbs,
the host of celestials, showering flowers in rapture, opened their eyes wide,
and together with their consorts became utterly enchanted, as if dissolving into You, who are pure consciousness.
Then a certain cowherd woman, her tender vine-like body perspiring,
leaned upon Your beloved shoulder, with eyes half-closed from the burden of fatigue;
another, with loosened tresses, under the pretext [of embracing],
kissed Your arm — fragrant with fresh sandal-paste — from which hair stood on end.
One, placing her cheek near Yours, with her earring trembling upon her cheek,
— a treasury of accumulated merit — received the nectar of the betel-chewing from Your mouth;
in the course of the dance, having attained You — the playground of <s>Indirā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), the beauty of the world —
what state of ecstatic rapture did the women not reach!
O Lord! The singing gradually ceased, the accompaniment of instruments stopped —
the women, overwhelmed with the rapture of <s>Brahman</s>, simply danced in the arena;

children.text: nāvidannapi ca nīvikāṃ kimapi kuntalīmapi ca kañculīṃ
children.translated_text: they were unaware of their girdle-knots, their braids, or their bodices,

children.text: jyotiṣāmapi kadambakaṃ divi vilambitaṃ kimaparaṃ bruve //
children.translated_text: even the constellations hung suspended in the sky — what more shall I say!

children.text: modasīmni bhuvanaṃ vilāpya vihṛtiṃ samāpya ca tato vibho!
children.translated_text: Having brought the world to the pinnacle of delight and having concluded the play, O Lord,
of the cowherd women — whose bodies were beautiful with drops of fresh perspiration from the exertion of play,
whose minds were unable to bear [the force of] desire — prompted by their merit,
You then assumed forms [equal to their number] and bestowed the supreme festival of the heroism of love.
With those beloved women, tenderly caressed, delighting in various modes of play,

children.text: svairamīśa! nanu sūrajāpayasi cāru nāma vihṛtiṃ vyadhāḥ /
children.translated_text: freely, O Lord, You sported beautifully in the waters of the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>);
and in the forest too — enchanting with its cool, gentle young breezes,
and fragrant with blossoms — You reclined, captivating hundreds of beauties.

children.text: kāminīriti hi yāminīṣu khalu kāmanīyakanidhe! bhavān
children.translated_text: Thus, O Treasury of all that is beautiful, with these loving women in those nights,
experiencing some ocean full of the essence of perfect rapture, accessible [only] to <s>yogins</s>,
honoring even <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, and others in these cowherd women,
O You whose form is accessible to the devoted, O Charming One, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — protect me!
After You had thus sported with Your beloveds, steeped in <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic delight), the cowherds
once again went to the forest of <s>Ambikā</s> for <s>Ambikā</s>'s festival;

children.text: sametya bhavatā samaṃ niśi niṣevya divyotsavaṃ
children.translated_text: having gathered with You at night and celebrated the divine festival,
they slept happily — but then a fierce serpent swallowed the cowherd chief (<s>Nanda</s>).
When that [serpent], though struck with firebrands, forcefully would not release him, they fell at Your feet [crying] 'Save us! Save us!' —

children.text: damuñcati bhavatpade nyapati pāhi pāhīti taiḥ /
children.translated_text: then indeed You approached with Your foot and touched him;

children.text: tadā khalu padā bhavān samupagamya pasparśa taṃ
children.translated_text: and he, abandoning his serpent form, appeared in his own <s>Vidyādhara</s> body and shone.

children.text: babhau sa ca nijāṃ tanuṃ samupasādya vaidyādharīm //
children.translated_text: 'O bearer of the <s>Sudarśana</s> (disc), O Lord! I am indeed named <s>Sudarśana</s>;
I once offended the <s>Siddhas</s>, and they made me a serpent here;

children.text: sunīn kvacidapāhasaṃ ta iha māṃ vyadhurvāhasam /
children.translated_text: by the offering of Your feet, I have attained purity' — thus he
praised [You] and departed to his own realm; and the cowherds too returned to <s>Vraja</s> with joy.

children.text: stuvan nijapadaṃ yayau vrajapadaṃ ca gopā mudā //
children.translated_text: Once, while You were sporting with the women along with <s>Halī</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>),

children.text: kadāpi khalu sīriṇā viharati tvayi strījanair-
children.translated_text: that follower of <s>Kubera</s> called <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s> abducted the women.
Pursuing him swiftly, You then — having freed the women —
slew him and gave his crest-jewel to the bearer of the plough (<s>Balarāma</s>).
And during those days, absorbed in play in the forests with Your dear friends,

children.text: dineṣu ca suhṛjjanaiḥ saha vaneṣu līlāparaṃ
children.translated_text: O captivator of <s>Manmatha</s>'s (the love-god's) heart, the nectar of Your melodious flute-song —
the <s>gopīs</s>, thinking of You who bestowed the end-of-fast offering of nectar to the eyes of the immortals,
scorched by the heat of separation — what laments did they not utter!
Then a certain servant of the lord of the <s>Bhojas</s> (<s>Kaṃsa</s>), of cruel, wicked gaze, named <s>Ariṣṭa</s>,
of fearsome form, bellowing hideously,
stood before You in the form of a bull.
Then this mighty one, bearing the earth-shaking greatness of a <s>Śākvara</s> [metre],

children.text: paṅktimāśu parighūrṇya paśūnāṃ chandasāṃ nidhimavāpa bhavantam //
children.translated_text: swiftly scattering the herds of cattle, encountered You, the repository of all the metres (<s>Chandas</s>).
Seizing him who charged with lowered lofty horns,
You crushed that demon of [deceptively] fine form but evil nature, and delighted the world of the gods.
'Wonderful! Today, O Lord, from the slaying of the bull, the stability of <s>Vṛṣa</s> (righteousness) on earth is well-established in [Your] reign,

children.text: vardhate ca vṛṣacetasi bhūyānmoda ityabhinuto'si surastvam //
children.translated_text: and in the heart of the righteous, ever-greater joy increases!' — thus were You praised by the gods.
'O bulls! Run far away! Behold this bull-slayer here!' —
thus, with laughter along with the cowherds, You went home — O Lord of <s>Vātapura</s> (Guruvāyūr), protect me!

children.text: yatneṣu sarveṣvapi nāvakeśī keśī sa bhojeśituriṣṭabandhuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Keśī</s>, that dearest ally of the lord of the <s>Bhojas</s> (<s>Kaṃsa</s>), [thinking] 'in all efforts the Mane-bearer [has failed],'

children.text: tvaṃ sindhujāvāpya itīva matvā saṃprāptavān sindhujavājirūpaḥ //
children.translated_text: as if thinking 'If you obtain the Ocean-born one (<s>Lakṣmī</s>)' — arrived in the form of an ocean-born horse.
This one, though having attained <s>Gandharva</s> status, with his harsh neighing terrified all beings,

children.text: bhavadvilokāvadhi gopavāṭīṃ pramardya pāpaḥ punarā patat tvām //
children.translated_text: and having ravaged the cowherd settlement — until he saw You — the wicked one charged at You again.

children.text: tārkṣyārpitāṅghrestava tārkṣya eṣa cikṣepa vakṣobhuvi nāma pādam /
children.translated_text: He, placing his foot upon Your foot [dedicated to] <s>Garuḍa</s> — this one indeed was a <s>Garuḍa</s> [of sorts] — planted his hoof upon Your chest;

children.text: bhṛgoḥ padāghātakathaṃ niśamya svenāpi śakyaṃ taditīva mohāt //
children.translated_text: as if, hearing the story of <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s kick [on <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s chest], [thinking] 'I too can do this!' — out of delusion.

children.text: pravañcayannasya khurāñcalaṃ drāgamuṃ ca vikṣepitha dūradūram /
children.translated_text: Swiftly dodging his hoof-edge, You hurled him far, far away;
though stunned, he charged at You again to devour [You], his fury revived despite the blow.

children.text: tvaṃ vāhadaṇḍe kṛtadhīśca bāhādaṇḍaṃ nyadhāstasya mukhe tadānīm /
children.translated_text: You, having resolved on [using] the arm as a weapon, thrust Your arm into his mouth;
his breath blocked by its swelling, his life departed — though a horse, he attained unity [with You].

children.text: ālambhamātreṇa paśoḥ surāṇāṃ prasādake nūtna ivāśvamedhe /
children.translated_text: Merely by the touching of the [sacrificial] animal, You, the bestower of grace upon the gods, performed as it were a novel <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice);

children.text: kṛte tvayā harṣavaśāt surendrāstvāṃ tuṣṭuṣuḥ keśavanāmadheyam //
children.translated_text: and in their joy, the king of the gods and others praised You with the name <s>Keśava</s>.

children.text: kaṃsāya te śaurisutatvamuktvā taṃ tadvadhotkaṃ pratirudhya vācā /
children.translated_text: Having told <s>Kaṃsa</s> of Your being the son of <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>), and restraining his eagerness for [Your] slaying with words,
the glorious <s>Nārada</s>, arriving at the conclusion of the destruction of <s>Keśī</s>, praised You.

children.text: kadāpi gopaiḥ saha kānanānte nilāyanakrīḍanalolupaṃ tvām /
children.translated_text: Once, when You were eager to play the hiding game with the cowherds at the forest's edge,
the son of <s>Maya</s>, a demon of boundless <s>māyā</s> (illusion) called <s>Vyoma</s>, an obstructor of sky-farers, approached You.
When he pretended to be a guard while the cowherds played thieves, he stole away the cowherd boys and their cattle,

children.text: guhāsu kṛtvā pidadhe śilābhistvayā ca buddhvā parimardito'bhūt //
children.translated_text: concealing them in caves sealed with boulders — but he was discovered by You and crushed.
With such varieties of wondrous sport, causing <s>Vraja</s> to swoon with unparalleled joy
at every step, ever-fresh and boundless — O Supreme Self, O Lord of <s>Pavana</s> (Wind-God), protect me!
Then <s>Kaṃsa</s>, hearing from <s>Nārada</s>'s words that You were a dweller of <s>Vraja</s>,
his heart shattered, summoned the grandson of <s>Gāndinī</s> (<s>Akrūra</s>),
and sent him to bring You, under the pretext of a bow-sacrifice —
O You who recline on the serpent (<s>Śeṣa</s>), O <s>Ahināthaśāyin</s>!
<s>Akrūra</s>, devoted to Your feet for a long time,
his mind unable to bear [the wait for] Your sight, [yet] out of fear of the king,
now, at [<s>Kaṃsa</s>'s] very command, setting out to see You again,
bore an exceedingly great burden of bliss.
That fortunate one, going by chariot to Your dwelling,
savoring the multitude of desires centered upon You,
again and again beseeching fate out of fear that [the desires] might not be fulfilled,
was unaware of anything along the way.
'I shall see that Supreme Person whose gait is praised by hundreds of gods!
Shall I perhaps touch Him? Shall I even embrace Him?

children.text: kiṃ vakṣyate sa khalu māṃ kva nu vīkṣitaḥ syā-
children.translated_text: What will He say to me? Where shall I behold Him?' —
thus, he traversed the road entirely absorbed in You.
Gradually entering <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — purified by Your footsteps,
revered by <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), and the gods —
as if drowned in bliss, as if stuck in rapture,
what state of ecstasy did he not attain, O Lotus-eyed One!
Seeing the places of Your pastimes, he bowed down,
and rolled in the dust marked with Your footprints;

children.text: kiṃ brūmahe bahujanā hi tadāpi jātā
children.translated_text: what shall we say — many indeed have been such [devotees] even then,
but such devotion, O Supreme Self, is rare!
In the evening, seeing the cowherd dwellings — whose ears' nectar was the singing of Your deeds,
flowing with the nectar of Your story —
as if carried along by a river of joy,
he continued on and reached the vicinity of Your dwelling.
There he beheld You — watching for the milking of the cows,
as if awaiting the arrival of the foremost devotee —
O All-pervading One! You, accompanied by Your elder brother, [appeared] within
as though overflowing an ocean of the bliss of the experience of <s>Brahman</s>.
With bodies purified by the special evening bath,
the two of You — charming in yellow and blue garments — were captivating;
not overly adorned yet beautifully attired,
with faces moist with gentle smiles — thus he beheld You both.
Dismounting from the chariot at a distance, as he bowed,
You raised him up — the crest-jewel of the devotee-clan — and then embraced him;
with joy, inquiring about his welfare in words of few syllables,
grasping his hand, You, together with <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), led him to the house.
Having worshipped that <s>Yādava</s> together with <s>Nanda</s>, with boundless regard,
and having heard the tidings spoken by him,
conveying to the cowherds the account of the king's command,
You spent the night here with him, [exchanging] various stories.
'Is he at <s>Candrā</s>'s house, or perhaps at <s>Candrabhāgā</s>'s house?
At <s>Rādhā</s>'s house? Or perhaps at <s>Mitravindā</s>'s dwelling?' —
'The rogue is delaying!' — thus by the young women, loudly
suspected in the night — O Lord of <s>Marutpura</s> (Guruvāyūr), protect me!
Then, hearing the news of Your departure, the cowherd maidens, deeply distressed,

children.text: kimidaṃ kimidaṃ kathaṃ nvitīmāḥ samavetāḥ paridevitānyakurvan //
