children.translated_text: 'What is this? What is this? How can it be?' — gathering together, they began their lamentations.
'How can this <s>Nanda</s>'s son, the ocean of compassion, abandon us who have no other refuge?'

children.text: bata naḥ kimu daivamevamāsīditi tāstvadgatamānasā vilepuḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Alas, what fate befell us thus!' — those women, their minds fixed on You, lamented. //
Departing in the last watch [of the night], together with Your father and Your company of friends,
intending to allay the heavy anguish of the women, You sent forth a single messenger. //

children.text: acirādupayāmi sannidhiṃ vo bhavitā sādhu mayaiva saṅgamaśrīḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I shall come to your presence soon; the glory of union shall be well accomplished by Me alone;
I shall quickly immerse you in an ocean of nectar' — thus consoling, You [encouraged] the young women. //
Laden with sorrow, with longing, gazed upon from afar by the women
to a great distance, gently casting Your side-glances in their direction, together with <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), You departed on <s>Akrūra</s>'s chariot. //

children.text: anasā bahulena vallavānāṃ manasā canugato'tha vallabhānām /
children.translated_text: Followed by the carts in abundance of the cowherds, and in mind by the beloved women,
having passed beyond the forest with its grieving deer and despondent trees, You reached the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>. //

children.text: miyamāya nimajjya vāriṇi tvamabhivīkṣyātha rathe'pi gāndineyaḥ /
children.translated_text: You bathed by plunging into the water; and then <s>Gāndinī</s>'s son (<s>Akrūra</s>), beholding [You] upon the chariot also,

children.text: vivaśo'jani kinnvidaṃ vibhoste nanu citraṃ tvavalokanaṃ samantāt //
children.translated_text: became overwhelmed — 'What is this, O Lord?' — indeed, the sight of You everywhere is no wonder. //

children.text: punareṣa nimajjya puṇyaśālī puruṣaṃ tvāṃ paramaṃ bhumaṅgabhoge /
children.translated_text: That meritorious one, plunging again, [beheld] You, the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, upon the coils of <s>Śeṣa</s>,
radiant with discus, conch, mace, and lotus, surrounded by hosts of gods and <s>Siddhas</s>. //

children.text: sa tadā paramātmasaukhyasindhau vinimagnaḥ praṇuvan prakārabhedaiḥ /
children.translated_text: He, submerged in the ocean of supreme Self-bliss, praising You in various ways,

children.text: avilokya punaśca harṣasindhoranuvṛttyā pulakāvṛto yayau tvām //
children.translated_text: not seeing [You] again, yet from the ocean of joy, overwhelmed with horripilation, went forth to You. //

children.text: kimu śītalimā mahān jale yat pulako'sāviti coditena tena /
children.translated_text: 'Was there great coldness in the water, that this horripilation [arose]?' — being thus asked,

children.text: atiharṣaniruttareṇa sārdhaṃ rathavāsī pavaneśa! pāhi māṃ tvam //
children.translated_text: unable to reply from excess of delight — riding the chariot with him, O Lord of the Wind! Protect me! //
Having reached <s>Mathurā</s> when half the day had passed, lodging there in a garden,
having eaten food, You went with Your companions to see the city.
You reached the royal road — being drawn by the countless chains of merit of
men and women whose curiosity was stirred by long-heard [reports] and eagerness to behold [You]. //
Like the radiance of Your feet, the women who arrived were lovely with passion; like Your form,
they were endowed with gleaming breasts; fickle like Your gaze;
captivating like Your chest; O Lord, confident like Your gentle smile,
sparkling with purity, and graced with peacock-like splendor like the beauty of Your tresses. //
Creating delight for them through the play of sidelong glances, while the people were tossing with joy and wonder,

children.text: vyāloleṣu janeṣu tatra rajakaṃ kañcit paṭīṃ prārthayan /
children.translated_text: there You requested a certain washerman for garments.
'Who will give you royal garments? Away with you!' — thus addressed by him,

children.text: sadyastasya kareṇa śīrṣamahṛthāḥ so'pyāpa puṇyāṃ gatim //
children.translated_text: You instantly severed his head with Your hand — and he too attained an auspicious state. //
Then a certain weaver of broad mind, who with delight gave You garments befitting Your attire —

children.text: dāśvāṃsaṃ svapadaṃ ninetha sukṛtaṃ ko veda jīvātmanām /
children.translated_text: You led him to Your own abode. Who knows the merit of embodied souls?
And a garland-maker, honored with garlands, flower-clusters, and praises,

children.text: bhaktiṃ tena vṛtāṃ dideśitha parāṃ lakṣmīṃ ca lakṣmīpate! //
children.translated_text: You bestowed upon him the devotion he desired, as well as supreme <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity), O Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>! //
Then, seeing on the road <s>Kubjā</s> (the hunchback), lotus-eyed, and when she
offered body-unguent, You applied the unguent well and placed a great [love] in her heart.
Then, to manifest straightness in the one crooked at heart, clearly also in her body,
grasping her beautifully by the chin with Your hand, You raised her up — and she became the beauty of the world! //
Until then, those of established glory, O Lord — people not exceedingly sinful —
offered something according to their capacity — betel, garlands, and such.

children.text: gṛhṇānaḥ kusumādi kiñcana tadā mārge nibaddhāñjalir-
children.translated_text: Accepting some flowers and such, with palms joined on the road,

children.text: nātiṣṭhaṃ bata yato'dya vipulāmārtiṃ vrajāmi prabho! //
children.translated_text: 'I did not stand [thus before You]' — alas, from that day I suffer great distress, O Lord! //
'I shall come' — though released by that unguent-giving woman, O Lord,
she, anxious, watching Your departure from afar — You entered the city gate.
From the announcement, <s>Devakī</s>, inferring Your arrival, overflowing with great joy,
milk flowing from her breasts in torrents — Your fame entered [her heart] within. //
Having entered the festive city, going to the bow-hall,

children.text: mādhuryeṇa nu tejasā nu puruṣairdūreṇa dattāntaraḥ /
children.translated_text: whether by charm or by might, given wide berth by the attendants,
You grasped the excellent bow, adorned and worshipped with garlands — despite the cry 'Do not!' from the guards —
strung it, drew it, and broke it! //
The great sound of the bow's destruction, like the opening drumroll of the festival of <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s destruction
on the morrow — O Lord! — made the gods thrill with horripilation.
<s>Kaṃsa</s> too trembled; and the arisen tumult, aggravated by You
with the roar of the guards struck by the two fierce halves of the broken bow, became tumultuous. //

children.text: śiṣṭairduṣṭajanaiśca dṛṣṭamihimā prītyā ca bhītyā tataḥ
children.translated_text: Your greatness beheld by both the virtuous and the wicked — with love and with fear respectively —

children.text: saṃpaśyan purasampadaṃ pravivaran sāyaṃ gato vāṭikām /
children.translated_text: beholding the city's splendor and exploring it, You returned to the garden at evening.

children.text: śrīdāmnā saha rādhikāvirahajaṃ khedaṃ vadan prasvapa-
children.translated_text: Speaking with <s>Śrīdāman</s> of the sorrow born of separation from <s>Rādhikā</s>, falling asleep,
yet rejoicing at the unfolding of the purpose of Your incarnation — O Lord of the Wind! Protect me! //
In the morning, when the wrestling drums were sounded at the command of the terrified <s>Bhoja</s> king,

children.text: saṅghe rājñāṃ ca mañcānabhiyayuṣi gate nandagope'pi harmyam /
children.translated_text: and when the assembly of kings had ascended the viewing platforms, and <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd too [was led to] the upper chamber,
and <s>Kaṃsa</s> was seated on the royal balcony — You too, together with <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) and Your companions, splendidly attired,
came to the arena-gate, which was blocked by the enraged elephant <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>. //
'Wretch, clear the path at once!' — with such words, when the cruel-minded keeper
drove [the elephant] upon You with great speed, and the elephant seized You,
You playfully slipped free, and striking the frontal globe of that [elephant] — long rivaling the pitcher-like breasts of the <s>Gopīs</s> —
You hid at its feet, and emerging again, [stood] with a charming smile. //
Though within reach of its trunk, yet ungraspable — like [the Self] to sages — running, playing,
falling to the ground, and as [the elephant] charged again, [You] tore out its tusk, alive,
from the very root — and the great pearls lodged at its base —
You gave to Your dear friend, saying 'Make a necklace of these, finely crafted, for <s>Rādhikā</s>.' //
Carrying the tusk upon Your shoulder, entering the arena together with <s>Halin</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) —
beholding You, the people, their minds and eyes captivated by the splendor of Your auspicious limbs, [exclaimed:]

children.text: haṃho dhanyo nu nando nahi nahi paśupālāṅganā no yaśodā
children.translated_text: 'Blessed indeed is <s>Nanda</s>! No, no — the cowherd women! No — <s>Yaśodā</s>!

children.text: no no dhanyekṣaṇāḥ smastrijagati vayameveti sarve śaśaṃsuḥ //
children.translated_text: No, no — we are the most blessed in the three worlds, we with blessed eyes!' — so all proclaimed. //
The full <s>Brahman</s> itself, directly — of boundless, dense, supreme bliss and radiance —
You sported among the cowherds, yet were not then recognized by the multitude.
But seeing You then, at this first auspicious occasion [in the arena], the crowds,
filled with complete bliss, freed of sins, joyfully sang Your remembered deeds. //
<s>Cāṇūra</s>, the champion wrestler, then at the king's command, and <s>Muṣṭika</s>, mighty of fist,

children.text: tvāṃ rāmaṃ cābhipede jhaṭajhaṭiti mitho muṣṭipātātirūkṣam /
children.translated_text: attacked You and <s>Rāma</s> — swiftly exchanging exceedingly rough blows of fists.
Throwing, casting down, dragging — various modes of combat proceeded there. Wondrous —
even before death, this lord of wrestlers experienced many bondages and releases. //

children.text: hā dhik kaṣṭaṃ kumaārau sulalitavapuṣau mallavīrau kaṭhorau
children.translated_text: 'Alas! How terrible! These two youths of delicate bodies against the hardened champion wrestlers!

children.text: na drakṣyāmo vrajāmastvaritamiti jane bhāṣamāṇe tadānīm /
children.translated_text: We cannot watch — let us leave at once!' — while the crowd was saying such things,
You hurled that <s>Cāṇūra</s>, his life-breath departing from the whirling of Your hands, and smashed him to the ground.
<s>Muṣṭika</s> too was crushed swiftly by <s>Halin</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), and the remaining [wrestlers] fled. //

children.text: kaṃsaḥ saṃvāryaṃ tṅryaṃ khalamatiravidan kāryamāryān pit ṃstā-
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṃsa</s>, of wicked mind, halting the music, not knowing the task at hand, [ordered] the noble parents
to be slain; and commanded [guards to seize] You of all-pervading form — when he leapt from his platform, ascending,
even as he brandished his sword in a struggle difficult to overcome, You forcibly seized the son of <s>Ugrasena</s>. //
Immediately dashing the king to the ground with his joints shattered, and upon him

children.text: tvayyāpātye tadaiva tvadupari patitā nākināṃ puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: as You descended, at that very instant a shower of flowers fell upon You from the celestials.

children.text: kiṃ kiṃ brūmastadānīṃ satatamapi bhiyā tvadgatātmā sa bheje
children.translated_text: What, what shall we say of that moment? He who had always, through fear, fixed his mind on You, attained

children.text: sāyujyaṃ tvadvadhotthā parama! paramiyaṃ vāsanā kālanemeḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>sāyujya</s> (complete union) with You! O Supreme One! This indeed was the supreme <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) of <s>Kālanemi</s>! //

children.text: tad bhrāt naṣṭa piṣṭvā drutamatha pitarau sannamannugrasenaṃ
children.translated_text: Having crushed and destroyed his brothers, then quickly honoring the parents and <s>Ugrasena</s>,
making him king, and delighting the entire <s>Yadu</s> clan with the granting of desires,
and obtaining <s>Uddhava</s>, the foremost devotee, who had learned statecraft from the guru of the gods, as [Your] friend —

children.text: labdhvā tuṣṭo nagaryāṃ pavanapurapate! rundhi me sarvarogān //
children.translated_text: You were pleased in the city. O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, remove all my diseases! //
Then, going to <s>Sāndīpani</s> [the teacher], in merely sixty-four days,
You, the omniscient, together with the wielder of the pestle (<s>Balarāma</s>), mastered all sciences.
Having retrieved his lost son from the abode of <s>Yama</s>, as the offering of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (teacher's fee),
giving [the son] to him, You returned to Your own city, sounding the <s>Pāñcajanya</s> (conch). //
Remembering again and again, the beautiful-eyed cowherd women, impelled by the weight of love —
You too, out of compassion, helpless [with emotion], sent that <s>Uddhava</s> [to them].
And to this supreme friend, this best of devotees, [You wished] to show
the excess of devotion of those [<s>Gopīs</s>], rare in all the world. //
Having reached <s>Gokula</s> at evening, which proclaimed the manifestation of Your greatness,
he gladdened <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Yaśodā</s> with abundant news of You.
In the morning, seeing the gem-studded chariot, the lotus-eyed women grew apprehensive;
hearing that a messenger of Yours had arrived, they abandoned their tasks and assembled. //
Seeing him, charming with attire and ornaments shining like Yours,
remembering again and again Your various pastimes — those and those [in particular] —
their voices choked, somehow they spoke with faltering words,
forgetting even the distinctions of propriety between self and other. //

children.text: śrīman! kiṃ tvaṃ pitṛjanakṛte preṣito nirdayena
children.translated_text: 'O noble one! Were you sent by that heartless one for the sake of His parents?

children.text: kvāsau kānto nagarasudṛśāṃ hā hare! nātha! pāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where is that lover of the city-women? Alas, O <s>Hari</s>! O Lord! O protector!
Of His embraces, His nectar-like body, alas, His kisses,

children.text: munmādānāṃ kuhakavacasāṃ vismaret kānta! kā vā //
children.translated_text: His intoxications, His deceptive words — O beloved! What woman could forget?' //
'Your body, made languid and lovely by the <s>Rāsa</s> (dance), its tresses loosened,
with gently emerging drops of perspiration, captivating —
O ocean of compassion! Show it to us, [that we may] embrace it even once!' —
thus, out of the madness of love, Your beloved ones lamented to You, O Delight of the world! //
The <s>Gopīs</s>, distraught with such helpless words,
were then brought to their natural state by <s>Uddhava</s> through Your messages, pregnant with spiritual wisdom.
And then, with those women of gladdened minds, now wholly absorbed in You,
he spent some days, joyfully exchanging stories of You. //
Constantly accompanied by songs about You, every household task,
only talk of You circulated among them — and that was even their sleep-talk.
Their gestures were mostly imitations of Yours; everything was pervaded by You —
seeing this there, <s>Uddhava</s> was exceedingly amazed with wonder. //
'This is most dear to my <s>Rādhā</s>; my beloved says thus' —

children.text: tvaṃ kiṃ maunaṃ kalayasi sakhe! māninī matpriyeva /
children.translated_text: 'Why are you silent, friend? Like my darling, you are proud!' —

children.text: ityādyeva pravadati sakhi! tvatpriyo nirjane mā-
children.translated_text: and 'Dear friend, in solitude Your beloved [speaks of] me' — with such words,
he delighted that lotus-eyed beloved of Yours, [speaking] as Your [representative]. //
'I shall come soon; my non-arrival is merely due to the burden of duties;
even in separation, since firmness of remembrance is possible, let there be no grief.

children.text: brahmānande milati nacirāt saṅgamo vā viyogas-
children.translated_text: When one merges in the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>, before long, union or separation

children.text: tulyo vaḥ syāditi tava girā so'karonnirvyathāstāḥ //
children.translated_text: shall become the same for you' — by Your words, he made them free from pain. //

children.text: evaṃ bhaktiḥ sakalabhuvane neśitā na śrutā vā
children.translated_text: 'Such devotion has not been seen or heard of in all the world!

children.text: kiṃ śāstraughaiḥ kimiha tapasā gopikābhyo namo'stu /
children.translated_text: What use are heaps of scriptures? What use of austerity? Salutations to the <s>Gopīs</s>!' —
thus, seeing <s>Uddhava</s> return from <s>Gokula</s>, overwhelmed with bliss,
You were delighted. O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, protect me from the multitude of ailments! //
Then, to <s>Sairandhri</s> (<s>Kubjā</s>), who had long been tormented by desire,
You went gracefully, together with <s>Uddhava</s>,
to the dwelling of that woman who always meditated
on the festival of Your arrival, preparing her attire daily. //
When You arrived, she whose wishes were fulfilled,
her breasts trembling with the excitement of joy,
offering various welcomes with delight —
You secretly pleasured her and experienced bliss. //
When asked to choose a boon, the poor woman requested
only continued lovemaking with You during the nights.
'Let there be <s>sāyujya</s> (complete union)' — a wise person might say; even desire for
'Let there be <s>sāmīpya</s> (proximity) always' — did she not even say that? //
Then, O Lord, on certain nights,
secretly delighting that fawn-eyed woman,
You gave [her] a son who came to be known as <s>Upaśloka</s> (the praised one)
He became a knower of the <s>Sāttvata-tantra</s> (the <s>Pāñcarātra</s> doctrine) through <s>Nārada</s>. //
Then, from <s>Akrūra</s>'s house, You, with <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) and <s>Uddhava</s>,
worshipped and much praised by that joyful one,
having taken leave of him, learned of the circumstances of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> who had gone to the forest,
and also of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>'s conduct. //
When, from the slaying of his son-in-law, the dearest friend King <s>Bhoja</s> (<s>Kaṃsa</s>),
<s>Jarāsandha</s>, blinded with boundless fury, besieged <s>Mathurā</s>,
You, with <s>Bala</s>, possessing only a modest force, with chariots and other [equipment] obtained from heaven,
destroyed twenty-three <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> (armies) brought by him. //
Though <s>Bala</s> had forcefully captured him, stronger even than the strong, You,
by an even greater display of valor, released him.
For from him who had gathered the armies of the entire world through conquest of all directions —
who else at that time possessed such strength and prowess? //
Though defeated, he, his heart set [on revenge], urged by other kings,
waged war with You sixteen times in this manner.
Auspicious, auspicious! You slew his <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s>, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>!
altogether three hundred and ninety-one at that time! //
When his eighteenth battle approached, You
beheld before You the <s>Yavana</s> (barbarian) with three crores of <s>Yavana</s> [soldiers].
Having <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> (<s>Viśvakarman</s>) swiftly construct a city in the midst of the ocean,
You then brought Your own people there by the power of <s>yoga</s>. //

children.text: padbhyāṃ tvaṃ padmamālī cakit iva purānnirgato dhāvamāno
children.translated_text: You, wearing a lotus-garland, as if startled, went forth from the city on foot, running,
pursued by the barbarian lord — who lacked the merit [needed] for being slain [by You] — You lay down on a mountain.
Then, quickly, by <s>Mucukunda</s>, sleeping there, kicked on the foot [by the barbarian] — when he was reduced to ashes,
to that king, at the back of the cave, You appeared in Your exquisitely beautiful form, [as one] worthy of devotion. //
'I am of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage; I am detached from all royal pleasures; I desire only Your grace —

children.text: hā deveti stuvantaṃ varavitatiṣu taṃ nispṛhaṃ vīkṣya hṛṣyan /
children.translated_text: alas, O Lord!' — thus he praised [You]. Seeing him, free from desire, among the multitude of boons, You were pleased.

children.text: muktestulyāṃ ca bhaktiṃ dhutasakalamalaṃ mokṣamapyāśu dattvā
children.translated_text: Granting him devotion equal to that of the liberated, and liberation too, with all impurities shaken off,

children.text: kāryaṃ hiṃsāviśuddhyai tapa iti ca tadā prārtha lokapratītyai //
children.translated_text: You then counseled: 'For purification from [past] violence, perform austerities' — for the sake of public convention. //

children.text: tadanu mathurāṃ gatvā hatvā camūṃ yavanāhṛtāṃ
children.translated_text: Then, going to <s>Mathurā</s>, having slain the army brought by the <s>Yavana</s>,
[You were] again blocked on the road by the troops of the king of <s>Magadha</s> (<s>Jarāsandha</s>), as before.
Granting him a final victory to inflate his pride, [You] feigned flight
and went to the city in the ocean (<s>Dvārakā</s>) — O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Protect me! //
Adorned with the skill of the celestial architect (<s>Viśvakarman</s>) and endowed with all the splendors granted by the gods,
You beautified the new city in the midst of the ocean, with Your own radiant form. //

children.text: daduṣi revatabhubhṛti revatīṃ halabhṛte tanayāṃ vidhiśāsanāt /
children.translated_text: When King <s>Revata</s> gave his daughter <s>Revatī</s> to the Plough-bearer (<s>Balarāma</s>) by <s>Brahmā</s>'s command,
You celebrated with great festive sounds, together with the joyful <s>Yādavas</s>. //

children.text: atha vidarbhasutāṃ khalu rukmiṇīṃ praṇayiṇīṃ tvayi deva! sahodaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, O Lord! <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, the daughter of <s>Vidarbha</s>, who was in love with You — her brother
desired to give her to the king of <s>Cedi</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>), resorting to the darkness of his own <s>tamas</s> (ignorance). //
The young maiden, who had long cherished her love for You, suddenly overwhelmed by the threat of her hopes being dashed,
dispatched a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> to convey to You her anguish, born of the Love God (<s>Anaṅga</s>). //

children.text: dvijasuto'pi ca tūrṇamupāyayau tava puraṃ hi durāśadurāsadam /
children.translated_text: That <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s son swiftly arrived at Your city — difficult of approach for the ill-intentioned —

children.text: mudamavāpa ca sādarapūjitaḥ sa bhavatā bhavatāpahṛtā svayam //
children.translated_text: and received joy, worshipped with respect by You, by whom all suffering is removed. //

children.text: sa ca bhavantamavocata kuṇḍine nṛpasutā khalu rājati rukmiṇī /
children.translated_text: And he told You: 'In <s>Kuṇḍina</s>, the princess <s>Rukmiṇī</s> shines;

children.text: tvayi samutsukayā nijadhīratārahitayā hi tayā prahito'smyaham //
children.translated_text: she, ardent for You, unable to contain herself, has sent me.' //

children.text: tava hṛtāsmi puraiva guṇairahaṃ harati māṃ kila cedinṛpo'dhunā /
children.translated_text: 'I have long since been captivated by Your virtues; now the king of <s>Cedi</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>) is carrying me off;

children.text: ayi kṛpālaya! pālaya māmiti prajagade jagadekapate! tayā //
children.translated_text: O Compassionate One! Protect me!' — thus she spoke, O sole Lord of the world! //

children.text: aśaraṇāṃ yadi māṃ tvamupekṣase sapadi jīvitameva jāhāmyaham /
children.translated_text: 'If You, the helpless one's [refuge], should disregard me, I shall immediately give up my life' —

children.text: iti girā sutanoratanod bhṛśaṃ suhṛdayaṃ hṛdayaṃ tava kātaram //
children.translated_text: these words of that slender-waisted woman deeply agitated Your compassionate, anxious heart. //
You then said to him: 'Ah friend! My torment of love is even greater than hers;
I shall go before the assembled kings and carry away that dark-eyed beloved.' //

children.text: pramuditena ca tena samaṃ tadā rathagato laghu kuṇḍinameyivān /
children.translated_text: Then, riding swiftly in a chariot together with that delighted [<s>brāhmaṇa</s>], You went to <s>Kuṇḍina</s>;

children.text: gurumarutpuranāyaka! me bhavān vitanutāṃ tanutāṃ nikhilāpadām //
children.translated_text: O great Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! May You diminish all my calamities! //
Together with <s>Bala</s> and followed by an army, You entered the city, honored by <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>;

children.text: dvijasutaṃ tvadupāgamavādinaṃ dhṛtarasā tarasā praṇanāma sā //
children.translated_text: and she, upon hearing from the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s son of Your arrival, with [her heart] filled with emotion, eagerly bowed down. //
Beholding Your form, the delight of the world, and hearing of the prince of <s>Cedi</s>'s doings,
the night passed for the city-dwellers, overcome with great sorrow, amidst weeping and lamentation. //
Then, the moon-faced [<s>Rukmiṇī</s>], resplendent with auspicious ornaments and decorations,
went out to worship Goddess <s>Śivā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) — her life dedicated to You — from her city, preceded by an escort of warriors. //

children.text: kulavadhūbhirupetya kumārikā girisutāṃ paripūjya ca sādaram /
children.translated_text: The maiden, accompanied by the married women of noble families, worshipping the Daughter of the Mountain (<s>Pārvatī</s>) with respect,

children.text: muhurayācata tatpadapaṅkaje nipatitā patitāṃ tava kevalam //
children.translated_text: repeatedly prayed at her lotus feet, falling prostrate — solely for You. //

children.text: samavalokya kutuhalasaṅkule nṛpakule nibhṛtaṃ tvayi ca sthite /
children.translated_text: While the assembly of kings watched with curious excitement, and while You stood concealed,
the princess emerged from the temple of <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), exceedingly beautiful, illuminating the directions with her radiance. //
By the luster of her world-enchanting beauty, all the assembled host of kings were rendered helpless,

children.text: tvamapi deva! kaṭākṣavimokṣaṇaiḥ pramadayā madayāñcakṛṣe manāk //
children.translated_text: and even You, O Lord! with the release of sidelong glances, delighted, drew her [heart] slightly toward You. //

children.text: kva tu gamiṣyasi candramukhīti tāṃ sarasametya kareṇa haran kṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: 'Where will you go, O moon-faced one?' — thus approaching that [princess] swiftly and playfully, seizing her hand in an instant,

children.text: samadhiropya rathaṃ tvamapāhṛthā bhuvi tato vitato ninado dviṣām //
children.translated_text: You lifted her onto Your chariot and carried her away — and thereupon, the uproar of enemies spread across the earth. //

children.text: kva nu gataḥ paśupāla iti krudhā kṛtaraṇā yadubhiśca jitā nṛpāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Where has the cowherd gone?' — with fury, the kings joined battle but were defeated by the <s>Yādavas</s>;

children.text: na tu bhavānudacālyata tairaho piśunakaiḥ śunakairiva kesarī //
children.translated_text: but You, ah! were not even slightly disturbed by them — like a lion by barking dogs. //
Then, when <s>Rukmin</s> came to battle, sparing his life but binding and disfiguring him,

children.text: hṛtamadaṃ parimucya baloktibhiḥ puramayā ramayā saha kāntayā //
children.translated_text: You released the humbled one at <s>Bala</s>'s words, and returned to Your city with Your beloved <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Rukmiṇī</s>). //
[She], her mind enchanted by the new union, her love-play awakened by tender curiosity,

children.text: aramayaḥ khalu nātha! yathāsukhaṃ rahasi tāṃ hasitāṃśulasanmukhīm //
children.translated_text: You delighted her as You pleased, O Lord! in seclusion — her face radiant with smiles. //
Thus, day and night, creating joy with various playful acts, one day
You, through ironically crooked words to the straightforward-minded [<s>Rukmiṇī</s>], aroused her excessive agitation. //
Then, with even greater skill in endearment, delighting that loving one all the more —

children.text: ayi mukunda! bhavaccaritāni naḥ pragadatāṃ gadatāntimapākuru //
children.translated_text: O <s>Mukunda</s>! Recount Your deeds to us! Remove the end of our disease! //
Then, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! You asked <s>Satrājit</s> for the divine
<s>Syamantaka</s> gem, obtained by him from the Sun God.
The reason for this appears to me to be manifold — surely,
as a pretext to marry his daughter, who was in love with You. //
When that excellent gem was not given to You by him, being of petty mind,
<s>Prasena</s>, his brother, wearing it on his neck, went hunting.
A lion slew him, and the jewel, [glittering] — the lord of apes (<s>Jāmbavān</s>), mistaking it for meat in his confusion,

children.text: kapīndrastaṃ hatvā maṇimapi ca bālāya dadivān //
children.translated_text: having killed the [lion], gave the jewel to his child. //
Following <s>Satrājit</s>'s allegation, people declared You the thief of the gem;
alas, for the virtuous, even nectar becomes a speck of blame among people.
Therefore, though omniscient, You, accompanied by Your kinsmen, devoted to the search,

children.text: prasenaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā harimapi gato'bhūḥ kapiguhām //
children.translated_text: having found <s>Prasena</s> [dead], went to the bear's (<s>Jāmbavān</s>'s) cave, following the trail. //
Not recognizing You, <s>Jāmbavān</s> of great age fought You himself,

children.text: mukundaśaranaṃ hi māṃ ka iha roddhumityālapan /
children.translated_text: saying: 'Who here can obstruct me, who has taken refuge in <s>Mukunda</s>?'

children.text: vibho! raghupate! hare! jaya jayetyalaṃ muṣṭibhi-
children.translated_text: 'O Lord! O <s>Raghupati</s>! O <s>Hari</s>! Victory! Victory!' — thus, with fists alone,
fighting, he performed Your worship — that crest-jewel of devotees! //

children.text: buddhvātha tena dattāṃ navaramaṇīṃ varamaṇīṃ ca parigṛhṇan /
children.translated_text: Then, understanding [the truth], he gave You his beautiful young daughter (<s>Jāmbavatī</s>), and the excellent gem — accepting both,

children.text: anugṛhṇannamumāgāḥ sapadi ca satrājite maṇiṃ prādāḥ //
children.translated_text: You bestowed Your grace upon him and returned, and immediately gave the gem to <s>Satrājit</s>. //
Thereupon, he — truly wise, ashamed and abashed — [offered] his daughter
<s>Bhāmā</s> (<s>Satyabhāmā</s>), with her trembling, restless eyes — she who had already been given away in speech —

children.text: adita maṇinā tubhyaṃ labhyaṃ sametya bhavānapi
children.translated_text: together with the gem, to You. Approaching, You too,
with a delighted mind, accepted [the gem] from him, [Your] intentions inscrutable. //
As You were delighting the bashful <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, the news of the burning of the sons of <s>Kuntī</s> (<s>Pāṇḍavas</s>) arrived,
and You set out for the <s>Kuru</s> [kingdom].
Alas! <s>Śatadhanvan</s>, instigated by the words of <s>Akrūra</s> and <s>Kṛtavarman</s>,
slew <s>Satrājit</s> and seized the gem. //
Seeing Your beloved come to the <s>Kurus</s> in grief, You
swiftly slew <s>Śatadhanvan</s> and consoled her.
Then, anxious about the jewel, going to the house of the <s>Mithila</s> [prince] (<s>Akrūra</s>),
<s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) trained the son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>) in mace-fighting. //
This <s>Akrūra</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! by Your will alone,
instigated the violence against the evil-doing <s>Satrājit</s>;
and You, taking the gem from <s>Akrūra</s> but then
restoring it to him — they say [it was] to establish his prosperity. //
He, <s>Gāndinī</s>'s son (<s>Akrūra</s>), was a steadfast devotee of You —
how then, O Lord! did his mind turn to wickedness?
'I am learned, I am tranquil' — the swelling pride
[of his] was surely created by You to be humbled. //
The [gem], which [<s>Akrūra</s>] had fled with in fear along with <s>Kṛtavarman</s>, You
recalled [him], exposing the gem placed by him,
and left it right there, in the keeping of that keeper of noble vows — being satisfied,
You lay upon the bosom of <s>Bhāmā</s> (<s>Satyabhāmā</s>), O Lord of the Wind! Protect [me]! //

children.text: snigdhāṃ mugdhāṃ satatamapi tāṃ lālayan satyabhāmāṃ
children.translated_text: Ever fondling the tender, innocent <s>Satyabhāmā</s>,

children.text: yāto bhūyaḥ saha khalu tayā yājñasenīvivāham /
children.translated_text: You again went with her to the wedding of <s>Draupadī</s> (<s>Yājñasenī</s>).
Then, for the delight of <s>Arjuna</s> (<s>Pārtha</s>), staying again at <s>Hastināpura</s> for some time, O Lord!
having also established the city of <s>Indraprastha</s>, You returned. //
<s>Bhadrā</s>, the virtuous one, Your own sister, when sought [in marriage] by the <s>Kaurava</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>) —
by Your instruction, <s>Arjuna</s>, the son of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), abducted her through a deceptive feat of archery.
Pacifying the angered <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) there, You returned with him
to <s>Indraprastha</s>, to the delight of Your dear friend (<s>Arjuna</s>), accompanied by <s>Satyabhāmā</s>. //
While sporting there, having taken <s>Kālindī</s>, seen on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
You went to Your city, having pleased <s>Agni</s> with [the burning of] the <s>Khāṇḍava</s> [forest].
O Lord! <s>Mitravindā</s> of <s>Avantī</s>, Your paternal aunt's daughter, trembling with fear of her brothers, overwhelmed by love,
You suddenly seized from the midst of kings. //
Going to <s>Satya</s> (<s>Kośala</s>), You then carried away the daughter of the <s>Nagnajit</s> king,
having subdued all seven bulls in seven forms in an instant.

children.text: bhadrāṃ nāma pradaduratha te deva! santardanādyās-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Santardana</s> and the others, O Lord! gave You <s>Bhadrā</s> by name,
their sister — she too, O Boon-granter! was Your paternal aunt's daughter. //
Piercing the target — a fish in water, visible only as a reflection — a feat unaccomplished even by <s>Arjuna</s> and others,
You won <s>Lakṣaṇā</s>, the princess of <s>Madra</s>.
Thus, eight became Your consorts; and among [all events], meanwhile,
You heard, from the words of <s>Indra</s>, of the evil deeds of <s>Bhauma</s> (<s>Narakāsura</s>). //
Summoning <s>Garuḍa</s>, the foremost of birds, who came when remembered, and mounting him, You set forth,
carrying <s>Bhāmā</s> (<s>Satyabhāmā</s>) in Your lap — toward the enemy's city as if it were a pleasure-garden.
Breaching the fortifications, with streams of blood from the severed army,
You turned <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s> into a flood of blood. //
<s>Mura</s>, the five-headed one, sprang at You from the midst of the ocean-forest;

children.text: sa cakre cakreṇa pradalitaśirā maṅkṣu bhavatā /
children.translated_text: he was swiftly made by You, with his heads split by the discus, [a lifeless mass].
Then, <s>Naraka</s> (<s>Narakāsura</s>), waging war riding four-tusked elephants,
was slain by You with Your discus, making him cross over [to death] (<s>tīrṇa-raka</s>) — [the demon] whose very name means 'hell.' //

children.text: stuto bhūmyā rājyaṃ sapadi bhagadatte'sya tanaye
children.translated_text: Praised by the Earth (<s>Bhūmī</s>), You swiftly bestowed the kingdom upon <s>Bhagadatta</s>, his son,

children.text: gajaṃ caikaṃ dattvā prajighāyitha nāgān nijapurīm /
children.translated_text: and giving him one elephant, You dispatched the [remaining] elephants to Your own city.
Also [You dispatched] sixteen thousand women

children.text: sahasrāṇi strīṇāmapi ca dhanarāśiṃ ca vipulam //
children.translated_text: imprisoned by the villain, their hearts devoted to You, as well as a vast heap of wealth. //
Then, going to heaven to return the earrings seized by <s>Bhauma</s> to their [rightful owner] <s>Aditi</s>,
You were honored by <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) and the others, while Your beloved [<s>Satyabhāmā</s>], challenged by the heavenly women, responded.
Having seized the <s>Kalpa-vṛkṣa</s> (wish-granting tree) and defeating <s>Indra</s> who attacked in fury, You returned —
this You did indeed [to demonstrate that] such is the fault of the pride of wealth. //
Planting the <s>Kalpa</s> tree in <s>Satyabhāmā</s>'s courtyard, having accepted the sixteen thousand women,
assuming multiple forms for each house, You delighted [each wife] with various love-sports.
Wonderfully, when <s>Nārada</s> came to observe [Your] manifold states, in every single home,

children.text: bhūyaḥ sarvāsu kurvan daśa daśa tanayān pāhi vātālayeśa! //
children.translated_text: and furthermore, begetting ten sons in each — O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, protect me! //

children.text: pradyumno raukmiṇeyaḥ sa khalu tava kalā śambareṇāhṛtastaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Pradyumna</s>, the son of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, he who is indeed Your partial manifestation — carried off by <s>Śambara</s>, that

children.text: hatvā ratyā sahāpto nijapūramaharad rukmikanyāṃ ca dhanyām /
children.translated_text: having slain [<s>Rukmin</s>], and arriving at his own city with <s>Rati</s> (his wife), he won the glorious daughter of <s>Rukmin</s>.
Then his son <s>Aniruddha</s>, a treasure of virtues, married <s>Rocanā</s>, the granddaughter of <s>Rukmin</s>;

children.text: tatrodvāhe gatastvaṃ nyavadhi musalinā rukmyapi dyūtavairāt //
children.translated_text: at that wedding You were present, and <s>Rukmin</s> was slain by the wielder of the plough (<s>Balarāma</s>) from a grudge over gambling.
There was a maiden named <s>Ūṣā</s>, the illustrious daughter
of <s>Bāṇa</s>, son of <s>Bali</s>, the thousand-armed devotee of <s>Maheśvara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>);
having experienced Your grandson <s>Aniruddha</s>, whom she had never seen before,
in a dream, O Lord, she became tormented by longing.
A <s>yoginī</s> named <s>Citralekhā</s>, exceedingly skilled,
her friend, drawing portraits of all the young men,
identified <s>Aniruddha</s> [from among them] for her; and at night,
she brought him from Your abode by the power of <s>yoga</s>.
While he was enjoying pleasures with his beloved in the maiden's chamber,
when somehow <s>Bāṇa</s>, the devotee of <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), bound him,
learning the tidings from <s>Śrī Nārada</s>, with exceedingly fierce rage,
You besieged his city of <s>Śoṇitapura</s> with the <s>Yadus</s>.
The guardian of his city, the lord who is the husband of the mountain's beloved daughter (<s>Śiva</s>),
together with hosts of spirits, fearlessly besieged the <s>Yadu</s> army.
The mighty <s>Bāṇa</s> immediately fought with <s>Yuyudhāna</s> (<s>Sātyaki</s>);
<s>Guha</s> (<s>Skanda</s>) with <s>Pradyumna</s>; and You engaged with the destroyer of the cities (<s>Śiva</s>).
When <s>Giriśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), all of whose weapons were neutralized by Your weapon, swooned,
the spirits fled in fear; the champions of the <s>Pramatha</s> hosts were routed.
<s>Skanda</s> retreated; <s>Bāṇa</s>'s minister <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s> was quickly shattered

children.text: sa kumbhāṇḍo bhāṇḍaṃ navamiva balenāśu bibhide //
children.translated_text: by <s>Balarāma</s>, like a new vessel; and [<s>Bāṇa</s>] was struck by the flower-arrows [of <s>Pradyumna</s>].
When <s>Bāṇa</s>, who had attacked forcefully with five hundred bows, had his bow shattered,
and when [his attack] had been rendered futile, the lord of Fever (<s>Śiva</s>'s Fever) fought with Your Fever;

children.text: jñānī stutvātha dattvā tava caritajuṣāṃ vijvaraṃ sa jvaro'gāt
children.translated_text: becoming wise, having praised [You] and received from You freedom from fever for those devoted to Your deeds, that Fever departed;

children.text: prāyo'ntarjñānavanto'pi ca bahutamasā raudraceṣṭā hi raudrāḥ //
children.translated_text: for even those who possess inner knowledge, if beset by great <s>tamas</s> (darkness), are fierce in their fierce deeds.
When <s>Bāṇa</s>, again attacking fiercely with various weapons, [was met by You who were]
cutting away all his faults at once, <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), who wished to understand, praised You.
At his word, leaving [<s>Bāṇa</s>] with only two arms, You made that dear one of his fearless on both sides,
and releasing him, having received [<s>Śiva</s>'s] honor, You went to Your own city together with <s>Aniruddha</s> and <s>Ūṣā</s>.
At various times You conquered <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) during the seizure of <s>Nanda</s>,
<s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Yama</s> at the rescue of the boys, the wind-god at the swallowing of the forest fire,
<s>Brahmā</s> at the stealing of the calves, and <s>Giriśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) in the battle with <s>Bāṇa</s> —
O Lord! This incarnation of Yours, surpassing the entire universe, is victorious!
Sending King <s>Nṛga</s>, who bore the body of a chameleon due to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s curse, to the heavenly abode,
and instructing Your own people in supreme devotion to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — O Lord of the Wind's abode, protect me!
When <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) had gone to <s>Gokula</s>, absorbed in the company of women,
and when, though summoned, he did not come, having subdued the <s>Yamunā</s> in his intoxicated arrogance —
the self-styled [<s>Vāsudeva</s>], <s>Pauṇḍraka</s>, freely indulging in pleasure, deluded by the flattery of his servants,
sent a messenger to You.
'I am <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, descended here on earth;
you too, it seems, bear my insignia;

children.text: utsṛjya tāni śaraṇaṃ vraja māmiti tvāṃ
children.translated_text: abandon them and come to me for refuge' —
thus the messenger addressed You, and was laughed at by all in the assembly.
When the messenger had departed, You, with a <s>Yādava</s> army,
went and beheld the appearance of <s>Pauṇḍraka</s>:
a <s>Śrīkaustubha</s> [gem] of no great value, branded on his chest by burning,
with crocodile-shaped earrings and yellow garment.
His <s>Sudarśana</s> made of black iron —
with the fire-like rays of Your [true] <s>Sudarśana</s>,
You severed his head and crushed his army;
and You also sent the head of his ally, the king of <s>Kāśī</s>, [flying] to <s>Kāśī</s>.
Through foolishness, even from childhood, repeating 'I am
<s>Śrī Vāsudeva</s>' — his conviction had long been fixed;
by [this] constant identification with You, he attained union (<s>sāyujya</s>) —
who indeed can know whose merit operates how?
Then the son of the king of <s>Kāśī</s>, named <s>Sudakṣiṇa</s>,
having worshipped <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), directed a spell of black magic against You.
Together with spirits who were terrified from the battle with <s>Bāṇa</s>,
somehow enlisted, he released a certain fire of <s>Kṛtyā</s> (destructive sorcery).
Seeing that <s>Kṛtyā</s> with feet the size of palm trees, burning everything,
though the frightened citizens reported it to You,

children.text: dyūtotsave kamapi no calito vibho! tvaṃ
children.translated_text: O Lord, You were not disturbed at all from a game of dice;
You quickly dispatched the discus of Time that stood at Your side.
When Your great weapon of limitless radiance came hurtling down,
the terrible <s>Kṛtyā</s> fled crying 'Alas!'
In fury, the discus burnt <s>Sudakṣiṇa</s>, whose conduct was graceless,
and set the city of <s>Kāśī</s> ablaze as well.

children.text: sa khalu vivido rakṣoghāte kṛtopakṛtiḥ purā
children.translated_text: That <s>Vivida</s> [monkey], who had formerly rendered service during the slaying of the <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: tava tu kalayā mṛtyuṃ prāptuṃ tadā khalatāṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: had by then turned wicked, seeking death at a portion of Your [hands];
that ally of <s>Naraka</s>, fighting with the wielder of the plough (<s>Balarāma</s>), was struck down by a blow of the palm.
When <s>Sāmba</s> was seized for abducting the daughter of a <s>Kaurava</s> prince, <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), going to appease the <s>Kurus</s>,
angered by their words, uprooted the city with its elephants and freed him.

children.text: te ghātyāḥ pāṇḍaveyairiti yadupṛtanāṃ nāmucastvaṃ tadānīṃ
children.translated_text: 'They shall be slain by the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>' — yet at that time You did not command the <s>Yadu</s> army [against the <s>Kurus</s>];

children.text: taṃ tvāṃ durbodhalīlaṃ pavanapurapate! tāpaśāntyai niṣeve //
children.translated_text: You whose play is hard to fathom — O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, I worship You for the pacification of my afflictions.
Once, at the time of a solar eclipse, placing <s>Kṛtavarma</s> and <s>Pradyumna</s> in charge of the city,
You went, accompanied by the women of the <s>Yadu</s> clan, to the holy site called <s>Samantapañcaka</s>.

children.text: bahutarajanatāhitāya tatra tvamapi punan vinimajjya tīrthatoye /
children.translated_text: There, for the benefit of the multitude, You too, purifying Yourself by immersing in the sacred waters,
distributing masses of wealth to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, met with friends such as the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.

children.text: tava khalu dayitājanaiḥ sametā drupadasutā tvayi gāḍhabhaktibhārā /
children.translated_text: Together with Your beloved wives, <s>Draupadī</s>, the daughter of <s>Drupada</s>, bearing a heavy load of deep devotion to You,
greatly rejoiced with the other queens, hearing accounts of Your deeds from them.

children.text: tadanu ca bhagavan! nirīkṣya gopānatikutukādupagamya mānayitvā /
children.translated_text: Then, O Lord, seeing the cowherds, approaching them with great eagerness and honoring them,
You followed the cowherd women, whose limbs were worn from long separation, with tender affection.
At once, through the festival of beholding You, in those full-hipped women whose pride had been stolen from their hearts,
You reclined upon their bosom, which was endearingly familiar, the bodice loosened in the excess of passion.
'Due to repeated battles with enemies, there has been such a long delay in coming to me' —

children.text: iti kṛtaparirambhaṇe tvayi drāgativivaśā khalu rādhikā nililye //
children.translated_text: thus, as You embraced [her], <s>Rādhā</s>, overcome with ecstasy, melted into You.

children.text: apagatavirahavyathāstadā tā rahasi vidhāya dadātha tattvabodham /
children.translated_text: Having removed their agony of separation, in private You imparted to them the knowledge of the ultimate truth:
'I am the Self of supreme bliss and consciousness — may this arise clearly in your minds.'
Formerly, through the teachings of <s>Uddhava</s>, their separation had been mixed with a taste of bliss;

children.text: samabhavadamutaḥ paraṃ tu tāsāṃ paramasukaikyamayī bhavadvicintā //
children.translated_text: but from that point onward, their contemplation of You became one of complete unity with the supreme bliss.
When hosts of great sages and Your father asked about auspicious rites for the removal of sins,
'What need is there for other auspicious means when You are present?' — with much laughter, he was made to perform the sacrifice.

children.text: sumahati yajane vitāyamāne pramuditamitrajane sahaiva gopāḥ /
children.translated_text: At the great sacrifice being conducted, with friends delighted, together with the cowherds,
honored by the <s>Yadu</s> folk, for three months they enjoyed the bliss of Your company as before.

children.text: vyapagamasamaye sametya rādhāṃ dṛḍhamupagūhya nirīkṣya vītakhedām /
children.translated_text: At the time of departure, having met <s>Rādhā</s> and embracing her tightly, seeing her freed from sorrow,

children.text: pramuditahṛdayaḥ puraṃ prayātaḥ pavanapureśvara! pāhi māṃ gadebhyaḥ //
children.translated_text: with a delighted heart, You returned to the city. O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, protect me from diseases!
Then, the kings imprisoned for a long time by the king of <s>Magadha</s> (<s>Jarāsandha</s>), suffering from prolonged confinement —
twenty thousand and eight hundred, O Lord, of those earthly rulers —
sent to You, the refuge of the shelterless, a certain messenger, who
begged only for the destruction of <s>Jarāsandha</s> — what more need be said?
When You wished to march against <s>Jarāsandha</s>, and then, from <s>Nārada</s>'s report,
learned of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s preparations for the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice, You were caught between the two tasks.
When <s>Uddhava</s> advised that from a <s>Digvijaya</s> (universal conquest), both goals would be accomplished,
You went with Your own people to the city of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> (<s>Indraprastha</s>).
When You arrived with all Your beloved wives, the son of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>),
having conquered the earth with his brothers, whose prowess was nurtured by Your sidelong glances,
bearing matchless glory — alas, what devotion-as-servitude! —
sent You, O Lord, against <s>Jarāsandha</s>, together with <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>.
Having gone to the city of <s>Girivraja</s>, You three, O God,
in the guise of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, challenged that <s>Magadha</s> king to a battle-festival.
Making him fight the son of the wind (<s>Bhīma</s>), as his merit was not yet complete,

children.text: nirīkṣya saha jiṣṇunā tvamapi rājayudhvā sthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: watching together with <s>Arjuna</s>, You stood like a king overseeing the combat.
When that fiercely combative [<s>Jarāsandha</s>], whose ardor in battle would not subside, [was finally thrown],
the son of <s>Jarā</s> was torn apart by the son of the wind, with the signal of splitting a twig,

children.text: vimucya nṛpatīn mudā samanugṛhya bhaktiṃ parāṃ
children.translated_text: and You, releasing the kings with joy, blessing them with supreme devotion,
appointed them, though free from desire, to the protection of <s>dharma</s> on earth.
When <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> then commenced the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice,
busy with all the kings who had come as willing servants —
You too, O Lord of the world, performed the washing of <s>brāhmaṇa</s> feet and other [humble] tasks;
what more can be said of the fortune of that best of kings!
Then, for the principal honor (<s>agrapūjā</s>) in the sacrificial rite,
that son of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>), following the words of <s>Sahadeva</s>,
joyfully bestowed it upon You in the assembly, O soul of all beings,
and at that moment the entire world, including gods and men, attained satisfaction.
Then immediately <s>Śiśupāla</s>, while sages and kings were still seated, [cried:]
'Alas! What fool honors this dull cowherd boy!'
Thus, while he was pouring forth a torrent of abusive words against You,
he sprang from his seat with weapon raised — and the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> likewise rose [to face] him.
Restraining those of Your own side, facing the adversary who charged toward You,
You Yourself severed his head with the discus, the slayer of demons.
With a mind purified by constant contemplation obtained through three births,
he attained through You the supreme oneness — which is difficult even for <s>yogis</s> to obtain.

children.text: tataḥ sumāhito tvayā kratuvare nirūḍhe jano
children.translated_text: Then, when the great sacrifice was duly completed by You, the people departed

children.text: yayau jayati dharmajo jayati kṛṣṇa ityālapan /
children.translated_text: exclaiming 'Victory to the son of <s>Dharma</s>! Victory to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!'

children.text: khalaḥ sa tu suyodhano dhutamanāḥ sapatnaśriyā
children.translated_text: But the wicked <s>Suyodhana</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>), his mind shaken by the splendor of his rival,
in the assembly hall given by <s>Maya</s>, was confounded by the illusion of land and water.
Then the laughter that arose from <s>Draupadī</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, and others —
You, O Lord, somewhat encouraged with a sidelong glance;
thus, quickly sowing the seed for the removal of the earth's burden —
O <s>Janārdana</s>! O dweller of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Protect me from disease!
<s>Śālva</s>, defeated at the wedding of <s>Rukmiṇī</s> by the <s>Yadu</s> forces, having obtained from the crescent-crested one (<s>Śiva</s>)

children.text: vindan saubhaṃ sa māyī tvayi vasati kurūṃstvatpurīmabhyabhāṅkṣīt /
children.translated_text: the aerial chariot <s>Saubha</s>, that master of <s>māyā</s>, while You were among the <s>Kurus</s>, attacked Your city.
<s>Pradyumna</s>, besieging him with all the <s>Yadu</s> warriors, captured the fiercely powerful

children.text: tasyāmātyaṃ dyumantaṃ vyajani ca samaraḥ saptaviṃśatyahāntam //
children.translated_text: <s>Dyumān</s>, his general, and the battle lasted twenty-seven days.
Then You, accompanied by <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), having come swiftly,

children.text: saubheśaṃ taṃ nyarundhāḥ sa ca kila gadayā śārṅgamabhraṃśayat te /
children.translated_text: besieged that lord of <s>Saubha</s> whose army was mostly destroyed; and he with his mace knocked the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow from Your hand.

children.text: māyātātaṃ vyahiṃsīdapi tava puratastat tvayāpi kṣaṇārdhaṃ
children.translated_text: He slew a phantom of Your father; but You too, for a half-moment,
did not perceive [the illusion] — so some say; but <s>Vyāsa</s> himself refuted that as derogatory.

children.text: kṣiptvā saubhaṃ gadācūrṇitamudakanidhau maṅkṣu sālve'pi cakre-
children.translated_text: Hurling the <s>Saubha</s>, crushed by the mace, into the ocean, and when <s>Śālva</s> too was beheaded by the discus,
<s>Dantavaktra</s>, rushing forward violently, hurled his mace at You.
He too was slain by the <s>Kaumodakī</s> (mace), and that treasure of good deeds, like <s>Śiśupāla</s>, attained oneness [with You];
for all of these, who had formerly fixed their minds on You, this incarnation was for the purpose of their liberation.

children.text: tvayyāyāte'tha jāte kila kurusadasi dyūtake saṃyatāyāḥ
children.translated_text: When You had come [back] and the game of dice took place in the <s>Kuru</s> assembly, for [<s>Draupadī</s>] who was being dragged,
crying piteously, daughter of <s>Yajñasena</s> (<s>Drupada</s>), You compassionately created an endless garland of cloth.
When the portion-born sage of <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Durvāsas</s>) came at the end of a meal, and <s>Draupadī</s> was alarmed — thinking of You,
You arrived, and by eating the remnant of vegetable rice, You made the host of sages satisfied in the forest.

children.text: yuddhodyoge'tha mantre milati sati vṛtaḥ phalgunena tvamekaḥ
children.translated_text: When war preparations were underway and counsel was sought, You alone were chosen by <s>Arjuna</s>,
while the <s>Kaurava</s> received Your army; You went to the elephant city (<s>Hastināpura</s>) as an envoy on behalf of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.

children.text: mīṣmadroṇādimānye tava khalu vacane dhikkṛte kauraveṇa
children.translated_text: When <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and others respected Your words, but the <s>Kaurava</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>) scorned them,
revealing Your cosmic form in the assembly of sages, having agitated the city, You departed.

children.text: jiṣṇostvaṃ kṛṣṇa! sūtaḥ khalu samaramukhe bandhughāte dayāluṃ
children.translated_text: You, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, became the charioteer of <s>Arjuna</s> on the battlefield, and when that compassionate one

children.text: khinnaṃ taṃ vīkṣya vīraṃ kimidamayi sakhe! nitya eko'yamātmā /
children.translated_text: Seeing that hero despondent, [You said]: 'What is this, O friend? This Self is ever one alone;

children.text: ko vadhyaḥ ko'tra hantā tadiha vadhabhiyaṃ projjhya mayyarpitātmā
children.translated_text: who is the slain and who the slayer? Therefore, casting away the fear of killing, with your self surrendered to Me,

children.text: dharmyaṃ yuddhaṃ careti prakṛtimanayathā darśayan viśvarūpam //
children.translated_text: fight the righteous war' — thus, showing the cosmic form (<s>Viśvarūpa</s>), You set right his nature.
When <s>Bhīṣma</s>, the crest-jewel of devotees, solely intent on the task of relieving the Earth's burden,

children.text: nityaṃ nityaṃ vibhindatyavanibhṛdayutaṃ prāptasāde ca pārthe /
children.translated_text: daily and daily shattered ten thousand of the earth-bearing warriors, and <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) was losing heart,
abandoning Your vow of not bearing weapons, grasping the great discus, wrathful,

children.text: vādhāvan prāñjaliṃ taṃ nataśirasamatho vīkṣya modādapāgāḥ //
children.translated_text: You rushed forward — but seeing him with joined palms, head bowed, You stopped with joy and turned back.
In the battle, when the <s>Vaiṣṇavāstra</s> (weapon of <s>Viṣṇu</s>), launched by <s>Bhagadatta</s>, steady in battle upon his elephant, was directed by <s>Droṇa</s>,
You received it on Your chest, Your radiance eclipsing the sun, blocked by the discus, and You tormented the king of <s>Sindhu</s> (<s>Jayadratha</s>).
When the <s>Nāgāstra</s> (serpent-weapon) was released by <s>Karṇa</s>, You pressed the earth down so that only his crown was cut;

children.text: tatre tatrāpi pārthaṃ kimiva na hi bhavān pāṇḍavānāmakārṣīt //
children.translated_text: there and everywhere, what indeed did You not do for the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>?

children.text: yuddhādau tīrthagāmi sa khalu haladharo naimiśakṣetramṛccha-
children.translated_text: He of the plough (<s>Balarāma</s>), going on a pilgrimage at the start of the war, reaching the holy site of <s>Naimiśa</s>,
killed the <s>Sūta</s> (<s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>) who did not rise to greet him, and appointed his son in his place;

children.text: yajñaghnaṃ balvalaṃ parvaṇi paridalayam snātatīrtho raṇānte
children.translated_text: destroying <s>Balvala</s> who disrupted the sacrifice at each festival, having bathed at the holy sites, at the end of the war

children.text: samprāpto bhīmaduryodhanaraṇamaśamaṃ vīkṣya yātaḥ purīṃ te //
children.translated_text: he arrived and, seeing the unresolved club-fight between <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Duryodhana</s>, departed to Your city.
<s>Aśvatthāman</s> (<s>Drauṇi</s>), his mind destroyed by the killing of <s>Draupadī</s>'s sleeping sons, was encountered; at Your word,

children.text: tanmuktaṃ brāhmamastraṃ samahṛta vijayo mauliratnaṃ ca jahe /
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s> (<s>Vijaya</s>) neutralized the <s>Brahmāstra</s> released by him and took his crest-jewel.
When, for the destruction of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, that weapon again entered <s>Uttarā</s>'s womb,
You, O Lord, protecting it, entered the womb, O Discus-Bearer, the size of a thumb!
<s>Bhīṣma</s>, of self-willed death, declaring the full flood of <s>dharma</s> to the son of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>),

children.text: tvāṃ paśyan bhaktibhūmnaiva hi sapadi yayau niṣkalabrahmabhūyam /
children.translated_text: gazing upon You with the fullness of devotion, instantly attained the state of the undivided <s>Brahman</s>.
Then, having had the son of <s>Dharma</s> perform three most exalted <s>Aśvamedha</s> sacrifices, fulfilling all desires,

children.text: samprāpto dvārakāṃ tvaṃ pavanapurapate! pāhi māṃ sarvarogāt //
children.translated_text: You returned to <s>Dvārakā</s> — O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, protect me from all disease!

children.text: kucelanāmā bhavataḥ satīrthyatāṃ gataḥ sa sāndīpanimandire dvijaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Kucelā</s> (<s>Sudāmā</s>), who had been Your fellow-student

children.text: tvadekarāgeṇa dhanādiniḥspṛho dināni ninye praśamī gṛhāśramī //
children.translated_text: at <s>Sāndīpani</s>'s school, through exclusive devotion to You and indifference to wealth and the rest,

children.text: samānaśīlāpi tadāyavallabhā tathaiva no cittahayaṃ sameyusī /
children.translated_text: spent his days in tranquility as a householder.

children.text: kadācidūce bata vṛttilabdhaye ramāpatiḥ kiṃ na sakhā niṣevyate //
children.translated_text: His wife, though of similar temperament, could not always rein in the horse of her mind;

children.text: itīrito'yaṃ priyayā kṣudhārtayā jugupsamāno'pi dhane madāvahe /
children.translated_text: once she said: 'Alas, why do you not approach the Lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), your friend, for a livelihood?'

children.text: tadā tvadālokanakautukād yayau vahan paṭānte pṛthukānupāyanam //
children.translated_text: Thus urged by his hungry wife, though himself averse to wealth that breeds pride,
he went, driven by the curiosity of seeing You, carrying flattened rice as a gift in a cloth's corner.

children.text: praviśya vaikuṇṭhamivāpa nirvṛtiṃ tavātisambhāvanayā tu kiṃ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: He entered Your wondrous city and, within Your palaces, reached the mansion of <s>Śaibyā</s> (Your queen);

children.text: prapūjitaṃ taṃ priyayā ca vījitaṃ kare gṛhītvākathayaḥ purā kṛtam /
children.translated_text: entering as if into <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, he experienced bliss — and how much more so from Your lavish welcome!
Worshipped and fanned by Your beloved, taking his hand, You recounted the past:

children.text: trapājuṣo'smāt pṛthukaṃ balādatha pragṛhya muṣṭau sakṛdāśite tvayā /
children.translated_text: how, when sent by the guru's wife for firewood, they endured unseasonable rain together in the forest.

children.text: kṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ nanviyateti sambhramād ramā kilopetya karaṃ rurodha te //
children.translated_text: Then, forcibly taking the flattened rice from the bashful one's fist, when You had eaten one handful,

children.text: bhakteṣu bhaktena sa mānitastvayā purīṃ vasannekaniśāṃ mahāsukham /
children.translated_text: 'Enough, enough, this much suffices!' — in haste, <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) came and seized Your hand.
Honored by You, most devoted among devotees, spending one night in Your city in supreme happiness,

children.text: yadi hyayāciṣyamadāsyadacyuto vadāmi bhāryāṃ kimiti vrajannasau /
children.translated_text: alas, the next day he departed without any wealth — wondrous indeed is Your grace!
'If I had asked, the Unfailing One would have given' — thus thinking, saying to himself 'What shall I tell my wife?', as he walked,

children.text: kiṃ mārgavibhraṃśa iti bhraman kṣaṇaṃ gṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ sa dadarśa vallabhām /
children.translated_text: absorbed in meditation on Your speech, playful smiles, he gradually began to see a row of gem-lamps.

children.text: sakhīparītāṃ maṇihemabhūṣitāṃ bubodha ca tvatkaruṇāṃ mahādbhutām //
children.translated_text: 'Have I lost my way?' — wondering and wandering a moment, entering his home, he beheld his wife,

children.text: sa ratnaśālāsu vasannapi svayaṃ samunnamadbhaktibharo'mṛtaṃ yayau /
children.translated_text: surrounded by companions, adorned with gems and gold, and understood Your most wondrous compassion.
Living in jeweled halls, yet of his own accord, his burden of devotion ever rising, he attained immortality.
O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, who thus fulfills the wishes of devotees — remove my ailments!

children.text: kāṅkṣantyā māturukatyā sutalabhuvi baliṃ prāpya tenārcitastvam /
children.translated_text: Before, when Your mother, through the words inspired by You, wished to see her six sons
brought back by the preceptor's son from the night's slumber, You reached <s>Bali</s> in <s>Sutala</s> and were worshipped by him.
Those six, cursed by <s>Brahmā</s>, born as sons of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> and then as sons of <s>Vasudeva</s>, slain by <s>Kaṃsa</s> —

children.text: śrutadeva iti śrutaṃ dvijendraṃ bahulāśvaṃ nṛpatiṃ ca bhaktipūrṇam /
children.translated_text: You brought them back, showed them, and then led those former sons of <s>Marīci</s> to Your own abode.

children.text: yugapat tvamanugrahītukāmo mithilāṃ prāpitha tāpasaiḥ sametaḥ //
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> chief named <s>Śrutadeva</s>, and also the king <s>Bahulāśva</s>, both full of devotion —
wishing to grace both simultaneously, You arrived at <s>Mithilā</s>, accompanied by sages.
Going in two forms, simultaneously to both their homes,
honored by one with lavish hospitality,
and by the other with the day's gathered fruits, rice, and the like —
You were equally pleased and granted both liberation.

children.text: ko vā daivaṃ nirundhyāditi kila kathayan viśvavoḍhāpyasoḍhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Again, in <s>Dvārakā</s>, when a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s sons kept dying, and even to his lamentations, You —

children.text: jiṣṇorgarvaṃ vinetuṃ tvayi manujadhiyā kuṇṭhitāṃ cāsya buddhiṃ
children.translated_text: 'Who can obstruct fate?' — thus speaking, endured it, though You are the bearer of the universe.
This was, I think, to humble <s>Arjuna</s>'s pride, and when his understanding was blunted by thinking of You as merely human,

children.text: naṣṭā aṣṭāsya putrāḥ punarapi tava tūpekṣayā kaṣṭavādaḥ
children.translated_text: to ground it in truth through the vision of Your supreme, transcendent abode.

children.text: spaṣṭo jāto janānāmatha tadavasare dvārakāmāra pārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Eight of his sons were lost, and again by Your seeming indifference, harsh talk
arose clearly among the people; then at that time <s>Pārtha</s> came to <s>Dvārakā</s>.
Staying there hospitably, when the excellent <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s wife was about to deliver her ninth child, hearing his cries,
he made a vow: if the son is not brought back, he would enter fire.

children.text: rundhānaḥ sūtigehaṃ punarapi sahasā dṛṣṭanaṣṭe kumāre /
children.translated_text: That proud one, without asking You, going to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s house, shielding the birth-chamber with webs of arrows and great weapons,
yet when the child was again seen and lost in an instant,

children.text: moghodyogaḥ patiṣyan hutabhuji bhavatā sasmitaṃ vārito'bhūt //
children.translated_text: he visited through his knowledge the realms of <s>Yama</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the cities of the great gods, but all his efforts vain, about to enter the fire, he was stopped by You with a smile.
Going with him toward the western direction in an exceedingly swift chariot,
passing beyond <s>Lokāloka</s> (the boundary mountain) and piercing the mass of darkness with the radiance of Your discus,

children.text: cakrāṃśukliṣṭadṛṣṭiṃ sthitamatha vijayaṃ paśya paśyeti vārāṃ
children.translated_text: with <s>Arjuna</s> standing there, his vision overwhelmed by the discus's light, You said 'Look, look!' and beyond the waters

children.text: pāre tvaṃ prādadaśaḥ kimapi hi tamasāṃ dūradūraṃ padaṃ te //
children.translated_text: You revealed Your abode, something far, far beyond all darkness.
There, upon the serpent-lord's couch, adorned with divine ornaments and weapons,
clad in yellow garments, dark as a fresh rain-cloud, with a glorious body,
the ruler of the three forms, the one goal of the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas),

children.text: tvāmeva tvaṃ parātman! priyasakhasahito nemitha kṣemarūpam //
children.translated_text: You Yourself — O Supreme Self — together with Your dear friend, bowed to Yourself in that form of auspiciousness.
'You two are indeed both Myself, manifested in a more revealed and more hidden way;
I Myself carried off the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s sons to see you;
now quickly take them back' — and having received them, those
were given to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and <s>Pārtha</s>'s (<s>Arjuna</s>'s) glory was humbled.
Thus, delighting the world with various sports, nourishing the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> clan,
pleasing those doe-eyed ones with Your incomparable playful deeds, dividing Yourself into many for the sacrifices —
You who descended under the pretext of removing the Earth's burden, but truly for the liberation of those devoted to Your lotus feet —

children.text: pūrṇaṃ brahmaiva sākṣād yaduṣu manujatārūṣitastvaṃ vyalāsīḥ //
children.translated_text: You, the complete <s>Brahman</s> Itself, sported among the <s>Yādavas</s>, adorned with the appearance of a mortal.
Mostly in <s>Dvārakā</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, absorbed in the nectar of You, frequented Your presence;
from him, on one occasion, Your father, that treasury of merit, received the knowledge of truth.

children.text: bhaktānāmagrayāyī sa ca khalu matimānuddhavastvatta eva
children.translated_text: And <s>Uddhava</s>, the foremost among devotees, that wise one, from You Yourself

children.text: prāpto vijñānasāraṃ sa kila janahitāyādhunāste vadaryām //
children.translated_text: received the essence of wisdom; and now, they say, he dwells at <s>Badarī</s> for the welfare of the world.

children.text: so'yaṃ kṛṣṇāvatāro jayati tava vibho! yatra sauhārdabhīti-
children.translated_text: This <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> incarnation of Yours triumphs, O Lord, in which through incomparable varieties of <s>yoga</s> —
friendship, fear, love, hatred, passion, and the like — effortlessly,
having crossed all affliction, beings from all sides, from all worlds, attained the immortal state.

children.text: sa tvaṃ viśvārtiśāntyai pavanapurapate! bhaktipūrtyai ca bhūyāḥ //
children.translated_text: May You, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, be present for the pacification of the world's suffering and the fulfillment of devotion!

children.text: ramājāne! jāne yadiha tava bhakteṣu vibhavo
children.translated_text: O Lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>)! I know, I know that among Your devotees, prosperity
does not come immediately — this is because for the unstable tenth [category of beings]
You first bestow tranquility, and then grant everything as desired;

children.text: praśānteṣu kṣipraṃ na khalu bhavadīye cyutikathā //
children.translated_text: for the tranquil ones, there is assuredly no talk of falling from Your path.
Some, O Lord, worshipping <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, and others, who grant boons quickly,
according to their own qualities —
fall alas, pitifully, for lack of far-sightedness;
the story of <s>Vṛkāsura</s> is a clear example of this.
That son of <s>Śakuni</s> once asked the sage <s>Nārada</s>, quick to be pleased, who among the gods was easiest to propitiate;

children.text: sa ca dideśa girīśamupāsituṃ na tu bhavantamabandhumasādhuṣu //
children.translated_text: and he instructed him to worship <s>Giriśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), not You — for You do not befriend the wicked.

children.text: tapastaptv ghoraṃ sa khalu kupitaḥ saptamadine
children.translated_text: Having performed terrible austerities, on the seventh day, enraged,
he cut off his own head and, placing it before <s>Śiva</s>,
asked from the Lord of the World the most petty and terrible boon — death by placing his hand on anyone's head;

children.text: jagannāthād vavre bhavati vimukhānāṃ kva śubhadhūḥ //
children.translated_text: where is auspiciousness for those who turn away from You?

children.text: moktāraṃ bandhamukto hariṇapatiriva prādravat so'tha rudraṃ
children.translated_text: Released from bondage, he ran after <s>Rudra</s>, his liberator, like a lion after a deer; in fear of the <s>daitya</s>,

children.text: daityād bhītyā sma devo diśi diśi valate pṛṣṭhato dattadṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: the god fled in every direction, looking behind him.
When the entire world was silent, seeing <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) about to ascend to Your abode,
You stood far ahead in the form of a clever young <s>brahmacārin</s>, before the <s>Dānava</s>.

children.text: bhadraṃ te śākuneya! bhramasi kimadhunā tvaṃ piśācasya vācā
children.translated_text: 'Blessings to you, O son of <s>Śakuni</s>! Why do you wander now? At the word of a ghost (<s>Piśāca</s>)?

children.text: sandehaścenmaduktau tava kimu na karoṣyaṅgulīmaṅga! maulau /
children.translated_text: If you doubt my word, why not place your finger on your own head, dear one?'
Thus deluded by Your words, placing his hand on his own head, he fell, shattered —

children.text: bhraṃśo hyevaṃ paropāsiturapi ca gatiḥ śūlino'pi tvameva //
children.translated_text: for thus is the downfall of those who worship others; yet even for the Trident-Bearer (<s>Śiva</s>), You alone are the refuge.
The sages dwelling near the <s>Sarasvatī</s> river once sent <s>Bhṛgu</s>
to determine which of the three <s>Mūrtis</s> (forms) had the highest <s>sattva</s> (goodness).
He, through disrespect: when <s>Brahmā</s>'s anger arose and was checked,

children.text: hare'pi ca jihiṃsiṣau girijayā dhṛte tvāmagāt //
children.translated_text: when <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) too wished to strike, held back by <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) — he came to You.
You, the Lotus-Eyed One, sleeping on <s>Ramā</s>'s (<s>Lakṣmī</s>'s) lap,
when the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> kicked You with his foot, You arose with joy.

children.text: sarvaṃ kṣamasva munivarya! bhavet sadā me
children.translated_text: 'Forgive everything, O best of sages! May the mark of your foot
always be an ornament on me here' — thus You spoke.

children.text: niścitya te ca sudṛḍhaṃ tvayi baddhabhāvāḥ
children.translated_text: Having ascertained this firmly, the sages of <s>Sārasvatī</s>, with minds fixed on You,
the best among sages, attained liberation.
We too worship You alone, O <s>Acyuta</s> (the Unfailing), free from the fault of falling,
whose sole body is the pure aggregate of <s>sattva</s>.
At the beginning of the world's creation, praised by the assemblages of <s>Vedas</s> as by bards,
O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose form is being-consciousness and the supreme nectar of non-duality,
O Supreme Self, O Boundless One! — to relieve the weariness and suffering of the cowherd devotees' great misfortune,
O Dweller of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, I worship You!
In the stories of <s>Vṛkāsura</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Mohinī</s>, <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, and others,
Your supremacy — triumphant over all, including <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) —
is established, O Supreme Self! That which shines as something beyond all parts, beyond speech —
that indescribable something is indeed Your true form.
What they call the five <s>Sadāśivas</s> (the five forms of <s>Śiva</s>) as lords of the three forms (<s>Mūrtis</s>) —
among them, the supreme <s>Sadāśiva</s> is declared to be the body of the Supreme Self.
And the <s>Īśvara</s> therein, the one in the <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> state — that is You Yourself;
and again You assume threefold form in the three-part <s>Satya</s> realm.
Among them, they call Your <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) form <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
<s>Brahmā</s> (<s>Dhātā</s>) is devoid of <s>sattva</s>, filled with <s>rajas</s> alone.
And even though there is an abundance of <s>sattva</s>, the activities of <s>tamas</s>-modification
and the like are present in Your form named <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
And that <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) who transcends even the <s>Trimūrti</s> —
even in <s>Śarva</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) form, because of Your all-pervading nature,
they speak of Him in the methods of worship; yet in essence
that is Your form — very firmly established, with many proofs on our side.
The glorious <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) himself, indeed, among all [beings],

children.text: tvāmeva mānayati yo na hi pakṣapātī /
children.translated_text: honors You alone — he who is indeed without partiality.
He expounded the <s>Sahasranāma</s> (Thousand Names) and other [hymns] as devoted to You,
and being himself devoted to Your praise, at the end attained Your state.
At the beginning of the <s>Mantra-Śāstra</s>, he declared You,
with beautiful rays of subtle time-units (<s>kalā</s>), as the Lord of all,
and prescribed formless (<s>niṣkala</s>) meditation in the <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) —
spoke of You alone therein as everything, and none other.

children.text: samastasāre ca purāṇasaṃgrahe visaṃśayaṃ tvanmahimaiva varṇyate /
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Purāṇa</s>-collection, which is the essence of all, Your glory alone is assuredly celebrated;

children.text: trimūrtiyuksatyapadatribhāgataḥ paraṃ padaṃ te kathitaṃ na śūlinaḥ //
children.translated_text: from the true share of three parts ascribed to the three <s>mūrtis</s> (forms), the supreme abode has been declared as Yours, not <s>Śūlin</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s).
The uncovered form, O Lord, spoken of in the second
<s>skandha</s> (book) of the <s>Bhāgavata</s> as [revealed] in the <s>Brahma-kalpa</s> to the Creator —
the name of that very [form], beginning with <s>Hari</s> and <s>Śarva</s>, was declared
as Śrī <s>Mādhava</s> in the <s>Purāṇasāra</s>, even by one devoted to <s>Śiva</s>.
Those who worship <s>Giriśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) in accordance with their own nature
obtain their fruit through the strengthening of their devotion to him;
<s>Vyāsa</s> indeed composed, for the sake of [such] qualified persons,
statements disparaging You in the <s>Skānda</s> and other [<s>Purāṇas</s>] as <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory eulogy).
Actual fact, restatement, and contradictory statement —
these three are the modes of <s>arthavāda</s>, intended for persuasion;
in the <s>Skānda</s> and others, many are the contradictory statements —
such as the disparagement of Your <s>tāmasatva</s> (association with <s>tamas</s>), and instructions [based thereon].
Whatever has been said even by me, an ignorant one, O Lord,
all of it is based on the authority of <s>mantras</s>, <s>śāstras</s>, and sacred texts;
O You who are celebrated in the <s>Bhāgavata</s> which is the essence of <s>Vyāsa</s>'s teachings!
Dispelling afflictions, bestow an abundance of devotion, O Supreme Self!
O <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>! The worship of Your feet I consider the most fearless [refuge] for a mortal being

children.text: martyasyārtasya manye vyapasarati bhayaṃ yena sarvātmaiva /
children.translated_text: who is afflicted and bound by the vision of false objects — by which fear departs, [since] one becomes the Self of all.
For even one who, following the methods of worship prescribed by You, though running on the path of delusion
with covered eyes, does not stumble anywhere, O God of gods, O Universal Self!

children.text: bhūman! kāyena vācā muhurapi manasā tvadbalapreritātmā
children.translated_text: O All-pervading One! Whatever I do — with body, speech, or mind, again and again, my self impelled by Your power —

children.text: yadyat kurve samastaṃ tadiha paratare tvayyasāvarpayāmi /
children.translated_text: all of that I offer here to You, the Supreme.
Even a <s>caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) by birth, if his mind, actions, words, senses, possessions,

children.text: prāṇo viśvaṃ punīte na tu vimukhamanāstvatpadād vipravaryaḥ //
children.translated_text: and vital breath are fixed upon You, purifies the world; but not the foremost <s>brāhmaṇa</s> whose mind is turned away from Your feet.

children.text: bhītirnāma dvitīyād bhavati nanu manaḥkalpitaṃ ca dvitīyaṃ
children.translated_text: Fear arises from a second [entity] — and that second is but a fabrication of the mind;
therefore, by the practice of [realizing] unity, let me restrain my heart here, to the best of my ability, through the intellect.

children.text: māyāviddhe tu tasmin punarapi na tathā bhāti māyādhināthaṃ
children.translated_text: But when that [mind] is struck by <s>māyā</s>, it does not shine thus again — O Master of <s>Māyā</s>!

children.text: tat tvāṃ bhaktyā mahatyā satatamanubhajannīśa! bhītiṃ vijahyām //
children.translated_text: Therefore, by constant and great devotion, O Lord, worshipping You continually, may I abandon fear!
The arising and growth of devotion to those devoted to Your feet [is obtained]

children.text: māsādye puṇyabhājāṃ śriya iva jagati śrīmatāṃ saṅgamena /
children.translated_text: through the company of meritorious persons, just as prosperity [comes] in the world through the company of the prosperous.

children.text: tatsaṅgo deva! bhūyānmama khalu satataṃ tanmukhādunmiṣaddhis-
children.translated_text: May I have such company always, O Lord! The wisdom that dawns from their presence,
through [hearing] the various accounts of Your greatness, makes devotion firm and destroys sins.
Among the paths of the good, holding devotion in the highest esteem, singing again

children.text: gāyan kṣemāṇi nāmānyapi tadubhayataḥ pradrutaṃ pradrutātmā /
children.translated_text: Your auspicious birth-deeds and names — from both [singing and hearing], with mind swiftly melted,

children.text: udyaddhāsaḥ kadācit kuhācidapi rudan kvāpi garjan pragāya-
children.translated_text: now laughing, now weeping, now roaring and singing aloud,
dancing as if mad — O show me compassion, that I may wander beyond worldly convention!
All these beings, all that is composed of the elements, birds, fish, beasts, and others,
mortals, friends, and even enemies — with disciplined mind, bowing to them as pervaded by You,

children.text: tvatsevāyāṃ hi sidhyenmama tava kṛpayā bhaktidārḍhyaṃ virāgas-
children.translated_text: may I succeed in Your service! By Your grace, may firmness of devotion, detachment,
and the realization of Your truth also [come to me], O Lord of the world, without any separate effort!
