Not bewildered by hunger, thirst, and the like — [afflictions] arising from the course of existence — because my mind rests in You,
always constant in contemplation, not wavering from Your feet even for the blink of an eye,
free from elation and sorrow regarding the desired and the undesired, through the understanding that [all] is illusory —
may I walk about with a self cooled exceedingly by the moonbeams of Your nail-crescents!
If I do not yet have the qualification for the meditation of realizing unity with You in all beings,

children.text: tvatprema tvatkamaitrī jaḍamatiṣu kṛpā dviṭsu bhūyādupekṣā /
children.translated_text: then let there be love for Your devotees, friendship toward [the indifferent], compassion toward the dull-witted, and indifference toward enemies;
or, may my eagerness for worship at Your image grow with ever-greater faith —
for even so, one who worships You swiftly attains the highest rank among devotees.
Concealing Your true nature, projecting through earth, water, wind, and the rest,
casting living beings — helplessly driven by the momentum of accumulated <s>karma</s> — into the net of suffering,
may Your <s>māyā</s> not overpower me! O Lord of the world! For its pacification,
devotion to Your feet alone [suffices] — thus declared the awakened, perfected <s>yogin</s>, O Lord!
Having observed the sufferings among beings, with discrimination well-arisen, from the best of teachers
having obtained the truth of Your nature, having attained the height of devotion through the narration of Your qualities and deeds,
having crossed over this <s>māyā</s>, may I rejoice at Your feet, which are the abode of supreme bliss —
this is but the prelude to that [attainment] — O Lord of <s>Pavanapura</s> (Guruvāyūr), destroy all my diseases!
Understanding that all rituals prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s> have been described as being for the sake of a fruit [beyond themselves],

children.text: tāni tvayyarpitānyeva hi samanucaran yāni naiṣkarmyamīśa! /
children.translated_text: performing those [rituals] as offered to You — that is <s>naiṣkarmya</s> (actionless action), O Lord!

children.text: mā bhūd vedairniṣiddhe kuhacidapi manaḥkarmavācāḥ pravṛttir-
children.translated_text: May there be no engagement of mind, deed, or speech in what is prohibited by the <s>Vedas</s>, anywhere;

children.text: durvarjaṃ cedavāptaṃ tadapi khalu bhavatyarpaye citprakāśe //
children.translated_text: but if something unavoidable is encountered, even that I offer to You, O Light of Consciousness!
As for the other path of <s>karma-yoga</s> infused with worship of You — therein, meditating upon Your beloved form,

children.text: hṛdyāṃ sattvaikarūpāṃ dṛṣadi hṛdi mṛdi kvāpi vā bhāvayitvā /
children.translated_text: charming and purely of <s>sattva</s> nature, in a stone, in the heart, in clay, or wherever,
with flowers, incense, food-offerings, and the like, prepared with devotional purity according to one's ability,

children.text: nityaṃ varyāṃ saparyāṃ vidadhadayi vibho! tvatprasādaṃ bhajeyam //
children.translated_text: performing the supreme daily worship — O Lord, may I attain Your grace!
Women and <s>śūdras</s>, deprived of hearing Your stories — let them be objects of Your compassion;
but alas, I grieve for those born in <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families who have come near Your feet yet remain unpeaceful —
performing sacrifices to You only for livelihood, though much has been told, not listening to [the truth about] You,

children.text: dṛptā vidyābhijātyaiḥ kimu na vidadhate tādṛśaḥ mā kṛthā mām //
children.translated_text: puffed up with learning and birth — do they not do [all manner of wrong]? Make me not such as these!

children.text: papo'yaṃ kṛṣṇa! rāmetyabhilapati nijaṃ gūhituṃ diścāritraṃ
children.translated_text: 'This sinner keeps saying "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! <s>Rāma</s>!" to conceal his own wicked conduct;
by the words of this shameless one, my many discourses have been disrupted!' —

children.text: bhrātā me vandhyaśīlo bhajati kila sadā viṣṇumitthaṃ budhāṃste
children.translated_text: 'My brother, of barren character, always worships <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — thus the learned ones

children.text: nindantyuccairhasanti tvayi nihitaratīṃstādṛśaṃ mā kṛthā mām //
children.translated_text: censure and laugh aloud at those who are devoted to You — make me not such as them!

children.text: śvetacchāyaṃ kṛte tvāṃ munivaravapuṣaṃ prīṇayante tapobhi-
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kṛta</s> age, they please You — white in hue, in the form of the foremost sage — through austerities;
in <s>Tretā</s>, they worship You — red-bodied, marked with the sacrificial ladle and cup, in the form of <s>Yajña</s> — through sacrifices;
in <s>Dvāpara</s>, they serve You — dark-limbed, with resplendent <s>ari</s> [weapon] and mace — through <s>tantra</s>-paths;
in the <s>Kali</s> age, humans worship You — of blue hue — through <s>saṅkīrtana</s> (congregational chanting) and the like.

children.text: so'yaṃ kāleyakālo jayati muraripo! yatra saṅkīrtanādyair-
children.translated_text: This age of <s>Kali</s> is indeed victorious, O Slayer of <s>Mura</s>! — for herein, through <s>saṅkīrtana</s> and such
effortless paths alone, O Bestower of all, they swiftly attain Your grace;

children.text: jātāstretākṛtādāvapi hi kila kalau sambhavaṃ kāmayante
children.translated_text: even those born in <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Kṛta</s>, and other [ages] desire birth in <s>Kali</s> —

children.text: daivāt tatraiva jātān viṣayaviṣarasairmā vibho! vañcayāstmān //
children.translated_text: yet those born therein by fortune — O Lord, do not let them be deceived by the poison-taste of sense-objects!

children.text: bhaktāstāvat kalau spurdramilabhuvi tato bhūriśastatra coccaiḥ
children.translated_text: Devotees in <s>Kali</s> are numerous in the southern <s>Dramiḍa</s> land, and exceedingly so

children.text: kāverīṃ tāmraparṇīman kila kṛtamālāṃ ca puṇyāṃ pratīcīm /
children.translated_text: along the <s>Kāverī</s>, <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>, <s>Kṛtamālā</s>, and the sacred western [rivers].

children.text: hā māmapyetadantarbhavamapi ca vibho! kiñcidañcidrasaṃ tva-
children.translated_text: Alas, even me — born within this [blessed region] — do not, O great Lord,

children.text: yyāśāpāśairnibadhya bhramaya na magavan! pūraya tvanniṣevām //
children.translated_text: lead astray by tethering me with the ropes of [worldly] hope, but fulfill my devotion to You!

children.text: dṛṣṭvā dharmadruhaṃ taṃ kalimapakaruṇaṃ prāṅ mahīkṣit parīkṣi-
children.translated_text: Seeing that <s>Kali</s>, the destroyer of <s>dharma</s>, was merciless, the former king <s>Parīkṣit</s>,

children.text: ddhantuṃ vyākṛṣṭakhaḍgo'pi na vinihatavān sāravedī muṇāṃśāt /
children.translated_text: though he drew his sword to slay [him], did not kill him — being a knower of essences, on account of [<s>Kali</s>'s] partial merit.

children.text: tvatsevādyāśu sidhyedasadiha na tathā tvatpare caiṣa bhīrur-
children.translated_text: Devotion to You and such [practices] may indeed succeed swiftly [in <s>Kali</s>]; evil does not so much; and <s>Kali</s> is fearful of Your devotees —

children.text: yattu prāgeva rogādibhirapaharate tatra hā śikṣayainam //
children.translated_text: but when he first robs [devotees] through diseases and the like — alas! — discipline him in that regard!

children.text: gaṅgā gītā ca gāyatryapi ca tulasikā gopikācandanaṃ tat
children.translated_text: The <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the <s>Gītā</s>, the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Tulasī</s>, <s>Gopīcandana</s> (sacred clay),
worship of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone, O Supreme Person, and <s>Ekādaśī</s> (the eleventh-day fast), and the syllables of Your name —
these eight, effortless in the <s>Kali</s> age, by the increase of Your grace
swiftly grant liberation — so declared the sages. Engage me in these!

children.text: devarṣīṇāṃ pit ṇāmapi na punarṛṇī kiṅgaro vā sa bhūman!
children.translated_text: He who, with his entire being, takes refuge in You, abandoning all duties,

children.text: yo'sau sarvātmanā tvāṃ śaraṇamupagataḥ sarvakṛtyāni hitvā /
children.translated_text: is no longer a debtor or servant to the divine sages, the ancestors, or anyone, O All-pervading One!
Even the <s>vikarma</s> (transgressions) that arise [for such a one], You — dwelling in his heart — remove entirely;

children.text: tanme papotthatāpān pavanapurapate! rundi bhaktiṃ praṇīyāḥ //
children.translated_text: therefore, remove the torments born of my sins, O Lord of <s>Pavanapura</s>! And bestow devotion!

children.text: bandhusnehaṃ vijahyāṃ tava hi karuṇayā tvayyupāveśitātmā
children.translated_text: May I, by Your compassion, abandon attachment to kin, with my self absorbed in You,

children.text: sarvaṃ tvaktvā careyaṃ sakalamapi jagad vīkṣya māyāvilāsam /
children.translated_text: and wander having renounced everything, seeing the entire world as a play of <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: nānātvād bhṛāntijanyāt sati khalu guṇadoṣāvabodhe vidhirvā
children.translated_text: Since multiplicity is born of error — when there is awareness of virtues and faults,

children.text: vyāsedho vā kathaṃ tau tvayi nihitamatervītavaiṣamyabuddheḥ //
children.translated_text: how can injunction or prohibition apply to one whose mind is fixed in You, whose sense of disparity is gone?
Countless are the creatures whose intellect is set merely on [satisfying] hunger and thirst;
among them, a human being is superior because of [the capacity for] knowledge, and human birth is indeed rare;

children.text: tatrāpyātmātmanaḥ syāt suhṛdapi ca ripuryastvayi nyastacetā-
children.translated_text: therein too, the self can be its own friend or its own enemy — one whose mind is placed in You

children.text: stāpocchitterupāthaṃ smarati sa hi suhṛt svātmavairī tato'nyaḥ //
children.translated_text: remembers the remedy for the cutting of affliction — such a one is a friend; the self-enemy is the other.

children.text: tvatkāruṇye pravṛtte ka iva na hi gururlokavṛtte'pi bhūman!
children.translated_text: When Your compassion operates, who indeed is not a teacher? Even in worldly life, O All-pervading One!

children.text: sarvākrāntāpi bhūmirna hi calati tataḥ satkṣamāṃ śikṣayeyam /
children.translated_text: Even the earth, though trodden upon by all, does not waver — from her let me learn noble forbearance;
from the wind, O Lord, let me learn non-attachment even amid contact with various sense-objects,

children.text: vyāptatvaṃ cātmano me gaganaguruvaśād bhātu nirlepatā ca //
children.translated_text: and from the sky-teacher, may my all-pervasiveness of self shine forth, along with untaintedness!

children.text: svacchaḥ syāṃ pāvano'haṃ madhura udakavad vahnivanmā sma gṛhṇāṃ
children.translated_text: May I be pure and purifying like water, may I not take on [the faults of others] like fire;

children.text: sarvānnīno'pi doṣaṃ taruṣu tamiva māṃ sarvabhūteṣvaveyām /
children.translated_text: though consuming all food, [let me be] free of blemish; in all beings let me see myself, as in trees [the sap is one].

children.text: puṣṭirnaṣṭiḥ kalānāṃṃ śaśina iva tanornātmano'stīti vidyāṃ
children.translated_text: May I know that waxing and waning belong to the phases of the moon, not to the self;
and that the self's unity [persists] across bodies — like the sun [reflected] in different waters — by Your grace!
May I not, out of affection, become like the pigeon that died with attachment to mate and offspring;

children.text: prāptaṃ prāśnan saheya kṣudhamapi śayuvat sindhuvat syāmagādhaḥ /
children.translated_text: let me accept what comes and endure hunger too, like a python; let me be unfathomable like the ocean.

children.text: mā paptaṃ yoṣidādau śikhini śalabhavad bhṛṅgavat sārabhāgī
children.translated_text: May I not fall [prey] to women and the like, as the moth [falls] into fire; like the bee, may I take only the essence;
but unlike the bee, let me not, O Lord, perish from the compulsion of hoarding wealth!

children.text: mā badhyāsaṃ taruṇyā gaja iva vaśayā nārjayeyaṃ dhanaughaṃ
children.translated_text: Let me not be bound by a young woman, like an elephant by a decoy cow; let me not amass heaps of wealth

children.text: hartānyastaṃ hi mādhvīhara iva mṛgavanmā guhaṃ grāmyagītaiḥ /
children.translated_text: to be stolen by another, like the honey-gatherer [steals] from bees; like a deer, may I not be trapped by vulgar songs.

children.text: nātyāsajjeya bhojye jhaṣa iva baḍiśe piṅgalāvannirāśaḥ
children.translated_text: Let me not be overly attached to food, like a fish to the hook; like <s>Piṅgalā</s> (the courtesan), may I become

children.text: supyāṃ bhartavyayogāt kurara iva vibho! sāmiṣo'nyairna hanyai //
children.translated_text: content through desirelessness; from the <s>kurara</s> (osprey), O Lord, [let me learn that] one with morsel is harmed by others.
May I live having abandoned self-importance, happily like a small child; may I wander without companions,

children.text: kanyāyā ekaśeṣo valaya iva vibho! varjitānyonyaghoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: like the single remaining bangle on a maiden's wrist, O Lord, avoiding the noise of mutual [contact].
With mind absorbed in You, may I not notice, like the arrow-maker, the passing of the king's procession;
may I dwell in houses built by others, like a serpent in a mouse's burrow.

children.text: tvayyeva tvatkṛtaṃ tvaṃ kṣapayasi jagadityūrṇanābhāt pratīyāṃ
children.translated_text: That You create, sustain, and destroy the world through Your own [power] — may I learn from the spider;

children.text: tvaccintā tvatsvarūpaṃ kuruta iti dṛḍhaṃ śikṣeye peśakārāt /
children.translated_text: that contemplation of You transforms one into Your own nature — may I learn firmly from the <s>peśakāra</s> (wasp).

children.text: viḍbhasmātmā ca dehi bhavati guruvaro yo vivekaṃ viraktiṃ
children.translated_text: And this body, composed of excrement and ash, becomes the supreme teacher when it imparts

children.text: dhatte sañcintyamāno mama tu bahurujāpīḍito'yaṃ viśeṣāt //
children.translated_text: discrimination and detachment upon reflection — and mine especially, being afflicted with many diseases.

children.text: hī hī me dehamohaṃ tyaja pavanapurādhīśa! yatpremahetor-
children.translated_text: Alas, alas! Abandon this delusion of the body, O Lord of <s>Pavanapura</s>! — for out of love for it,

children.text: gehe citte kalatrādiṣu ca vivāśitāstvatpadaṃ vismaranti /
children.translated_text: those enslaved to home, mind, wife, and the rest forget Your feet.

children.text: so'yaṃ vahneḥ śuno vā paramiha parataḥ sāmprataḥ cākṣikarṇa-
children.translated_text: This [body] belongs to fire or to dogs hereafter, and at present the eyes, ears,

children.text: tvagjihvādyā vikarṣantyavaśamata itaḥ ko'pi na tvatpadābje //
children.translated_text: skin, tongue, and the rest drag [the self] helplessly — hence no one [attends to] Your lotus feet.

children.text: durvāro dehamoho yadi punaradhunā tarhi niśśeṣarogān
children.translated_text: If the delusion of the body is indeed hard to overcome now, then at least remove all my diseases,

children.text: hṛtvā bhaktiṃ dradhiṣṭhāṃ kuru tava padapaṅkeruhe paṅkajākṣa! /
children.translated_text: and bestow the firmest devotion to the lotus of Your feet, O Lotus-eyed One!
Surely after many, many births, this liberation-granting <s>brāhmaṇa</s> body has been obtained —

children.text: kṣudre hā hanta mā mā kṣipa viṣayarase pāhi māṃ māruteśa! //
children.translated_text: alas, alas! Do not cast it into the paltry taste of sense-objects — protect me, O Lord of the <s>Maruts</s> (Guruvāyūr)!
The diversity, corpulence, thinness, and the like are superimposed on You through contact with the body born of the <s>guṇas</s>,
just as greatness, smallness, brightness, and dullness [are superimposed on fire] according to the kinds of wood.
By the lower churning-stick in the form of the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), kindling the upper churning-stick in the form of the disciple —
by the fire of awakening made fully manifest through the agitation [of the <s>guṇas</s>],
when the vast wilderness of illusion — the world-body created by the latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) of the chain of <s>karma</s> — is being consumed,

children.text: dāhyābhāvane vidyāśikhini ca virate tvanmayī khalvavasthā //
children.translated_text: and when the fire of knowledge, [finding] nothing left to burn, ceases — the state that remains is indeed one with You. //
Thus there is no other means of destroying all afflictions than attaining You.
Neither absolute nor ultimate are agriculture, the six [Vedic] virtues, and the six [ordained] occupations.
Even those on the Vedic paths, though imperfect through grievous defects, having attained their fruits,

children.text: mattāstvāṃ vismarantaḥ prasajati patane yāntyanantān viṣādān //
children.translated_text: yet intoxicated, forgetting You — when downfall occurs, they go to endless sorrows. //

children.text: tvallokādanyalokaḥ kva nu bhayarahito yat parārdhadvayānte
children.translated_text: Where is any world free from fear other than Yours? For even at the end of two <s>parārdhas</s> (half-lifetimes of <s>Brahmā</s>),

children.text: tvadbhītaḥ sapyaloke'pi na sukhavasatiḥ padmabhūḥ padmanābhaḥ! /
children.translated_text: even <s>Padmabhū</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) in his own world does not have a peaceful abode, fearing You, O <s>Padmanābha</s>!
This being so, what need to speak of the hellish ones, immersed in great darkness acquired through unrighteousness?

children.text: tanme tvaṃ chindhi bandhaṃ varada! kṛpaṇabandho! kṛpāpūrasindho! //
children.translated_text: Therefore, O Boon-granter, O Friend of the wretched, O Ocean of compassion — sever my bondage! //

children.text: yāthārthyāt tvanmasyaiva hi mama na vibho! vastuto bandhamokṣau
children.translated_text: In truth, O Lord, since I am Yours alone, bondage and liberation do not really exist for me.

children.text: māyāvidyātanubhyāṃ tava tu viracitau svapnabodhopamau tau /
children.translated_text: But they are fashioned by Your <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) and <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), like dream and waking.

children.text: baddhe jīvadvimuktiṃ gatavati ca bhidā tāvatī tāvedeko
children.translated_text: Even between the bound and the liberated-while-living, the difference is only this much:
one, dwelling in the tree of the body, tastes the fruits of sense-objects; the other, the painless Self, does not. //
'Liberation-while-living is of this nature' — what use of such words when [the reality is] far, far away?

children.text: tannāmāśuddhabuddherna ca laghu manasaḥ śodhanaṃ bhaktito'nyat /
children.translated_text: For that is not [attainable] by an impure mind, and there is no quick purification of the mind other than devotion.
Therefore, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, draw forth in me a weight of devotion in which everything is surrendered to You,
whereby, through some word of a <s>guru</s>, I may swiftly attain awakening to You and become one with You. //
Even those who exert their minds in the <s>Śabdabrahman</s> (Vedic word-<s>Brahman</s>) do not know You here.

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ vandhyaśramāste cirataramiha gāṃ bibhrate niṣprasūtim /
children.translated_text: Alas, futile is their effort — they long bear a barren cow!
Whose divine incarnations and pastimes are delightful to all and destroy all impurity,

children.text: saccitsāndraṃ ca rūpaṃ tava na nigaditaṃ tāṃ na vācaṃ bhriyāsam //
children.translated_text: and whose form is dense with existence and consciousness — may I not bear that [barren] speech that does not declare these! //

children.text: yo yāvān yādṛśo vā tvamiti kimapi naivāvagacchāmi bhūma-
children.translated_text: Who You are, how great, or of what nature — I do not comprehend at all, O Infinite One!
Yet being of single-minded devotion, I hold dear only the devoted worship of You, O Enemy of <s>Caidya</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>)!
The seeing, touching, and the like of Your emblems and the assemblies of those dear to Your feet —
may I have reverence for worship, prostration, praise, and recounting of Your qualities and deeds! //

children.text: yadyallabhyeta tattat tava samupahṛtaṃ deva! dāso'smi te'haṃ
children.translated_text: Whatever is obtained — let all that be offered to You, O Lord! I am Your servant.

children.text: tvadgehonmārjanādyaṃ bhavatu mama muhuḥ karma nirmāyameva /
children.translated_text: Let the sweeping of Your temple and other such service be my constant work, performed without self-interest.
In the sun, fire, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the Self, and other [forms], I would worship You, the four-armed One shining forth.
May my <s>bhaktiyoga</s> (yoga of devotion), whose nature is melting with love for You, flow ceaselessly! //
Oneness with You, difficult to attain through charity, vows, observances, restraints, austerity, <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, and <s>Yoga</s> —
the <s>Gopīs</s>, the most meritorious, attained it, dense with bliss, through association with You alone.
Among other devotees too, though they be great, You esteem most the devotion of these [<s>Gopīs</s>].

children.text: tanme tvadbhaktimeva draḍhaya hara gadān kṛṣṇa! vātālayeśa! //
children.translated_text: Therefore, strengthen devotion to You in me, remove [my] diseases, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! //
In the beginning, You assumed the golden-cosmic (<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>) body, the undivided Self of the individual soul.
Having become the individual soul, imbued with the qualities of <s>Māyā</s>, You persist, O Source of the universe!

children.text: tatrodvṛddhena sattvena tu gaṇayugalaṃ bhaktibhāvaṃ gatena-
children.translated_text: Therein, through <s>Sattva</s> (goodness) grown predominant, when the pair of [other] quality-groups has entered the state of devotion,

children.text: cchitvā sattvaṃ ca hitvā punaranupahito vartitāhe tvameva //
children.translated_text: cutting even <s>Sattva</s> and leaving it behind, You again exist unaffected — that indeed is You! //

children.text: sattvonmeṣāt kadācit khalu viṣayarase doṣabodhe'pi bhūman!
children.translated_text: Through the rise of <s>Sattva</s>, sometimes indeed, even when the defect in sense-pleasures is known, O Infinite One,

children.text: bhūyo'pyeṣu pravṛttiḥ satamasi rajasi proddhate durnivārā /
children.translated_text: renewed engagement in them is irresistible when <s>Tamas</s> and <s>Rajas</s> surge — hard to prevent.

children.text: cittaṃ tāvad guṇāśca grathitamiha mithastāni sarvāṇi roddhuṃ
children.translated_text: Mind and qualities are intertwined here — to restrain all of them,

children.text: turye tvayyekabhaktiḥ śaraṇamiti bhavān haṃsārūpī nyagādīt //
children.translated_text: singular devotion to You, the <s>Turīya</s> (Fourth), is the refuge — thus You, in the form of <s>Haṃsa</s> (the Swan), declared. //

children.text: santi śreyāṃsi bhūyāṃsyapi rucibhidayā karmiṇāṃ nirmitāni
children.translated_text: There exist many paths of welfare, created with varied tastes for ritual practitioners;

children.text: kṣudrānandāśca sāntā bahuvidhagatayaḥ kṛṣṇa! tebhyo bhaveyuḥ /
children.translated_text: their small joys end, and many different destinies arise from them, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!

children.text: tvaṃ cācakhyātha sakhye nanu mahitatamāṃ śreyasāṃ bhaktimekāṃ
children.translated_text: But You have declared to Your friend (<s>Uddhava</s>) that devotion alone is the greatest of all paths of welfare.

children.text: tvadbhaktyānandatulyaḥ khalu viṣayajuṣāṃ sammadaḥ kena vā syāt //
children.translated_text: Indeed, what joy of sense-enjoyers could equal the bliss of devotion to You? //

children.text: tvadbhaktyā tuṣṭabuddheḥ sukhamiha carato vicyutāśasya cāśāḥ
children.translated_text: For one of satisfied mind through devotion to You, happily moving about here, free from desires — all desires
become filled with happiness, like [the earth] for one who has found water, becoming entirely [permeated] by water.
Such a one indeed desires not the world of <s>Indra</s>, the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, nor the delightful <s>Yoga</s>-powers,
let alone these — he is indifferent even to the bliss of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) that comes of its own accord. //
Your devotee, though tormented by sense-pleasures on account of the restlessness of the senses,
cannot be conquered by them — now weakened, being overpowered by devotion.
Just as a blazing fire with seven tongues burns even a vast mass of timber,

children.text: tvadbhaktyoghe tathaiva pradahati duritaṃ durmadaḥ kvendriyāṇām //
children.translated_text: so the flood of devotion to You burns away sin — where then the arrogance of the senses? //

children.text: cittārdrībhāvavamuccairvapuṣi ca pulakaṃ harṣabāṣyaṃ ca hitvā
children.translated_text: The melting of the heart, horripilation of the body, and tears of joy — without these,

children.text: cittaṃ śudhyet kathaṃ vā kimu bahutapasā vidyayā vītabhakteḥ /
children.translated_text: how indeed can the mind be purified? What [can be achieved] by much austerity or learning for one devoid of devotion?
This Self, constantly polished with the collyrium perfected through the relish of songs about You,

children.text: cakṣurvat tattvasūkṣmaṃ bhajati na tu tathābhyastayā tarkakoṭyā //
children.translated_text: perceives the subtle essence of reality, like the [purified] eye — but not so through even well-practiced dialectical reasoning. //
I would practice meditation upon You: seated in a comfortable posture with body erect, gaze fixed on the tip of the nose,
having controlled the path of breath through <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation) and other [techniques], [I would contemplate] the downward-facing lotus of the heart,
making it face upward, visualizing the Sun, Moon, and Fire above it —
therein I would meditate upon You, dark as a rain-cloud laden with water, of tender limbs. //
With dark, smooth hair, brilliant with fine <s>makara</s>-shaped earrings, with a face
moistened by the flowing of a gentle smile, beautiful with the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem, the forest-garland, and <s>Śrī</s> (radiance),
marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, with beautiful arms, soft and fair belly, garment of golden hue,
with charming smooth thighs and lotus-like delicate feet — thus would I meditate upon You. //
O Lord! Holding the mind with playful curiosity upon all the limbs again and again,
I would then fix it upon one spot — the beautiful lotus-face with its gentle smile.
The mind absorbed therein, I would expand it into the form of non-dual supreme bliss and consciousness,
thinking of nothing else whatsoever — thus I would become one established in <s>Yoga</s>. //
When such meditation-yoga upon You is attained, the eight <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers) beginning with <s>aṇimā</s>,
and even clairaudience and others, would eagerly rush toward me, O Slayer of <s>Mura</s>!
But as they would delay the attainment of You, I would not regard all this. I desire
You alone, full of bliss! O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, protect me from all suffering! //
You are indeed <s>Brahman</s> directly, O Supreme One of vast glory! Among syllables, You are the letter 'A';

children.text: stāro mantreṣu rājñāṃ manurasi muniṣu tvaṃ bhṛgurnārado'pi /
children.translated_text: among <s>mantras</s>, the <s>Tāra</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>); among kings, You are <s>Manu</s>; among sages, You are <s>Bhṛgu</s> and also <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: prahlādo dānavānāṃ paśuṣu ca surabhiḥ pakṣiṇāṃ vainateyo
children.translated_text: <s>Prahlāda</s> among demons; among cattle, <s>Surabhī</s> (the wish-fulfilling cow); among birds, <s>Vainateya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>);
among serpents, You are <s>Ananta</s>; and among rivers, the celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), O Universal Form! //

children.text: brahmaṇyānāṃ balistvaṃ kratuṣu ca japayajño'so vīreṣu pārtho
children.translated_text: Among the pious, You are <s>Bali</s>; among sacrifices, the <s>japayajña</s> (sacrifice of silent repetition); among heroes, <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>);

children.text: bhaktānāmuddhavastvaṃ balamasi balināṃ dhāma tejasvināṃ tvam /
children.translated_text: among devotees, You are <s>Uddhava</s>; among the powerful, You are strength; among the radiant, You are splendor.
There is no end to Your glories — every surpassingly splendid thing is You alone.

children.text: tvaṃ jīvastvaṃ pradhānaṃ yadiha bhavadṛte tanna kiñcit prapañce //
children.translated_text: You are the individual soul, You are the <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter); nothing in this world exists without You. //
The <s>dharma</s> of the <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) and <s>āśramas</s> (life-stages), ordained in the Vedic path, performed with devotion directed toward You —
those who do so, when inner detachment blossoms, gradually relinquishing [actions], attain
the pure realization of You as 'I am the supreme Self' — undivided across all objects though they appear divided —
the rootless root of the universe, manifesting as existence, consciousness, and dearness in all things. //

children.text: jñānaṃ karmāpi bhaktistritayamiha bhavatprāpakaṃ tatra tāvad
children.translated_text: Knowledge, action, and devotion — this triad leads to You. Therein,
for those who are completely disgusted with all worldly things, the qualification is for the yoga of knowledge.

children.text: saktānāṃ karmayogastvayi hi vinihito ye tu nātyantasaktā
children.translated_text: For those attached [to the world], <s>karmayoga</s> (yoga of action) dedicated to You [is prescribed]; but those who are neither excessively attached

children.text: nāpyatyantaṃ viraktāstvayi ca dhṛtarasā bhaktiyogo hyamīṣām //
children.translated_text: nor excessively detached, yet holding love for You — <s>bhaktiyoga</s> (yoga of devotion) is for them. //

children.text: jñānaṃ tvadbhaktatāṃ vā laghu sukṛtavaśānmartyaloke labhante
children.translated_text: Knowledge or devotion to You — beings in the mortal world obtain easily through merit.

children.text: tasmāt tatraiva janma spṛhayati bhagavan! nākago nārako vā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O Lord, even a heaven-dweller or a hell-dweller desires birth there [in the mortal world].

children.text: āviṣṭaṃ māṃ tu daivād bhavajalanidhipotāyite martyadehe
children.translated_text: As for me, placed by fate in this mortal body that serves as a boat on the ocean of existence —
making You the helmsman, with the <s>guru</s> as the favorable wind, do carry me across! //
Those greedy for mere knowledge, seeking the Unmanifest through scriptures and reasonings,
struggle exceedingly and attain success only at the end of many births.

children.text: durasthaḥ karmayogo'pi ca paramaphale nanvayaṃ bhaktiyoga-
children.translated_text: <s>Karmayoga</s> too is distant from the supreme fruit. But this <s>bhaktiyoga</s>
is delightful from the very root and swiftly leads to You — may it grow in me! //
The sage (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) declares that even for knowledge, supreme effort [is needed]; but one who, hearing the truth of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: gāḍhaṃ tvatpādabhaktiṃ śaraṇamayati yastasya muktiḥ karāgre /
children.translated_text: takes deep refuge in devotion to Your feet — liberation is in his very hand.
Even in meditation upon You, the difficulty is equal [to other paths] due to the mind's fickleness;
but through practice, it can be quickly mastered — through Your grace and [its] beauty. //

children.text: nirviṇṇaḥ karmamārge khalu viṣamatame tvatkathādau ca gāḍhaṃ
children.translated_text: Disgusted with the path of <s>karma</s>, which is indeed most arduous, and though deeply

children.text: jātaśraddho'pi kāmānayi bhuvanapate! naiva śaknomi hātum /
children.translated_text: faithful in Your stories and the like, O Lord of the world — alas, I am unable to abandon desires!

children.text: tad bhūyo niścayena tvayi nihitamanā doṣabuddhyā bhajaṃstān
children.translated_text: Yet, with renewed resolve, with mind fixed on You, worshipping those [desires] with the understanding that they are faults,

children.text: puṣṇīyāṃ bhaktimeva tvayi hṛdayagate maṅkṣu naṅkṣyanti saṅgāḥ //
children.translated_text: I shall nourish devotion alone — when You enter the heart, attachments shall quickly perish. //
A certain one, whose mind was purified by the loss of wealth earned through much toil, pressed by the crowds of people,

children.text: prāgevaṃ prāhi vipro na khalu mama janaḥ kālakarmagrahā vā /
children.translated_text: formerly spoke thus: 'It is not people, nor time, nor <s>karma</s>, nor the planets that [cause my suffering] —

children.text: ceto me duḥkhahetustadiha guṇagaṇaṃ bhāvayat sarvakārī-
children.translated_text: my own mind is the cause of my sorrow; for it, contemplating the multitude of qualities [of objects], performs everything' —

children.text: tyuktvā śānto gatastvāṃ mama ca kuru vibho! tādṛśīṃ cittaśāntim //
children.translated_text: having said this, he became tranquil and attained You. O Lord, grant me such peace of mind too! //
<s>Aila</s> (<s>Purūravas</s>), formerly with helplessly infatuated mind toward <s>Urvaśī</s>, serving her long,

children.text: gāḍhaṃ nirvidya bhūyo yuvatisukhamidaṃ kṣudrameveti gāyan /
children.translated_text: became deeply disgusted and sang: 'This pleasure of women is petty indeed!'

children.text: tvadbhaktiṃ prāpya pūrṇaḥ sukhataramacarat tadvaduddhūya saṅgaṃ
children.translated_text: Having attained devotion to You, he moved about fulfilled and in greater bliss. Likewise, shaking off attachment,

children.text: bhaktottaṃsaṃ kriyā māṃ pavanapurapate! hanta me rundhirogān //
children.translated_text: make me the crest-jewel of devotees, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>! Alas, remove my diseases! //

children.text: traiguṇyād bhinnarūpaṃ bhavati hi bhuvane hīnamadhyottamaṃ ya-
children.translated_text: Due to the three <s>guṇas</s>, everything in the world appears in differentiated form — inferior, middling, and superior:

children.text: jñānaṃ śraddhā ca kartā vasatirapi sukhaṃ karma cāhārabhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: knowledge, faith, the doer, dwelling, happiness, action, and food — all differ.

children.text: tvatkṣetratvanniṣevādi tu yadiha punastvatparaṃ tattu sarvaṃ
children.translated_text: But whatever here is Your <s>kṣetra</s> (field), Your service, and so forth — all that which is directed toward You
is declared to be established in freedom from the <s>guṇas</s>; through devoted worship of that, may I swiftly become perfected! //
With mind placed in You alone, moving happily about, all actions performed for Your sake,
resorting to sacred places where Your devotees are served and Your deeds are enacted,
with equal regard for thief and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, householder and others, freed from the faults of contempt,
rivalry, envy, and the like — I would worship You constantly in all beings. //

children.text: tvadbhāvo yāvadeṣu sphurati na viśadaṃ tāvadevaṃ hyupāstiṃ
children.translated_text: As long as the sense of Your presence does not shine clearly in these [beings], just so long would I thus worship;
when the awareness of oneness suddenly blossoms, I would move about as one with You.

children.text: tvaddharmasyāsya tāvat kimapi na bhagavan! prastutasya praṇāśa-
children.translated_text: Of this <s>dharma</s> of Yours that has been commenced, there is never, O Lord, any destruction whatsoever.

children.text: stasmāt sarvātmanaiva pradiśa mama vibho! bhaktimārgaṃ manojham //
children.translated_text: Therefore, with my whole being, O Lord, bestow upon me the path of devotion, delightful to the mind! //

children.text: taṃ cainaṃ bhaktiyogaṃ draḍhayitumayi! me sādhyamārogyamāyur-
children.translated_text: And to strengthen this very <s>bhaktiyoga</s> — alas, for me the prerequisite is health and life!

children.text: diṣṭyā tatrāpi sevyaṃ tava caraṇamaho bheṣajāyeva dugdham /
children.translated_text: Fortunately, even for that, Your feet are to be served — like milk, [which is both] medicine [and nourishment].
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, long ago, whose lifespan was declared by astrologers to be twelve years,

children.text: sevitvā vatsaraṃ tvāṃ tava bhaṭanivahairdrāvayāmāsa mṛtyum //
children.translated_text: having worshipped You for one year, put Death to flight through Your attendants! //

children.text: mārkaṇḍeyaścirāyuḥ sa khalu punarapi tvatparaḥ puṣpabhadrā-
children.translated_text: <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, of long life, he indeed, devoted to You, performing austerity

children.text: tīre ninye tapasyannatulasukharatiḥ ṣaṭ tu manvantarāṇi /
children.translated_text: on the bank of the <s>Puṣpabhadrā</s> river, experiencing incomparable bliss, passed six <s>Manvantaras</s> (world-ages).
The seventh <s>Devendra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), wishing to delude him with celestial maidens, winds, and the arrows of Love —

children.text: yogoṣmapluṣyamāṇairna tu punaraśakat tvajjanaṃ nirjayet kaḥ //
children.translated_text: but they, being scorched by the fire of his <s>Yoga</s>, could not prevail. Who can conquer one devoted to You? //
Then You, named <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, companion of <s>Nara</s>, came graciously to his side

children.text: tuṣṭyā toṣṭūyamānaḥ sa tu vividhavarairlobhito nānumene /
draṣṭuṃ māyāṃ tvadīyāṃ kila punaravṛṇod bhaktitṛptāntarātmā
tsaptārṇorāśimagne jagati sa tu jale sambhraman varṣakoṭīḥ /
dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ hṛṣṭaromā tvaritamabhigataḥ spraṣṭukāmo munīndraḥ
evaṃ tvatsevayaiva smararipurapi sa prīyate yena tasmā-
yasminnetad vibhātaṃ yata idamabhavad yena cedaṃ ya etad
yo'smāduttīrṇarūpaḥ khalu sakalamidaṃ bhāsitaṃ yasya bhāsā /
yo vācāṃ dūradūre punarapi manasāṃ yasya devā nunīndrā
no vidyustattvarūpaṃ kimu punarapare kṛṣṇa! tasmai namaste //
janmātho karma nāma sphuṭamiha guṇadoṣādikaṃ vā na yasmin
no tiryañcaṃ na martyaṃ na ca suramasuraṃ na striyaṃ no pumāṃsaṃ
na dravyaṃ karma jātiṃ guṇamapi sadasad vāpi te rūpamāhuḥ /
bhūyaḥ saṃhṛtya sarvaṃ kamaṭha iva padānyātmanā kālaśaktyā
gambhīre jāyamāne tamasi vitimiro bhāsi tasmai namaste //
vedāntairyat tu gītaṃ puruṣaparacidātmābhidhaṃ tat tu tattvaṃ
sattvenāsattayā vā na ca khalu sadasattvena nirvācyarūpā
bhūṣāsu svarṇavad vā jagati ghaṭaśarāvādike mṛttikāvat
vidyālābhe tathaiva sphuṭamapi vikaset kṛṣṇa! tasmai namaste //
yadbhītyodeti sūryo dahati ca dahano vāti vāyustathānye
yenaivāropitāḥ prāṅ nijapadamapi te cyāvitāraśca paścāt
tasmai viśvaṃ niyantre vayamapi bhavate kṛṣṇa! kurmaḥ praṇāmam //
satyaṃ śuddhaṃ vibuddhaṃ jayati tava vapurnityamuktaṃ nirīhaṃ
cakraṃ te kālarūpaṃ vyathayatu na tu māṃ tvatpadaikāvalambaṃ
viṣṇorvīryāṇi ko vā kathayatu dharaṇeḥ kaśca reṇūn mimīte
yo'sau viśvāni dhatte priyamiha paramaṃ dhāma tasyābhiyāyāṃ
bhaktātmā viṣṇave yaḥ prādiśati havirādīni yajñārcanādau /
kṛṣṇādyaṃ janma vā mahadiha mahato varṇayet so'yameva
prītaḥ pūrṇo yaśobhistvaritamabhisaret prāpyamante padaṃ tat //
he stotāraḥ! kavīndrāstamiha khalu yathā cetayadhve tathaiva
he viṣṇo! kīrtanādyaistava khalu mahatastattvabodhaṃ bhajeyam //
viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi sampaśyata manasi sadā yaiḥ sa dharmānabadhnād
yānīndrasyaiṣa bhṛtyaḥ priyasakha iva ca vyātanot kṣemakārī /
deva! śreyāṃsi vidvān pratimuhurapi te nāma śaṃsāmi viṣṇo! /
āpaḥ sṛṣṭyādijanyāḥ prathamamayi vibho! garbhadeśe dadhustvāṃ
yatra tvayyeva jīvā jalaśayana! hare! saṅgatā ekyamāpan /
tasyājasya prabho! te vinihitamabhavat padmamekaṃ hi nābhau
he lokā viṣṇuretad bhavanamajanayat tanna jānītha yūyaṃ
yuṣmākaṃ hyantarasthaṃ kimapi tadaparaṃ vidyate viṣṇurūpam /
mūrdhnāmakṣaṇāṃ padānāṃ vahasi khalu sahasrāṇi sampūrya viśvaṃ
tat protkramyāpi tiṣṭhan parimitavivare bhāsi cittāntare'pi /
bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ ca sarvaṃ parapuruṣa! bhavān kiñca dehendriyādi-
yat tu trailokyarūpaṃ dadhadapi ca tatonirgatānantaśuddha-
jñānātmā vartase tvaṃ tava khalu mahimā so'pi tāvān kimanyat /
bhūyiṣṭhaṃ sāndramodātmakamupari tato bhāti tasmai namaste //
avyaktaṃ te svarūpaṃ duradhigamatamaṃ tat tu śuddhaikasattvaṃ
mūrtiṃ te saṃśraye'haṃ pavanapurapate! pāhi māṃ kṛṣṇa! rogāt //
llolambāṃ lambamānāmurasi tava tathā bhāvaye ratnamālām //
ūrū cārū tavorū ghanamasṛṇarucau cittacorau ramāyā
cchāyāṃ jānudviyaṃ ca kramapṛthulamanojñe ca jaṅghe niṣeve //

children.translated_text: I meditate upon the auspicious array of [Your] fingers, which destroys the darkness of affliction.
Among the limbs of Yours [contemplated by] the greatest <s>yogis</s>, the exceedingly sweet abode of those who attain liberation,
the root of Your feet, O Lord — a wish-fulfilling tree whose tender shoots rain down all desires for devotees —

children.text: nityaṃ cittasthitaṃ me pavanapurapate! kṛṣṇa! kāruṇyasindho!
children.translated_text: may it always remain established in my mind, O Lord of <s>Guruvāyūr</s>, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O Ocean of Compassion!
Having removed all afflictions without remainder, may it bestow the splendor of a flood of supreme bliss!

children.text: ajñātvā te mahattvaṃ yadiha nigaditaṃ viśvanātha! kṣamethāḥ
children.translated_text: If, not knowing Your greatness, anything has been spoken amiss herein, O Lord of the Universe, please forgive it.
May this hymn, exceeding one thousand [verses], conduce to Your grace.

children.text: dvedhā nārāyaṇīyaṃ śrutiṣu ca januṣā stutyatāvarṇanena
children.translated_text: The <s>Nārāyaṇīya</s> is twofold: in the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas) and by birth — through the description of praiseworthy [deeds];
this one, abundant with playful incarnations, may it bring about longevity, health, and happiness here.
